MANCHESTER UNITED fans left Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium early in their numbers as their team fell to a humiliating 4-1 defeat.

It was another far from enjoyable European night for Michael Carrick and United, who were played off the park by Cesc Fabregas‘ team.



Fabregas was asked about a potentially vacant Man Utd management role in the lead up to the clash, a question he dismissed at the time.

But the pressure is piling on Carrick, who hasn’t overseen a win for seven games.



This limp and lifeless performance at Como could well be the death knell for Michael Carrick, a serial winner as a player who now looks permanently beaten on the touchline.

As they did last week against Atletico, United conceded early.

It took Como’s star man Nico Paz just two minutes to open the scoring in the Wednesday early kick-off.

And a quickfire double at the beginning of the second half put the debutant hosts in total command against the three-time European champs.

Even centre-back Jacobo Ramon fancied getting on the scoresheet as Como made it four with 15 to play.

Joshua Zirkzee‘s late consolation did not restore much respect to the struggling Red Devils, who were battered away from home in Europe again.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

United skipper Bruno Fernandes also made more headlines as he fiercely shook his head after being hooked.

However his replacement Zirkzee appeared to offer more in 20 minutes than Fernandes did in over an hour, as he bagged United’s late consolation.

Sports.title: Como 4 Man Utd 1: Michael Carrick fighting for job as woeful United are humiliated by Cesc Fabregas’ side
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED were undone in seconds in Como and it may be a question of days until they change manager.

This limp and lifeless performance at Como could well be the death knell for Michael Carrick, a serial winner as a player who now looks permanently beaten on the touchline.



United are seven games without a win, their longest winless run since December 2015, when Carrick was playing for them.

Louis van Gaal got a five-month long stay of execution but Carrick will do well to get five days. This defeat was worse than any during Van Gaal’s lean run.



An added-time Joshua Zirkzee goal spared United from their heaviest European defeat since 1994.

Carrick looks like he knows what awaits him. After Nico Paz clipped in Como’s third before the hour, Carrick’s head dropped and he trudged back to the dugout out of sight from the majority of photographers.



This spiral is not all on Carrick. United deprived him of key signings in the summer and the absence of a support striker and new left back have been particularly costly of late.

Yet their squad is better than the one that ended last season in third and Carrick’s selection errors are into the dozens after less than a dozen games.

He is making so many changes that they have their own air of resignation.

Crowbarring Bruno Fernandes into the team as a false nine was the latest and an experiment that did not last beyond the first half.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Fernandes started on the right and on the left last week. This week, he replaced Bryan Mbeumo, on the scoresheet in two of his three previous games as a centre forward.

That had a knock-on effect on Youri Tielemans, so creative as the No10 against Atletico Madrid and Leeds, when he chiefly serviced Mbeumo. There was no sign of that with Fernandes.

The United captain was substituted in the 67th minute. Once Fernandes reached the dugout, there was no acknowledgement from Carrick and no need, in truth. The game was lost.

Matthijs de Ligt’s first appearance in 325 days coincided with the heaviest defeat of Carrick’s reign. United conceded after 47 seconds in Madrid last week. This time it was after 118 seconds.

Sometimes a team is beaten before a ball is kicked. It was blustery in Italy but the sight of United defender Noussair Mazraoui in tights set an ominous tone.



How different it might have been had Diogo Dalot been capable of finishing from open play. Dalot miscontrolled Matheus Cunha’s lofted pass in the second minute, the ball still rolled invitingly for him to shoot yet he blazed wide.

From Como’s goal kick, they worked the ball into the final third, Lucas da Cunha played it inside to Nico Paz and Harry Maguire inexplicably stood off him, inviting the shot beyond Senne Lammens’ palms.

Mazraoui slapped his thighs in exasperation while Mason Mount told Maguire what he should have done.

The anger spread to Carrick, who stood motionless for the first 20 minutes until he had a robust exchange of views with Cunha.



United soon ceded possession again and Carrick cursed before retreating into the dugout.

In contrast, the casually-attired Cesc Fabregas was alert and engaged throughout in the technical area. Carrick may be true to his conservative character but you have to wonder what Sir Jim Ratcliffe makes of his studious style.

Andrey Santos scythed down Paz in the 25th minute for the first card of the game. The Brazilian declined to console the Argentine and that was Fernandes’ cue to unload on teammates, demanding answers from a perplexed Mbeumo. Mount offered Cunha some pointers.

United were playing walking football. There was more movement from some of the substitutes Carrick sent out to limber up half-an-hour in.



Three minutes later, mutiny was in the air as United supporters chanted “Attack, attack, attack”.

This was the latest show of dissent on the terraces in a season where the substitution of Kobbie Mainoo was booed at Fulham and that soundtrack accompanied the home draw with Tottenham.

At one stage, the Como fans aired a chant to the tune of “You’re getting sacked in the morning” and you had to wonder whether it was the Italian translation. United ended the first 45 without an attempt on target.

Half-time changes were essential and Carlos Baleba and Amad were back put on the pitch almost as soon as their teammates had disappeared down the tunnel. Cunha and Santos were hooked.

Cue more switches: Fernandes went to the left, Mbeumo moved up front while Mazraoui and Dalot swapped sides. Things only got worse.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Como went easy on United for a few more minutes at the start of the second half than in the first. Tasos Douvikas gave the cumbersome De Ligt the slip and lashed the ball past Lammens in the 51st minute.

Paz hared into the United area with a minimum of fuss to sweep in his second on 57 minutes. Defender Jacobo Ramon nodded in the fourth from Kaiki’s pinpoint cross on 76 minutes and an already sparse United away end emptied a little more.

Sports.title: French cops call for PSG clash to be postponed amid fears of further riots after ring of steel at Champions League tie
Sports.content:
Next

FRENCH cops have called for PSG’s clash with Lyon on Sunday to be postponed amid fears of further riots.

Paris is bracing for another volatile week after apocalyptic unrest swept across the nation over the weekend.



Police have urged the Professional Football League (LFP) to postpone the Ligue 1 match initially scheduled for 8.45pm.

According to L’Equipe, the match could be postponed to the following day.



But the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony is also set for Monday – and PSG players are expected to be in contention for the ultimate individual award.

PSG and Lyon are not alone. France’s league body moved the match between Toulouse and Troyes from its original Saturday slot to Sunday.



It also postponed the second-division clash between Montpellier and Red Star to Monday.

Around 5,000 officers including special forces armed with water cannons were deployed ahead of the Champions League match on Tuesday.



PSG defeated FC Barcelona 4-2 at the Parc des Princes, surrounded by a ring of steel.

Ahead of the game an Interior Ministry source said: “This is a hugely sensitive time, with violence likely to break out at any time, especially when large crowds gather.

“Thousands of extra officers will be on duty for the game, and they will include special forces officers.”

Time curfews were also imposed across several areas of the French capital to prevent further unrest.

The measures were brought in after targeted curfews were hailed for helping keep calm following the worst riots France has seen in years.



At least 3,000 businesses were looted or damaged and more than 2,400 people were arrested.

The Gilet Jaunes – Yellow Vests – movement is meanwhile calling for another round of mass demonstrations on Saturday.

French prime minister Sebastian Lecornu praised emergency measures which ensured a relatively quiet night from Monday to Tuesday in places including Paris and Marseille.



Over the weekend, French president Emmanuel Macron blamed “agitators from far-Left fringe groups, joined by numerous criminals” for plunging his country into “unbridled violence”.

He made an impassioned plea “for unity” following chaos said to have involved up to 500,000 protesters.

Macron said: “Businesses have been looted, while public buildings, shops, and town halls have been attacked.

“Looking at these images, we have all asked ourselves how French people could do this to France.”

He said he was particularly upset at Limoges City Hall being burnt, along with a tourist office in Lyon.



“Nothing justifies it, nothing explains it, nothing excuses it,” he said.

French police have already admitted that they “lost control” of major cities during a weekend of “apocalyptic rioting”.

“It was apocalyptic,” said a high-ranking officer.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It follows almost five weeks of protests by school and university students against France’s crumbling education system.

They have now been joined by numerous other social groups, including the infamous Gilets Jaunes which brought chaos to France at the start of Macron’s time in office.

Sports.title: Fuming Bruno Fernandes shakes head as he is hauled off for Zirkzee in 67th minute of Man Utd’s Como horror show
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED skipper Bruno Fernandes shook his head in frustration as he was HOOKED by Michael Carrick in Como.

The Portuguese, 32, was hauled off in the 67th minute as United trailed 3-0 to the Italian side.



Fernandes trudged off the pitch at the nearest point rather than running over to slap hands with his replacement, Joshua Zirkzee.

Como would soon rub salt into his wounds by grabbing a fourth.



And Zirkzee will not have made Fernandes feel much better by doing what the captain failed to do and getting on the scoresheet as the game finished 4-1.

Fernandes seemed fuming at being subbed as he glanced over towards the bench with a steely look in his eye.

It is unclear whether Carrick was saving Fernandes for Bournemouth’s visit to Old Trafford on Sunday, or was simply unhappy with his performance.

But United travelling to Como with a threadbare squad – young Jack Fletcher made the bench HOURS after scoring in a Youth League game – will ensure that Fernandes’ withdrawal raises more than a few eyebrows.



With Benjamin Sesko out injured, Fernandes was deployed in an unfamiliar centre-forward role.

And he had an exceptionally tough night in Italy.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

His first-half stats sheet read zero for goals, assists, shots, dribbles and tackles won.



While he also lost possession seven times and misplaced five passes.

His struggles continued after the break as a clip did the rounds on social media showing a wayward left-footed shot flying miles over the crossbar.

Fernandes did not seem a happy camper at any point during the contest, at one point angrily pulling up Bryan Mbeumo for not pressing intensely enough.

A second-minute beauty from Nico Paz set the tone on a gloomy night for United.

The brilliant Paz teed up Anastasios Douvikas for Como’s second after the break, before helping himself to another goal just before the hour mark.



Jacobo Ramon then twisted the knife in the 76th minute to put Carrick under serious pressure.

United have now gone seven straight games without a win in all competitions, losing four matches on that run.

Sports.title: Miserable Man Utd ripped apart by Como
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's Manchester United were ripped apart in a dreadful 4-1 defeat at Como in the Champions League, as their miserable run of results stretched to seven without a win.

The pressure continues to pile up on Carrick and this United side as their start to the season lurches from bad to worse - and on Wednesday night they were humbled by a Como team which delivered more intensity and quality in Italy.

The first attribute should be a non-negotiable but, despite United's application being in the spotlight, they were once again outworked by their opposition. Static in midfield, allowing Como players to run off them, losing markers... this was a shocking show of United's big failings out of possession.

The tone was set just two minutes in when Man Utd went behind early on - again. They are the first English side ever to concede in back-to-back Champions League games so soon and never got to grips with Cesc Fabregas' impressively coached team.

Nico Paz brought the class for the hosts. The talented Argentina international stuck the opener into the top corner when Harry Maguire gave him too much space and then slotted in a third after catching Carlos Baleba in possession.

Paz set up another Como goal, too, playing in Tasos Douvikas, who ran away from a disoriented Matthijs de Ligt to find the net inside four minutes of the second half.

Image: Diogo Dalot during Man Utd's Champions League match with Como

This was De Ligt's first start in 325 days due to back problems and came due to a wider spate of injuries at the club. But excuses for this United performance may wear thin quickly for the travelling support who stood in the pouring rain to watch this dismantling.

United's own star, Bruno Fernandes, was anonymous again, with just one goal involvement now in his past nine appearances for the club. His head-shaking summed up the mood before a sweeping Como fourth, which saw unmarked centre-back Jacobo Ramon head in, underline the vast gap between the sides on the night.

Joshua Zirkzee's injury-time goal was of little consolation. With just three points from their first three games, United have an uphill battle to make it out of the league phase in this competition. More immediately they are in desperate need of a better performance and win at home to Bournemouth on Sunday in the Premier League, live on Sky Sports.

Analysis: No shock to see Man Utd beaten

Sky Sports' Paul Merson:

"They've got to start winning matches. The problem with Manchester United is we still live in the age of when it was Rooney, Ronaldo and people like that.

"We're caught by the name - one of the biggest clubs in the world. But they're not one of the biggest teams in the world. They're far from it.

"Everybody judges them on when they had superstars. I don't see it as a shock. I look at their players and I don't go, 'oh this is a surprise'. I didn't expect them to beat Leeds. Absolutely not. I didn't expect them to beat Como. That's where they are.

"Rooney, Ronaldo, Keane... they're a million miles away."

Key moments from Como...

2: BIG MISS! Diogo Dalot takes a Matheus Cunha cross down in the box but his left-foot shot flashes wide of the far post.

2: GOAL! Nico Paz curls Como's opener into the top corner after Harry Maguire gives him too much space. A similar chance to Dalot's - a different result!

17: WIDE! Harry Maguire heads wide from a Bryan Mbeumo cross.

39: BIG MISS! Tasos Douvikas blazes over after stepping into the United box, failing to capitalise on static defending.

41: OFFIDE! A let-off for Senne Lammens and Man Utd as an offside flag goes up against Douvikas after he is brought down in the box by the goalkeeper.

HT: SUBS! Michael Carrick makes two changes at the break with Amad Diallo and Carlos Baleba sent on for Andrey Santos and Matheus Cunha.

Image: Como players celebrate taking an early lead against Man Utd in the Champions League

49: GOAL! Man Utd concede at the start of the second half, too, as Paz plays in Douvikas, who runs off Matthijs de Ligt before firing in.

54: CLOSE! Lucas da Cunha blasts a left-foot shot wide from inside the box when he looked primed to add a third.

57: GOAL! Baleba makes an ill-advised turn in his own half with no cover behind him and Paz takes the ball and races in on goal to add a third.

64: CHANCES! But Amad can't connect with Fernandes' clipped pass into the box to pull one back for United. Moments later he sees a shot tipped over.

76: GOAL! Centre-back Jacobo Ramon heads in to finish off another sweeping Como move.

90+1: GOAL! Joshua Zirkzee is narrowly onside to grab a late goal for Man Utd, finding the net after controlling Amad's cross.

Man Utd's next fixtures...

Sports.title: Brilliant sprinter Almeraq retired to stud
Sports.content:
Champion sprinter-elect Almeraq has been retired to stand at Shadwell's Beech House Stud for 2027.

Winner of three six-furlong Group Ones this season for William Haggas and Tom Marquand, that would be a a remarkable season in any book before even considering what happened to him at the end of the 2025 season.

Running in a Listed race at York in September he clipped heels and took a very heavy fall. Connections feared the worst yet while the horses emerged generally unscathed, neither jockey involved, the now-retired Jim Crowley or Trevor Whelan, have ridden since.

For Almeraq to bounce back this season to not only win races but at the very highest level, shows another side to his character.

The four-year-old by Dark Angel won the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes at Royal Ascot, the Haydock Sprint Cup by over four lengths and on Saturday he took the British Champions Sprint.

Haggas said: "Almeraq has been a fantastic horse and we have always held him in high regard. He is a strong, powerful sprinter with an iron constitution.

"He has done remarkably well to come back from a horrendous fall at York and win three six-furlong Group One races this season, which speaks volumes not only for his ability but also for his mental strength and resilience.

Sports.title: England 'not thinking about points difference' against France
Sports.content:
England suffered Rugby League World Cup opening game loss to Tonga; they now have to get a large win against France and then beat Papua New Guinea handsomely to keep slim hopes of progressing to the semi-finals alive; England play France on Saturday October 24 at 7.35am

England's Brad O'Neill says the side will resist the urge to 'go for broke' against France

England hooker Brad O'Neill says his side will resist the urge to go for broke when they face France in their second Rugby League World Cup match in Perth on Saturday.

An opening 30-12 defeat to Tonga has left their hopes of reaching the semi-finals hanging by a thread, with points difference looking increasingly like the only way to progress.

But head coach Brian McDermott has named an unchanged 19-man matchday squad, a sign that he does not plan radical changes against a France team smarting from their 78-4 humbling by Samoa.

O'Neill, the newly-crowned Super League Man of Steel, said: "We have discussed what is required but I feel like the mentality can't be any different to what we had against Tonga.

You can change your settings at any time via the Privacy Options Unfortunately we have been unable to verify if you have consented to Twitter cookies. To view this content you can use the button below to allow Twitter cookies for this session only. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once

"We can't go into this game thinking about the points difference. We've got to go into this game hard-nosed like we did against Tonga, and hopefully if we do our jobs well enough we're going to get the win."

A complicated cross-group format has left England needing Tonga to beat Samoa in their final group game in a fortnight's time to stand any chance of reaching the last four - provided all the other games go to form.

That would take the final semi-final slot down to points difference between England and Samoa - and McDermott's men are already up against it given Samoa's stunning win over the Super League-laden French side.

Image: England know they will have to score points as Samoa have already beaten France 78-4

"I feel like we play France in Super League most weeks with Catalans and Toulouse, so there will be some familiar faces," O'Neill added.

"We're expecting a great game at the weekend. France are coming off a loss, like us as well, so they are going to come out firing.

"But we're not changing anything about the way we play. It's more about working on the execution side of things that we didn't do so well against Tonga. As you'd expect, Saturday was very disappointing, but there is still a real belief in this team."

What's next?

England must regroup ahead of facing France in Perth next Saturday, kick-off 7.35am (UK and Ireland time). Meanwhile, England women face Australia at 10.05am.

Sports.title: England star Kildunne dropped for Canada rematch
Sports.content:
Ellie Kildunne has been dropped to the bench in the England Red Roses squad to face Canada on Friday, a week on from suffering defeat in Toronto which ended a 41-match unbeaten run.

Head coach John Mitchell has made four changes to the starting XV in total, with Gloucester-Hartpury duo Emma Sing and Mia Venner coming into the back three at full-back and wing respectively, while Helena Rowland of Loughborough Lightning returns at inside-centre.

In the forwards, there is just one amendment to the team that began the second Test - Sadia Kabeya, also of Loughborough Lightning, is selected at openside flanker.

While Kildunne - 2024's World Player of the Year - and back-row Alex Matthews move to the replacements bench, wing Claudia Moloney-MacDonald and centre Tatyana Heard drop out of the squad altogether.

"Friday is our first chance to respond," Mitchell said.

"Last Friday, we lost sight of what we could control when it mattered most; that's on us to fix. This week is about getting back to who we are: hungry, accountable to each other and demanding more of ourselves than anyone outside this group ever could.

"We've earned a strong period, but nothing about it is owed to us going forward. Friday is an opportunity to apply sustained pressure, learn from what we missed and come out the other side better than we went in."

Image: Kildunne has been dropped to the bench as England's Red Roses seek to respond to defeat in Canada against the same opposition

Mitchell: Kildunne going through difficult period

Speaking more about the major selection call at his pre-match press conference, Mitchell shed further light on the decision.

The head coach revealed Kildunne is "going through a difficult period" in the search for consistency:

"Well, firstly it's undisputed that she adds huge value. She's just going through a difficult period at the moment.

"It's important for us to help her through that.

Image: John Mitchell revealed the reasons for dropping Kildunne, saying she is going through a 'difficult period' in terms of consistency

"She wants to become consistent as well and she'll get back. It's also important to create competition and to recognise that you have to become more consistent, especially when you're competing in the Red Roses.

"So it's really important to reinforce the behaviours that we think are necessary to our game. And that goes for everyone."

Sports.title: White: Fisher will reach "another level" for his next fight
Sports.content:
Johnny Fisher will reach “another level” for his next fight, says Zuffa Boxing founder Dana White.

Fisher had his first bout with new promoter Zuffa Boxing in September, coming through a draining 10-round battle with Michael Pirotton.

"He looked good until he started gassing out in the last couple of rounds. But he fought through it, won the fight and I'm excited to see him fight again. He's fun, the crowd is fun, his family are good, fun people and I love having him a part of Zuffa Boxing," White told Sky Sports.

Fisher is a hugely popular figure on social media, known for his love of Chinese takeout. He may though need to improve on his conditioning for his next fight. White has invited him to make use of the UFC's Performance Institute.

"I have seen something where he said he overtrained for the fight, which is a possibility. I don't know, only he knows. But he should absolutely positively come out to Las Vegas and spend some time at the PI [performance institute]," White said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Zuffa Boxing 11 fight between Johnny Fisher and Michael Pirotton.

"All the fighters should. It's incredible. It's an unbelievable amenity you get being a part of our company. He should do that."

White is certainly expecting an improved Fisher in his next fight.

"He didn't look terrible. He gassed out there. But I tell you what I really liked about it, when you see a guy gas like he did and you push yourself through, you don't quit and you make it through that, it just takes you to another level for your next fight," the promoter said.

"Mentally now he knows what he did. Did he overtrain, did he not train enough? He knows and now he knows what he needs to fix coming into his next fight so it'll be exciting to see what tweaks he makes in his training for his next fight."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dillian Whyte has welcomed a heavyweight showdown with Johnny Fisher and believes it will be 'exciting while it lasts'.

Who's next?

Fisher will have appealing options for his next fight. Dillian Whyte was ringside for his last bout at the Copper Box and former world champion Charles Martin is open to boxing Fisher.

Martin's manager Mike Borao told Sky Sports: "He's had an amazing career and became IBF heavyweight champion. He wants one more big opportunity."

Image: Former IBF world champion Charles Martin is open to fighting Fisher in the UK.

Martin, who lost to Anthony Joshua at the O2 in 2016, is looking to fight in Britain again next year. Borao said: "Possible opponents Johnny Fisher, Dillian Whyte or perhaps another UK fighter. We will have to see what happens but Charles is going to make one more big push."

Sports.title: Bayern Munich v Arsenal: Champions League – live
Sports.content:
40s ago 15.21 EDT 20 min: Odegaard swings in from the right. Neuer comes for the ball and flaps. The ball drops to Calafiori, six yards out, level with the far stick. Calafiori should score, but leans back and hoicks over. What a miss! Share

5m ago 15.17 EDT 15 min: Kim pings a speculative pass down the left for Davies, who nearly manages to nip past Timber at high speed, only for the defender to give him a gentle tap on the back, one that causes him to take an extra step that sends both ball and player over the byline. Goal kick. Saucy defending. Share

8m ago 15.14 EDT 13 min: Havertz goes into the book for a late slide into Stanišić. Things suddenly not going Arsenal’s way. Share

9m ago 15.13 EDT 12 min: “Word precludes me from tuning in on Paramount+ in the States,” begins Jeff Necessary, Gunner in North Carolina, “so keeping the MBM open for occasional checks. Given the way Arsenal first halves have gone lately, I may not miss much for a while.” Well, Jeff, you’ve got that damn straight at the moment. Share

11m ago 15.10 EDT 10 min: Saka is able to get up, but he’s limping heavily and not happy. He blows out in frustration as he hobbles off. Eze comes on in his place. Share

13m ago 15.09 EDT 8 min: Saka spins Davies down the right, but the Canadian international comes back at his man to ensure the Arsenal winger doesn’t enter the box. Saka nips infield instead, then takes a clumsy prod at the ball before grabbing his thigh and crumpling to the floor in pain. This doesn’t look great. View image in fullscreen Arsenal's Bukayo Saka receives medical attention after sustaining an injury. Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/Reuters Share Updated at 15.16 EDT

15m ago 15.07 EDT 6 min: Saka and Havertz combine down the inside-right channel, the latter entering the Bayern box. Havertz scuffs a cross; Saka can’t force the ball home from the middle of a melee on the edge of the six-yard box. Bayern clear, but Arsenal will be very happy with these early attacks. Share

17m ago 15.05 EDT 4 min: Raya passes long. Timber cushions a header in from the right for Saka, who shuttles the ball further across towards Madueke. For a second, it looks like Bayern have been opened up with a couple of simple passes, but Madueke clanks into Laimer and the danger is gone. Share

19m ago 15.02 EDT 2 min: Pinball + hot potato = shapeless first 120 seconds. Share

21m ago 15.00 EDT Vincent Kompany and Mikel Arteta worked with each other at Manchester City. When the former emerges from the tunnel, the pair embrace warmly and have a quick catch-up. And then Arsenal get the game started. Share

23m ago 14.58 EDT The teams are out! Bayern are in one of their all-red phases, while Arsenal are harking back to the early 90s with a blue version of the famous bruised banana. Vincent Kompany is in the house, by the way, having recovered from a virus that threatened to keep him in bed. And so is Germany boss Jurgen Klopp, in the stands flashing that smile and throwing his arm around the shoulder of another erstwhile Liverpool manager, Rafael Benitez. Everyone having a good time, it seems, and looking forward to this big showdown, including Arsenal fan Charles Antaki … well, kind of: “Pretty dismal, the fare served up in the game against Forest. But! Pundits have assured us that because Bayern are going to be on the attack, Arsenal will be free to entertain us with a dazzling display of skill, ambition, irresistible cheeks and above all, goals. Not much to say about that except We Shall See.” We’ll be off in a minute or two. Share

35m ago 14.47 EDT Mikel Arteta speaks to TNT Sports. “We’re gonna have to play, I expect, three or four different games at different stages … we need everybody ready because we need to change and adapt to that … freshness … very excited … we have talked about our enthusiasm for playing on these big stages … that’s where you want to get tested … play with a lot of courage … a lot of aggression … be decisive … we have prepared for what we have to do.” Share

1h ago 13.57 EDT Bayern are without Joshua Kimmich following a death in his immediate family. Harry Kane leads the line, while former Liverpool winger Luis Diaz is on the bench. Michael Olise is suspended following his two-yellows-in-two-minutes fiasco during the 3-3 draw at Viking. Share Updated at 13.58 EDT

1h ago 13.53 EDT Arsenal make two changes to their starting XI following the staunch 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest. Noni Madueke and Jurriën Timber replace Eberechi Eze and Ben White, who drop to the bench. Share Updated at 13.57 EDT

Sports.title: Como 4-1 Manchester United: Champions League – live reaction
Sports.content:
7m ago 15.14 EDT Here are some snippets from Michael Carrick’s post-match interview: double quotation mark It was more than disappointing. I think everybody’s got to take responsibility for that. I’ll take responsibility for the overall team and performance, it stops with me and I’m fine with that. But as a supporter of this football club, to see a performance like that is unacceptable, I have to say. I’ll look at what we’ve done. It’s the motivation and the purpose and the intensity of a game of football that you have to bring. We didn’t bring that today. You can’t choose when you want to perform or you don’t, when you give absolutely everything and when perhaps you don’t. I care an unbelievable amount about the supporters. They’re the heartbeat of this football club and always will be. I’ve got to apologise for the performance. Everything they’ve done to get here tonight, for them to watch that performance tonight, I feel for them. Tonight’s not about me. It’s about digesting the game, and how it went. That’s the most important thing right now. Share

10m ago 15.11 EDT I assume this is a wave of apology rather than farewell. View image in fullscreen Manchester United manager Michael Carrick apologises to the away fans at full time at Como. Photograph: Kieran McManus/Shutterstock Share

20m ago 15.00 EDT Thankfully we can rely on Jamie Jackson, who is lakeside for us tonight. And here is his match report! In sight of the Alps, a boat ride from George Clooney’s villa, Manchester United will hope, in what has been a terrible start to the season, that things do not get any worse. They can’t – for the team’s prospects, and Michael Carrick’s job security, because witnessed here by Lake Como was a humiliation of the three-times European champions by Cesc Fàbregas’s competition debutants, as United suffered their worst defeat in continental football since 1994. By 57 minutes this was over, as Como were 3-0 ahead, and Nico Paz had destroyed Carrick’s men with a scintillating display featuring two goals and the assist for Tasos Douvikas’s strike. Much more here: Carrick under more pressure as Manchester United humbled against Como Read more Share

25m ago 14.56 EDT It may take Manchester United fans some time to get over this performance/result, but TNT Sports have moved on pretty quickly. As I suppose they had to, given that loads more games start in five minutes, but doesn’t help me bring you the hottest reaction from a windswept, drenched Como. Share

34m ago 14.46 EDT The good news for Michael Carrick is that Dimitar Berbatov, on TNT Sports, doesn’t say that United now have to beat Bournemouth on Sunday for him to stay in his job. The bad news for Carrick is that Berbatov’s reasoning is that Carrick might not still be in his job on Sunday. “I don’t think everyone was giving their best,” Berbatov says of this performance. “It didn’t look like that on the pitch. Como were having fun.” View image in fullscreen Manchester United's manager Michael Carrick leaves the pitch after his side’s heavy defeat to Como. Photograph: Antonio Calanni/AP View image in fullscreen Meanwhile his opposite number Cesc Fabregas is savouring a famous victory for Como. Photograph: Claudia Greco/Reuters Share Updated at 14.51 EDT

38m ago 14.43 EDT Manchester United’s next few games: Sunday 25 October: Bournemouth (h)

Saturday 31 October: Chelsea (a)

Tuesday 3 November: Roma (h)

Sunday 8 November: Aston Villa (h)

Sunday 22 November: Liverpool (a) Share

40m ago 14.40 EDT United’s players wander over to apologise to whatever flimsy remnant of the travelling support isn’t already drowning their sorrows in a nearby hostelry. View image in fullscreen Manchester United's Mason Mount (second left), Noussair Mazraoui (left) and Diogo Dalot (second right) look dejected as they applaud their fans. Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/Reuters Share Updated at 14.48 EDT

42m ago 14.39 EDT Final score: Como 4-1 Manchester United 90+4 mins: Say what you like about this United performance, they completely dominated that period of stoppage time, and won it 1-0! Share Updated at 14.39 EDT

45m ago 14.36 EDT GOAL! Como 4-1 Manchester United (Zirkzee, 90+1 mins) United do have their consolation! Amad chips the pass into the box, Zirkzee escapes from his marker and brings it down beautifully, leaving himself with a pretty easy finish which he calmly completes. View image in fullscreen Joshua Zirkzee bags a consolation goal. Photograph: Antonio Calanni/AP Share Updated at 14.45 EDT

46m ago 14.34 EDT 90+1 mins: There’ll be three minutes of stoppage time, or thereabouts. Share

47m ago 14.33 EDT 89 mins: … Not like that they can’t. Lacey takes the corner, and three defenders line up at the near post to boot it clear, which one of them emphatically does. Share

48m ago 14.32 EDT 89 mins: Amad wins United a corner. Could they end the night with a consolation? Share

50m ago 14.31 EDT 87 mins: Lacey swiftly earns himself a booking. “The Guardian called for jeopardy in this competition. I think Man Utd have found it for you,” writes Ian Copestake. Their remaining Champions League fixtures: Roma (h), Sporting (a), Leipzig (h), Bayern Munich (h), Villarreal (a). Share

51m ago 14.29 EDT 86 mins: Another United substitution, Lacey replacing Mbeumo. Share

52m ago 14.28 EDT 84 mins: Kempf is booked, I think less for bringing down Amad than for being grumpy with the referee for giving the free-kick. Share

1h ago 14.24 EDT 80 mins: Como bring on Smolcic, Ricci and Dossena, and take off Couto, Paz and Perrone. Share

1h ago 14.24 EDT 79 mins: Amass comes on for De Ligt, whose return from injury is the silver lining to tonight’s miserable, charcoal-grey cloud for United. Share

1h ago 14.22 EDT 78 mins: Como are hunting for a fifth, but Paz shoots too close to Lammens. Share

1h ago 14.22 EDT GOAL! Como 4-0 Ohno (Ramon, 76 mins) That is delicious. Ramon, the centre-back, spots Maguire creeping out of position and reckons he can get into that empty space before anyone notices. And turns out he was right. Kaiki Bruno sees him sprinting into an empty penalty area and sends in a perfect, precise cross, and Ramon hammers his header home from six yards! View image in fullscreen Jacobo Ramon heads home to give Como a fourth goal. Photograph: Mattia Ozbot/Uefa/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Ramon celebrates. Photograph: Claudia Greco/Reuters View image in fullscreen Noussair Mazraoui (left) and Amad Diallo (right) look dejected after the visitors go even further behind. Photograph: Piero Cruciatti/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at 14.44 EDT

1h ago 14.18 EDT 73 mins: Zirkzee has brought a bit of extra pace and energy to the United team, if not any improvement in control. “Well, although it is quite funny (as a Liverpool fan) to watch a club swing from one manager to another chasing a dominance they once had (ahem), how much of the current malaise can be blamed on trying to keep up with the noisy neighbours across the city?” wonders Andy Flintoff (not that one). “Feeling that they have to do that has probably accelerated that swing and made the lurches more extreme.” I suppose it can’t have helped, though it seemed to have more of a positive effect on some other teams (if not their bank balances). Share

1h ago 14.14 EDT 69 mins: Kaiki Bruno and his exemplary caterpillar moustache comes on for Da Cunha. Share Updated at 14.14 EDT

1h ago 14.13 EDT 67 mins: Bruno Fernandes is taken off, which feels a bit like an admission of defeat. Zirkzee replaces him. Share

1h ago 14.10 EDT 66 mins: Amad shoots from 22 yards or so. The ball flies over Butez’s head and was probably also going over the bar but the keeper made sure. Share

1h ago 14.09 EDT 64 mins: Como bring Caqueret on for Baturina. United have been playing for the last five minutes or so with Mazraoui on the right and Dalot on the left. Share

1h ago 14.07 EDT 62 mins: Amad has been bright since he came on at half-time. He’s at the heart of a United attack but it ends with a blind cross, and a clearance. “Watching United at the moment, they look like a side completely in limbo, unable to move on,” writes Paul Flint. “The players surely know that Carrick is going sooner rather than later, and must be wondering about their futures. It doesn’t encourage in-game focus, however much they may be paid.” Share

1h ago 14.05 EDT 60 mins: Tielemans has a shot from the edge of the area, but it’s more of an apology than a challenge and Butez picks it up. Share

1h ago 14.03 EDT 59 mins: Paz tries another curler, this one from the edge of the D, but this one floats too close to Lammens. Share

1h ago 14.02 EDT GOAL! Como 3-0 Manchester United (Paz, 57 mins) Baleba hits a pass into Nico Paz’s shins just inside the United half and the ball runs beautifully into the Argentinian’s path, so he heads off, runs into the area, draws the keeper, and slides the ball across goal and in at the far post! View image in fullscreen Another smart finish from Nico Paz gives him his second goal of the night, and Como’s third. Photograph: Claudia Greco/Reuters View image in fullscreen Joy for Paz and the Como fans … Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/Reuters View image in fullscreen Despair for Bruno Fernandes and his Manchester United teammates … Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/Reuters View image in fullscreen And their manager Michael Carrick. Photograph: Kieran McManus/Shutterstock Share Updated at 14.15 EDT

1h ago 14.01 EDT 56 mins: An actually good United move ends with Mount flicking the ball towards Bruno Fernandes, but it’s intercepted. Share

1h ago 13.59 EDT 55 mins: Como should have had a third! Paz passes to Da Cunha, who shifts onto his left foot to open up a great shooting chance, 12 yards out, but then cuts across the ball rather than curling it with his instep, and it skews the wrong side of the post! Share

1h ago 13.58 EDT 54 mins: “I know watching United’s downfall has been fun for rival fans, I totally get that and don’t blame them for relishing it,” writes Lee Woolsey. “And I know this gets said a lot by fans about their team when they’re playing badly, but I’m sorry: this United team just look like they don’t care. They were a goal down after two minutes and the remaining 43 were an exercise in collective shoulder shrugging by a team of mercenaries assembled by a parasitic reign of witches. People DIED for this club. These players are a risible disgrace.” It’s very easy to blame the players, though. They aren’t well coached. They haven’t been well recruited. It’s the whole edifice. Share

1h ago 13.56 EDT 52 mins: “Not having a screen to watch this on, and just going on your mbm, I don’t think that Mount hasn’t been mentioned, is he doing as little as suggested?” wonders Martin Lancon. In brief, yes. United’s midfield hasn’t done very much. There were a couple of moments in the first half when Mount exchanged passes with Bruno Fernandes and the pair briefly looked pretty classy, but they haven’t achieved anything creatively. And as I type that Mount has a rubbish shot from 30 yards. Share

1h ago 13.55 EDT 50 mins: That’s just so easy. Paz carries the ball forwards, Douvikas runs into a massive space between De Ligt, who just didn’t see the run coming, and Maguire – the Dutchman stumbles at a crucial moment, but he was already out of the race – and finishes superbly! View image in fullscreen Tasos Douvikas (number 9) doubles Como’s lead with a smart finish. Photograph: Marco Luzzani/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Douvikas (third left) celebrates with his Como teammates. Photograph: Mattia Ozbot/Uefa/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Then heads back to his own half beside dejectected Manchester United players. Photograph: Marco Luzzani/Getty Images Share Updated at 14.06 EDT

1h ago 13.53 EDT GOAL! Como 2-0 Manchester United (Douvikas, 49 mins) A brighter restart for United, but in just over three minutes they’re two down! Share

2h ago 13.50 EDT 46 mins: Peeeeep! The game has restarted, and United have made a double halftimely substitution, Matheus Cunha and Andrey Santos going off, Diallo and Baleba coming on. Share

2h ago 13.43 EDT Just one goal, and that from a wonderful shot from outside the area, does not really reflect what has not been a tightly-contested game. Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo asked for punishment ‘without mitigation’, then fought to cut it
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo successfully fought to reduce his punishment for walking out on a Portugal training camp, after saying publicly that his sanction should be imposed “without mitigating circumstances”.

After leaving the training camp in Denmark last month, Ronaldo said in a lengthy statement on social media that he should be punished as the Portuguese Football Federation saw fit and that his role as captain constituted “an aggravating factor”.

However, during the disciplinary council’s inquiry the 41-year-old put forward several arguments for cutting his punishment, including his clean disciplinary record in recent seasons and his services to football.

Ronaldo received a 30-day suspension and a €255 (£215) fine, and the document accompanying the ruling reveals he presented three arguments in mitigation: his disciplinary record this season and in the previous three seasons; his services to football including recognition for sporting merit; and his contribution to establishing the facts of the case.

To support these arguments, Ronaldo listed the club titles he has won and his achievements with the national team: the 2016 European Championship and two Nations League titles. His individual awards were also highlighted, including the fact that the Al-Nassr forward has won the Ballon d’Or five times. Beyond his achievements on the pitch, he mentioned the honours he had received from senior state officials.

The decision-makers accepted Ronaldo’s arguments concerning his achievements and services to the country, using them to halve his suspension and fine. The punishment was then halved again because Ronaldo had accepted responsibility for his actions.

Ronaldo’s suspension will be served in a period during which there are no international matches. It is unclear whether he intends to return to the national team – or whether the head coach, Jorge Jesus, will select him again.

The account of events provides a clearer picture of the circumstances surrounding Ronaldo’s departure from the training camp. After head coach Jesus held a press conference in which he reiterated that he was in charge of the team and that no player would influence his selection decisions, Ronaldo requested a vehicle from the FPF and set off for Copenhagen airport.

During the journey, he called the Portuguese federation’s president, Pedro Proença, and told him he was “not in the right frame of mind” to remain with the team.

“The defendant [Ronaldo] did not inform or provide prior justification to the federation or the men’s national team officials regarding his intention to leave the stadium and the training camp,” the ruling states. It says that between 30 September and 4 October, Ronaldo missed more than 30 team activities, including travel, training sessions and meals.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The federation says that Ronaldo’s promise on social media, after leaving the training camp, to tell his fans “the whole truth” brought further negative attention to the incident: “Given his prominence as a public figure on a global scale, the defendant could not have been unaware that his conduct, in the circumstances in which it occurred, would be subject to intense media scrutiny, as indeed it was.”

Ronaldo was therefore “expected to exercise particular caution in choosing the timing and manner in which he expressed his dissatisfaction with the manager’s decisions and conduct”. Instead, the player “further fuelled speculation and public curiosity by posting on Instagram on the very day he left Copenhagen, announcing that, ‘in due course’, he would tell ‘all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to his departure from the men’s senior national team’,” the inquiry concluded.

Portugal are scheduled to play Denmark again in their next game on 14 November in Braga.

Sports.title: ‘A complete threat’: Rio Ngumoha’s electric display excites Van Dijk and Liverpool
Sports.content:
The shot sailed wide of Peter Gulacsi’s top corner and into the Kop, affording Villarreal much-needed respite at 4-2, but for Andoni Iraola it was a standout moment in a scintillating Champions League display from Rio Ngumoha. To a coach who called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield.

There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side won 4-3, Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with his left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game.

“I’m happy with his attitude because he’s eager to improve the things that we think he needs to improve,” the Liverpool head coach said after the comeback win against their Spanish opponents. “He has played a lot on the right lately. He’s feeling so comfortable now that he’s even adding some shots with the left. He hasn’t scored but he’s getting there, and if he can add these small things to his game it will put him in an even better position.”

Ngumoha’s 71st-minute attempt was reminiscent of Mohamed Salah in its intent, if not in execution. The Liverpool great’s final season at Anfield may have been the exception to the exceptional in terms of his own contribution but, as an education to a gifted and hungry young winger, it was not wasted.

Virgil van Dijk noted that “a few senior players” have taken Ngumoha under their wing. “I would say Cody [Gakpo] is definitely part of that. Everyone is chipping in but for him to work with Mo last year was obviously massive. Mo was one of the best wingers at the club and experienced everything so why not soak in all the information and show it on the pitch and show your own qualities? I think he has shown it this season but there is still much more to come. He’s pretty electric at times and he showed it again. He was a complete threat constantly and their defender had a tough time.”

View image in fullscreen Rio Ngumoha proved a constant threat to Villarreal. Photograph: Richard Martin-Roberts/CameraSport/Getty Images

The Salah comparison was not the only throwback for Liverpool against Villarreal. It was a flawed performance with Van Dijk’s early mistake, Iraola’s initial formation and Liverpool’s lethargy on the ball all punished by Iñigo Pérez’s slick side. “It was a terrible start,” the Liverpool captain said. “I think the saying is you fight an uphill battle and as a defender it is pretty difficult to come back from it. I tried but it was a bad day at the office personally but we do it together with 11 players. We turned it around and that’s the main thing.”

The rousing recovery, the relentless high press, Iraola’s bold changes and the character required to overturn a 2-0 deficit all carried echoes of the Jürgen Klopp era. Given that was where Liverpool wished to return when replacing Arne Slot with the Basque coach this summer, Iraola’s 11th game in charge showed development is not confined only to Ngumoha.

Van Dijk said: “If you look at it from that perspective, it is like that. We train a lot, tactically as well, but because there are so many games you learn playing games and this was a test in that sense because Villarreal were good on the ball. They also rotated a lot so you have to find moments when you can press them and when you can win the ball high.

“Is this squad used to that [pressing style] because I don’t think many players have been part of that? What the manager wants us to do is something which resonates with Liverpool and it is down to us to show it in each and every game. It’s not easy, it’s demanding, but if you want to win games and win games in the Liverpool way then we have to do it.

“The first half was obviously not good at all and the second half was solid and we turned it around and that’s a good sign. Now we have to get ready for Brighton, a super team, which is coming.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Champions League drama galore – so why do we feel hollow?
Sports.content:
IS BIGGER REALLY BETTER?

Now then, which one of you hipsters decided to put Porto 0-1 PSV on? Oh dear. This was another night of Bigger Cup at its Bigliest self, comebacks everywhere, 40 goals in nine games, six of those in a best-v-best clash as Paris Saint-Germain rallied late against Barcelona. Even in defeat, Lamine Yamal found space to decorate the room with a ludicrous toe-poke equaliser, and there was a wholesome tale in Italy as Scott McTominay scored twice for Napoli in their 4-3 win against Bodø/Glimt. These were his first strikes since returning from heart surgery, taking his tally at the club to 29 goals in 86 appearances. No wonder Erik ten Hag was peeved with his bosses at Manchester United for shipping the midfielder off to Naples.

But even after all that, Football Daily feels hollow, as it does for most of Bigger Cup’s group stage. The absence of jeopardy in the 36-team table remains a sore point, as PSG magnificently demonstrated during their back-to-back title-winning campaigns. In 2024-25 they finished 15th, taking seven points from their first six games; in the old days this meant a third-place finish in your group and a humiliating retreat to Big Vase. In 2025-26 Luis Enrique’s side settled for 11th and, once again, embraced their punishment of an extra knockout round. To be fair, this season they look as if they want to put their feet up in February, sitting pretty at the top with three wins from three.

Liverpool, too, would have been OK without a special night at home, having won their first two games, but try telling that to the Kop. They got the thrills of coming back from two goals down to beat Villarreal, under-the-pump Florian Wirtz hit the decisive goal, and Rio Ngumoha received plenty of love. The visitors got the full Anfield experience, with Villarreal’s manager, Iñigo Pérez, confessing: “We weren’t able to handle the emotion.”

Having said all that, try telling Michael Carrick that the match in Como doesn’t really matter, that it’s perfectly fine if his United side make it two wins in 11 games this season. Cesc Fàbregas’s side are the opposition, which should make you feel really, really old. The boy who infamously flung some pizza in an Old Trafford melee, splattering Sir Alex Ferguson, is enjoying himself on the touchline. All grown up, he could make life seriously messy for another Manchester United manager.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Simon Burnton from 5.45pm BST for Como 6-4 Manchester United in Bigger Cup, while Scott Murray will be all over Bayern Munich 5-3 Arsenal and Sarah Rendell will be on hand for a clockwatch covering the night’s other goalfests.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“Before ‌every game I asked God ‌to let me leave the pitch healthy. But it was in vain. Not much time has passed, yet one thought keeps circling in my head: ‘why me?’ I never held anything back. I think I prepared for this game better than I ever had before. I thought I was ready for everything – but not for this. I know I have to come back stronger for my people, who are ‌always by my side. I won’t let you down – I promise I won’t waste a single moment.” – Khvicha Kvaratskhelia vows to recover stronger after it was confirmed that the winger will have surgery following an ACL injury sustained during the 4-2 victory over Barcelona. Ousmane Dembélé and Marquinhos also suffered thigh tears that will keep them out for a few weeks.

Sports.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
Sports.content:
Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra.

I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri.

As a player and a columnist, I never had an issue with Manchester City – precisely because, for many years, the club avoided buying the most obvious superstars. Guardiola said it himself: the most valuable of the valuable do not go to a club such as City, who aren’t even the biggest football brand in their own home town.

Many became world stars in Manchester. Kevin De Bruyne had been discarded by Chelsea, Rodri’s true class was overlooked in Madrid for a long time, Gündogan’s career was on the brink after injuries, and most recently Gianluigi Donnarumma was no longer wanted in Paris. In Germany, City signed players from Hamburg, Frankfurt and Wolfsburg. Erling Haaland in 2022 was the first player they targeted who was also pursued by Bayern Munich. City did not operate like Paris Saint‑Germain did in the era before Luis Enrique.

From the outside, City fundamentally did not do much differently from the other 10 or so top European clubs. But what are achievements on the pitch worth if they are accompanied by rule-breaking? The club have been found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial regulations between 2009 and 2018. It allegedly invested almost €1bn more than allowed and declared. The league leaders face potential forced relegation or titles being stripped. City continue to deny wrongdoing and are appealing against the decision.

It is right for the Premier League to crack down on unfair competition. I also appreciate that Germany is holding on to the 50+1 rule, which the federal cartel office recently upheld. It ensures that the majority of voting rights must remain with the parent club – the non‑profit section of a professional club. The exceptions that have applied to Leverkusen and Wolfsburg are under review.

View image in fullscreen A Manchester City fan holds up a banner during the club’s Premier League match with Ipswich at the Etihad Stadium. Photograph: Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty Images

The bedrock of our football culture is 50+1. This rule exists only in Germany, yet it speaks to a spirit that fits perfectly with the European sports model: 50+1 maintains a balance; on the one hand it allows for investment, on the other it guarantees participation. It strengthens the rights of members and fans. Perhaps it is because of this rule that the average attendance in Germany is higher than anywhere else in the world.

What is the ultimate purpose of football? It is a business, but its infrastructure is still developed by the general public. That is how I have always understood sport. Even as a professional, it was clear to me that my privileged life was made possible by many people working on a voluntary basis. Through my role as tournament director of the European Championship, these political connections have become even clearer to me.

The stadium and football clubs can remain the final places where people gather and society debates its issues only if the elite and the grassroots stay connected, and the public is involved in the process. Football must not be detached from its roots, as was the case with Manchester City. This becomes possible when rules are enforced by an institution. Ideally, not by a commercial entity but by a non-profit one such as Uefa.

In business, as in politics, I am observing a shift in mindset. Today, it is deemed necessary to invest in non‑profit institutions. More and more companies realise that football allows for a genuine exchange with the population – that it provides the perfect vehicle to set up corporate social responsibility projects.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This is what is needed in these politically turbulent times. In our fragmented world, political parties, churches and the media have lost credibility. In sport, however, people still come together. It is a tool to foster social cohesion. Therefore, I consider 50+1 to be a distinct competitive advantage for the Bundesliga.

I also welcome the fact that rules mean something in another case. Uefa is standing firm against Gianni Infantino, who recently wanted to privatise the World Cup and its profits. Along with his friend Donald Trump, he was seen by many as breaking the normal rules when Folarin Balogun’s suspension was lifted. The outcry from the global football community was loud, and it is possible that the Fifa president will fall.

When behaviour such as that in Manchester and at Fifa is punished, it is a good thing. Football must prevent questionable ideas from distancing it even further from its grassroots. Only then can it drive engagement in civil society, and only then can it strengthen Europe.

Philipp Lahm’s column was produced in partnership with Oliver Fritsch at the German online magazine Die Zeit.

Sports.title: Coach banned until 2048 for training children in DR Congo while suspended for sexual abuse
Sports.content:
A coach in the Democratic Republic of the Congo who was banned from football for 20 years by Fifa for sexual abuse of a minor has had his ban extended by five years to 2048 by the world governing body.

Jonathan Bukabakwa, known as Messi, has also been ordered to pay an additional fine of $15,000 (£11,200) after the Guardian revealed he had continued to work with young players despite his suspension.

The Congolese Association Football Federation (Fecofa) and Racing Club Baki, where Bukabakwa was coaching, have been fined $50,000 each by Fifa’s ethics committee for failing to comply with its decision to ban him for 20 years in 2023.

Quick Guide How do I 

Fecofa has also been instructed to introduce a “comprehensive education, compliance and monitoring programme for its officials, affiliated clubs and registered members” to try to ensure there is no repeat.

“The Congo DR Football Association, the club Racing Club Baki (formerly known as Esperanto FC), and the coach Jonathan Bukabakwa were found responsible for failing to comply with the decision rendered by the Fifa ethics committee on 18 October 2023,” said a Fifa statement.

Bukabakwa, who previously coached youth teams in the Limpopo and Malabo regions, was convicted of sexually abusing minors by authorities in the DRC and was released from prison last year. A Guardian investigation in August revealed there was video footage of him coaching young players at Esperanto in the Limete district of the capital, Kinshasa. Local sources confirmed he had regularly been seen taking charge of players on a school field.

Bukabakwa did not deny continuing to coach young players but claimed he had not been informed of his Fifa ban. He said he had not been questioned or received any communication from the governing body. He has denied the allegations against him.

The case has raised further questions about safeguarding in Congolese football and the ability of authorities to ensure that suspended individuals do not continue participating in the sport. Bukabakwa was provisionally suspended by Fecofa in November 2022 after media reports of alleged widespread sexual abuse in the DRC. Several other coaches were provisionally suspended at the time, although investigations into some of those other cases did not establish sufficient evidence for further action by Fecofa or Fifa.

Véron Mosengo-Omba, elected as Fecofa’s president in May, has promised to look into the previous cases once he has re-established a disciplinary committee. Fecofa was under a Fifa-appointed normalisation committee from 2023 until his election. “We will make sure that no one who is behaving like this will be involved in football in this country,” he said.

Sports.title: CHRIS WHEELER: Man United were insipid, lifeless and downright ugly in tame Como surrender. How much longer can Michael Carrick and his team sleepwalk through this wretched season?
Sports.content:
CHRIS WHEELER: Man United were insipid, lifeless and downright ugly in tame Como surrender. How much longer can Michael Carrick and his team sleepwalk through this wretched season?

At full-time, Michael Carrick walked straight over to the few Manchester United fans who were left at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium and held up his hands in apology.

They had stood drenched through the wind and rain that whipped off Lake Como and witnessed one of their club’s worst nights in Europe. It has to be the most picturesque venue in the Champions League by some distance, but on a night like this it was downright ugly and so were United.

How much longer can this go on? How much longer can United sleepwalk through this wretched season as Carrick continues to grasp hopelessly for positives? If this turns out to be his last stand, it was a tame surrender.

A fifth defeat in 11 games against a Como side inspired by the excellent Nico Paz hardly begins to tell the story of one of United’s biggest embarrassments. They were insipid. Lifeless. The confidence and self-belief has been sucked out of this team.

It’s eight games since United last won, beating Sabah of Azerbaijan in this competition and recording their only clean sheet of the season. The 700 fans who made the journey to Lombardy stood in one of the areas of this stadium exposed to the elements beneath Giuseppe Terragni’s Monumento ai Caduti that sits at the head of the lake. It means monument to the fallen, and how much further can United keep falling from here?

This was meant to be the biggest game in Como’s history and they played like it. Cesc Fabregas’ team are a credit to the former Arsenal midfielder and it’s not by chance that they lie fifth in Serie A.

Manchester United were completely outplayed by Como as they lost 4-1 to the Italian side

The dreadful result heaps further pressure on under-fire Red Devils boss Michael Carrick

This was an incredible night for Como, but one of the worst in United's European history

Como 4-1 Man United: MATCH FACTS Como 1907 (4-2-3-1): Butez 6; Couto 7 (Smolcic 80, 6), Ramon 7, Kempf 6, Valle 6; Milla 7, Perrone 8 (Dossena 80, 6); Da Cunha 7, Paz 9 (Ricci 80), Baturina 7 (Caqueret 64, 7); Douvikas 8 Goals: Paz (2, 57), Douvikas (49), Ramon (76) Booked: Kempf Manager: Cesc Fabregas 8 Manchester United (4-2-3-1): Lammens 4; Dalot 3, De Ligt 3 (Amass 79, 5), Maguire 4, Mazraoui 3; Mount 3, Santos 4 (Baleba 46, 5); Mbeumo 4 (Lacey 86), Tielemans 4, Cunha 3 (Amad 46, 6); Fernandes 4 (Zirkzee 67, 6) Goal: Zirkzee (90+1) Booked: Santos, Baleba, Lacey Manager: Michael Carrick 3 Referee: Sven Jablonski 6

But Manchester United coming to town is no longer what it was. This is a pathetic imitation of the teams that have represented this great club down the years.

Shortly after the half hour mark, their supporters broke into a chorus of ‘attack, attack, attack’ which is never a good sign for any United manager.

From the chance that fell to Diogo Dalot in the opening seconds to Matheus Cunha’s tame effort on the stroke of half-time, they didn’t have another effort on goal in the first half.

Yes, Carrick was without nine senior players, forcing him to put Matthijs De Ligt into the starting line-up without playing a minute of football in the last 325 days due to a back injury, and name Jack Fletcher and Tynan Thompson on the bench even though both players had featured in the UEFA Youth League defeat to Como earlier in the day.

But that was no excuse for another performance that left you wondering just what these United players are doing on the training pitch all week – and what Carrick is saying to them.

If there was concrete evidence that they simply aren’t learning or progressing, it came after two minutes here. A week after United conceded after 50 seconds to Atletico Madrid in Spain, they were behind again.

‘Coming away from home in Europe, you want to see the ball and try to control the game,’ Carrick told TNT Sports before kick-off, and yet his team did the exact opposite.

No sooner had Dalot curled an effort wide after mistakenly creating the opportunity for himself by miscontrolling Cunha’s pass than Paz converted a similar chance at the other end.

United had been warned about the gifted Argentine, but you wouldn’t have known it by the way Harry Maguire stood off the 22-year-old when he received a pass from Lucas Da Cunha inside the box with Como’s first attack of the game. Paz looked up, picked his spot and guided the ball beyond Senne Lammens.

He was simply too much for United to handle. Andrey Santos was booked for hacking him down on the near touchline with a crude challenge, and Cunha resorted to similar tactics.

Argentina wonderkid Nico Paz was Como's star as he scored twice and laid on an assist

Paz put his side ahead in under two minutes after United's defence mistakenly stood off him

When Paz raced through in the 41st minute and Lammens pulled him down, the United goalkeeper was relieved to see the flag go up for offside before parrying another goalbound attempt from him after Noussair Mazraoui gave the ball away with a wayward pass.

Carrick made changes at half-time, sending on Amad Diallo and Carlos Baleba for Cunha and Santos so that Bryan Mbeumo could play through the middle. He also asked his full-backs, Dalot and Mazraoui, to switch sides.

It’s another sign of the growing crisis around Carrick that it only made things worse as United conceded another early goal.

Martin Baturina had gone close to a goal twice before half-time, so it was no surprise to see him extend Como’s lead. Paz was the architect this time with a fine pass to Baturina who got away from De Ligt and powered a shot past Lammens.

United were three down eight minutes later and staring at a humiliation. Baleba gave the ball away to Paz close to halfway and no United player looked like getting near him as he surged downfield and finished clinically.

Carrick’s misery was complete in the 76th minute when Jacobo Ramon, one of the rising stars of this team and best young defenders in Serie A, got the fourth.

United couldn't match Como's intensity and were insipid and error-ridden, which included Carlos Baleba giving the ball away for their second goal

United were awful and Carrick even hooked captain Bruno Fernandes in the second half

Joshua Zirkzee scored a consolation goal in added time but it was barely acknowledged

It was a measure of the brimming confidence in Fabregas’ side that his centre-back felt able to charge forward in open play and meet a left-wing cross from substitute Kaiki Bruno. No-one had tracked Ramon and he beat Lammens with a thumping header.

Carrick sent on teenagers Harry Amass and Shea Lacey which felt like a pathetic response to a pathetic performance. Joshua Zirkzee scored from close-range in the 91st minute but the damage was done.

As Carrick and his players fly home on Wednesday night, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the United board have to decide where they go from here.

Sports.title: England legend Sir James Anderson RETIRES from cricket at 44... after Lancashire tell him they will not give him a new contract for next summer
Sports.content:
England legend Sir James Anderson RETIRES from cricket at 44... after Lancashire tell him they will not give him a new contract for next summer

Jimmy Anderson’s long career is finally at an end at the age of 44 after Lancashire declined to offer him a new contract for the 2027 season.

Anderson, who took a record 704 Test wickets for England and this summer collected 50 wickets for Lancashire at 17 each in division two of the county championship, was told earlier this week by the club’s new chief executive, Richard Kenyon, and their new director of cricket, Paul Farbrace, that his time at Old Trafford was over.

Daily Mail Sport understands that Anderson will not look to extend a county career that began in 2001, bringing to an end one of the modern game’s great fast-bowling stories. In all, he took 1,193 first-class wickets at 24 each, as well as 358 in one-day cricket and 71 in T20s.

Barring an unexpected late franchise detail, that appears to be it. Since Anderson has only ever played T20 cricket for England and Lancashire, and said he ‘hated every minute’ of his two-match stint with Manchester Originals in The Hundred in 2025, that seems unlikely.

He had been mulling over the possibility of captaining Lancashire next summer, having done the job in 2026, when they struggled for runs and finished second-bottom in the championship, ahead only of Gloucestershire. It was their worst finish since 1984.

James Anderson took 50 Championship wickets for Lancs at an average of 17.7 last season

Anderson was knighted by Princess Anne in 2025 for his services to cricket

Anderson took 704 Test wickets for England and celebrated winning the Ashes Down Under

Their on-field struggles were reflected by turmoil off the pitch, with chief executive Daniel Gidney stepping down after 14 years in charge, and Mark Chilton sacked as director of cricket.

Farbrace, once England’s assistant coach, has been brought in from Sussex to replace Chilton, and presented with a simple brief: to return Lancashire, who won the most recent of their nine championship titles in 2011, to the top flight.

Anderson had hoped to be part of that push under the new management, only to be told otherwise. The club’s fans may ask why they are getting rid of one of their two most successful bowlers from 2026 (George Balderson picked up 53 wickets at under 22 each), especially with only two others – Tom Bailey and Mitchell Stanley – taking more than 12.

But Farbrace and Kenyon, who left Nottinghamshire to move to the club he supported as a boy, are determined to start afresh in 2027, leaving Anderson to contemplate, at long last, a life outside the game.
