Sports.title: Featured Comment: Budget cap not to blame for lack of winning teams in F1 | Brief
Sports.content:
This week’s poll asks whether Formula 1 needs to rethink its budget cap as the series’ top four team have pulled further away from their rivals this year.

But reader @Skydiverian suggests it might not be realistic to expect F1 to regularly have more than four race-winning teams:

Four competitive teams has happened before but it’s still not great and the problem is as it always is, money. And I’d like to see more teams in a season have a realistic shot of winning races. It’s unfortunate that the stats are not on my side.

Pretty much since the late 80s the problem has been that the best teams could throw more money at the problem to fix it. Now, teams that are significantly behind can’t throw more money at the problem to catch-up due to the cost cap, rather than simply not having the money in the first place as was common in the 80s. (This season is interesting. It seems that Mercedes blew most of it’s cap early to get and maintain their advantage, whereas Red Bull didn’t and that’s in part why Max has had a better car the last two races. But it’s not like Williams or Aston Martin can fix their problems by spending more money to fix the deficit).

The problem is that ultimately there’s no easy fix, but spending millions to be the so-called best of the rest basically seems pointless if there is a very unlikely chance of a team outside of the top four having a realistic shot at the podium or even a win. And that’s always been a problem going back decades.

Some number crunching by looking at the history books: the 500th race was 1990 Australia, 1,100th being Vegas 2023. In those 600 races I’ve found six that were won by drivers driving for teams who finished outside the top four in the constructors championship.

That’s six of 600 races over 33 years where we had a winner driving for a team who finished outside the top 4 in that years constructors championship, 1% of all races. Seven if you count Johnny Herbert’s win at the Nurburgring which to me was a genuine surprise at the time. To me those stats aren’t good enough.

Whether that’s the fault of teams with no money, teams with too much money or teams with a cash limit so they can’t design their way out is up for debate. But my point is that I’d like to see more teams have a reasonable chance of winning. F1 has never really had that and will continue not to unless something changes (maybe by letting teams further down have a bigger budget the following season rather than just more CFD time).

I’d rather that at least 70% of drivers have a realistic chance of winning, ideally 100% of teams. It’s the reason I preferred IndyCar before Alex Palou showed up, results were unpredictable and smaller teams have a chance of getting a win or two. That’s just so rare in F1 and the current cost cap rules will continue to make unlikely.

@Skydiverian

Sports.title: Early coronation for Antonelli? Five talking points for the United States Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli could win the world championship this weekend in only his second year as a Formula 1 driver. Here are the talking points for the United States Grand Prix.

Will Antonelli clinch the title?

The odds are stacked heavily in favour of Mercedes’ new star clinching the title at some point, but most likely not this weekend. That said it is not beyond the realm of possibility team mate George Russell could have another poor weekend and come away point-less while Antonelli takes his ninth victory of the season, putting him over the line.

The title has been won at this track twice before, and both times it was by a Mercedes druver: Lewis Hamilton won the championship there in 2015 and 2019. But regardless of whether Antonelli does clinch the title this weekend it is clearly a matter of ‘when’ not ‘if’.

Verstappen dominating again?

The driver most likely to delay Antonelli’s championship celebrations is not his team mate but Max Verstappen. Red Bull have made a breakthrough with their RB22 and as well as winning the last two grands prix plus a sprint race, Verstappen could have taken victory in Baku as well with better luck.

He arrives at this weekend’s race looking like the driver to beat, with every indication he could dominate the final rounds of the season, setting himself up for a shot at the title next year.

McLaren’s driver headache

McLaren arrive in Austin in a curiously similar situation to last year: a clash between their drivers at the previous race in Singapore has created an obvious tension. What’s more, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri’s collision during the sprint race in Singapore was more costly than the one they had in the grand prix 12 months ago.

Norris’s radio messages during the grand prix gave the distinction impression he was looking for ways to make amends, having eventually accepted he was the one at fault for their collision. But above all the team will be anxious to avoid a repeat of the first-corner collision which wrecked their sprint race at the circuit 12 months ago. Particularly as a resurgent Red Bull are poised to relegate the reigning constructors’ champions to fourth place in the standings.

US teams’ driver decisions

Of the two teams competing in their home event this weekend, one has settled its driver plans for 2027. Haas has announced Rafael Camara as the replacement for Esteban Ocon, whose Formula 1 future is in serious doubt as few likely alternatives remain for next year.

Could Cadillac be one of them? F1’s new American team is yet to confirm its plans for next year. However its hopes IndyCar star Colton Herta would take Formula 2 by storm and make himself an obvious candidate for promotion have been dashed: he lies 19th in the standings, 181 points behind fellow rookie and championship leader Camara.

Are Colapinto’s die-hards paying attention?

Last week Franco Colapinto spoke out in criticism of the element of his fanbase which has sent vile abuse to his rival drivers, team members and FIA officials since he made his F1 debut this year. The Alpine driver told those attacking others in his name that they are not helping his cause in F1.

Will they take his words on board? We’ll get an indication the next time he is involved in any kind of incident on-track – however slight it may be.

Sports.title: On This Day: Ralf Schumacher wins Formula Nippon title despite spinning out | Brief
Sports.content:
30 years ago today Ralf Schumacher won the Formula Nippon title despite retiring two laps into a rain-lashed race.

Schumacher arrived at the final race at Fuji Speedway just two points ahead of team mate Naoki Hattori. But Schumacher spun out two laps into the rain-hit race (see 3’50 in the video below).

That left Hattori on course for the title, which looked increasingly secure as the laps ticked down. But conditions worsened, and seven laps from home he spun out too, handing Schumacher the 1996 title. Schumacher made his F1 debut the following year for Jordan (now Aston Martin).

Katsutomo Kaneishi won ahead of future Formula 1 driver Pedro de la Rosa. Another future F1 driver, Shinji Nakano, took fourth place behind Masahiko Kageyama. Just seven of the 26 starters were running at the finish.

Sports.title: Jack Catterall Ready As Teofimo Lopez Deadline Hits Tomorrow
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall has made it known he is ready to get down to business with the October 22 deadline running out for talks on his ordered WBA welterweight title fight against Teofimo Lopez.

The British southpaw went onto social media while waiting to see if he lands his mandatory crack or gets hit with another postponement.

“READY FOR A FIGHT,” Catterall posted, tagging DAZN Boxing to make sure the network heard him loud and clear.

That puts Catterall’s stance out there in four words. He wants an official date on the calendar, yet the WBA process has not produced one.

Teofimo’s side has tried to get special permission to go after a different opponent, looking into a massive unification clash against Ryan Garcia for early 2027. Catterall stands as the main roadblock for that route because the WBA already issued the order for its super champion to face him next.

Catterall picked up the WBA regular title by beating Shakhram Giyasov back in May. Grabbing that strap put him in direct position for the bout he is trying to nail down right now. Five months have gone by, and he finds himself still stuck waiting for that mandatory pathway to deliver an actual ring return.

The deadline hits at the close of business Eastern Time on Thursday, October 22. It represents the conclusion of the official discussion window set up by the WBA, not an automatic guarantee that Teofimo gets stripped on the spot.

The pending appeal keeps Catterall hanging around for a ruling that will dictate who he faces and how quickly he gets back under the lights. He recently talked about his career being stalled out, and his latest message makes it obvious that no agreement came together behind closed doors.

There is a huge cash reason for Teofimo to chase Ryan Garcia instead. That matchup pulls in massive public interest compared to a mandatory chore against Catterall. Still, Catterall followed every single sanctioning body rule to earn his spot, and a giant commercial payday for the champion does nothing to restore the lost months Catterall spent on the shelf.

Sports.title: Brandon Figueroa’s Team Believed 75% Would Beat Kameda
Sports.content:
Brandon Figueroa’s corner figured a three-quarters version of their fighter could still handle Tomoki Kameda. Instead of an easy night, pushing through a wrecked training camp produced a blown scale reading along with a scrapped title defense.

How they talked themselves into that position tells the real story. They watched Kameda struggle against Angelo Leo, convincing themselves they had spotted an opponent Figueroa could overpower on cruise control. Counting on an opponent’s flaws while dragging a hurt fighter through a brutal cut was asking for trouble from day one.

Chris Mannix outlined that logic after sitting down with Figueroa alongside trainer Manny Robles during fight week. According to Mannix, the team rolled the dice on the belief that a seventy-five percent Figueroa could handle a fully prepared Kameda. Robles pointed directly to Kameda hesitating to let his hands go against Leo as justification. Spotting flaws in Kameda did nothing to heal Figueroa’s compromised body.

“They took a calculated risk that they believed that 75% of Brandon Figueroa was going to be good enough to beat 100% of Tomoki Kameda,” said Mannix on his channel.

Sergio Mora painted a grim scene from the hotel. Figueroa looked completely drained, showing sunken cheeks alongside zero energy in his voice. Mora also picked up zero real belief from the camp members standing around him.

Those details leave the team with little defense. This went beyond routine fight-week sluggishness. Their own timeline showed an injury disrupting preparation, followed by an obvious physical collapse trying to make the limit.

Mora mentioned Tim Bradley stepping up to challenge the room, asking them directly why they were walking toward the ring while compromised. Bradley told them bluntly that no purse justifies risking long-term health. Mora suspected Bradley played a major part in talking them off the ledge, even if that remains his personal read on the room.

Purses drove the train too. Mora noted the team nodded in agreement when he brought up walking away from guaranteed money. Mannix pointed out another worry, specifically that Figueroa lacked any guarantee about landing another broadcast date anytime soon.

Uncertainty explains the pressure. It still fails to justify putting a fighter in harm’s way.

Kameda did his job, locked in his weight, then watched his title shot vanish on fight morning. Figueroa completely dumped the momentum built from stopping Nick Ball.

Pulling the plug was the only acceptable move once Figueroa broke down. The heat belongs squarely on the days leading up to it, when his corner treated Kameda’s flaws as an excuse to ignore their own fighter’s reality.

Figueroa blew the biggest payday of his career in the process. Keeping that belt would have placed him directly in the crosshairs for Naoya Inoue’s planned jump to featherweight in 2027. Holding a world title gave him the one bargaining chip the Japanese star actually needs.

That belt was Figueroa’s golden ticket. Facing Kameda was simply supposed to be the routine checkpoint to keep him in line for the jackpot.

Instead, he walked out of Las Vegas with an empty bank account, no strap, plus a ruined argument for landing Inoue. While that clash was never locked in stone, tossing the hardware away stripped Inoue’s handlers of any reason to look his way.

That reality turns the corner’s gamble into pure negligence. Figueroa’s team got tunnel vision worrying if a three-quarters version could slide past Kameda, completely blind to what blowing the scale would cost down the road.

Sports.title: Keith Thurman Expects Less Volume From Vergil Ortiz
Sports.content:
Keith Thurman is already spinning Vergil Ortiz Jr. as a more manageable problem than Sebastian Fundora, which tells you everything about how veteran fighters rationalize dangerous matchups.

Thurman is betting that a drop in incoming punches equates to breathing room. Trading Fundora’s exhausting, awkward flurries for Ortiz’s firepower is a terrible bargain.

Fundora drowned Thurman in non-stop punches, but Ortiz does not need triple-digit punch outputs to ruin someone’s night. He sits down on every single delivery, cuts off escape routes, and forces opponents into survival mode.

“Virgil might be holding back his volume, but his power is going to be more intense,” Thurman told MillCity Boxing. “So, once again, it’s dangerous.”

Thurman talking about Ortiz holding back volume sounds like wishful thinking from a fighter trying to talk himself into believing he will get space to operate. He even tries to compare the transition to his past fights against Shawn Porter and Danny Garcia. Porter brought a relentless dogfight, while Garcia offered pauses between exchanges that allowed Thurman to reset his feet.

“I think he’s going to be easier to match the volume, the two-punch combos, the three-punch combos,” Thurman said.

The fatal flaw in that logic is simple: Garcia let fighters off the hook. Ortiz hunts. Those quiet moments Thurman thinks he will exploit between short combinations will not be rest periods. They will be traps where Ortiz walks him into the ropes and forces him to backpedal under heavy artillery.

At 37, Thurman’s legs look gone compared to his prime. He used to circle the perimeter, plant his feet, fire a quick combination, and skip out of range before anyone could touch him. Against Fundora, he had no snap left to hold his ground, which is why he spent from rounds 3 to 6 of that fight purely in track-and-field mode.

If Thurman refuses to sit down on his shots, Ortiz Jr. will walk through him. A dangerous puncher only respects what is coming back at him. The moment Ortiz Jr. realizes Thurman is strictly on his bicycle and throwing nothing to deter him, he will pin his ears back, cut off the ring, and trap Thurman on the ropes. Without pop on his punches to gain Ortiz’s respect, running just delays the inevitable while draining Thurman’s dwindling gas tank.

The threat of a referee stoppage is very real here. Against Fundora, Thurman reached a point where he was offering zero offensive resistance, and ringside officials will step in every time if a guy looks like target practice and shows no intention of fighting back.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Backs Tyson Fury To Stop Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
Frank Warren is convinced Tyson Fury stops Anthony Joshua inside the distance, pinpointing AJ’s defensive lapses during his own offensive bursts as the decisive flaw.

Fury’s timing and counterpunching remain central to Warren’s prediction. The promoter views the dynamic much like he viewed Daniel Dubois’s upset win over Joshua, even while admitting neither man is operating at their athletic peak.

“Styles make fights. I believe the same as I believed Daniel, when he fought AJ, he would knock him out and beat him. I think Tyson would do the same thing,” Warren said to Sky Sports Boxing. “I just feel that Tyson has his number, in my opinion. Maybe wrong. The one thing about AJ, as we all know, he can whack.”

Warren’s logic involves the split second Joshua commits to his combinations. While Joshua’s power creates danger whenever he fires, his delayed guard gives an elite counterpuncher clear targets before his hands return home.

“When he throws his shots, he leaves himself very vulnerable, and Tyson’s a good counterpuncher,” Warren added.

Capitalizing on those windows requires sharp reflexes, something that naturally diminishes with age. Warren admitted the bout will look different than it would have years ago, predicting a tighter, less mobile collision where neither heavyweight retreats.

“I think they’ll both be a little bit slower than they were,” Warren said. “I think it’ll be very exciting whilst it lasts.”

Warren dresses it up with complex talk about technical openings and counter angles, but the fundamental flaw is Joshua’s punch resistance. Once a heavyweight’s chin cracks, no amount of technical adjustment can compensate for it.

The warning signs were impossible to miss against Kristian Prenga. Surviving Dubois is one thing because Daniel hits with concussive force, but getting buzzed and nearly closed out by a fringe guy like Prenga signals that Joshua’s internal alarm system is permanently compromised. Every time clean contact lands, his legs betray him immediately.

Fury does not possess one-punch power, yet that makes little difference when the target crumples under ordinary pressure. With his towering frame and natural bulk, Fury merely needs to absorb the initial storm, step into the pocket, and let his hands go until something connects flush. A clean tap on a ruined chin does the exact same job as an explosive shot.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Aims To Become Undisputed Champion
Sports.content:
Las Vegas, Nevada – On Saturday night, Sebastian “The Towering Inferno” Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) defended his WBC junior middleweight championship at The Chelsea inside the Cosmopolitan Casino against the very tough and gritty Ermal “The Albanian Sniper” Hadribeaj (23-1-1, 8 KOs).

It was a much more challenging match than many expected; Hadribeaj tested Fundora on the inside by making him miss and countering him with an efficient attack. The Albanian Sniper’s total connect rate of 32.3 percent was more effective than The Towering Inferno’s 25.9

percent.

However, Sebastian did outland Ermal in total punches 202 to 144, outlanding him8 of the 12 rounds(Compubox). Fundora was able to score the finishing blow in the last second of the twelve-round fight, winning the fight by controversial knockout.

After the fight, Sebastian said, “It was an interesting fight. I had to go back and fight on the inside and show everyone again that I can still do that. It was dramatic to knock him out at the last second, but we’ll go back to the gym and fix some things.”

He added whom he’ll like to fight next by saying, “I want to go for undisputed in this division. We’ll break either Jaron Ennis or Josh Kelly down just like the last guy and the guy before that. We’ll keep breaking them down. When asked of the two whom he expects to win, Fundora answered, “I do favor Boots.” Meaning him and promoter Sampson Lewkowicz believe it will be Boots whom they’ll have to negotiate for the undisputed crown, but they appear they’ll be playing hardball in negotiations.

Lewkowicz told the media after the fight what he expects the terms of the contract to be, “It doesn’t make any difference…because we need each other. We need 50-50 because we want to unify. It doesn’t matter how many titles. I see so many st**d guys saying on the internet saying he has three belts. You have only two. People already saying he has three.

So many people saying he have three belts. Who’s he fighting? A bum? I respect boxing, and I tell you Kelly can fight.” Sampson went on to state he had already spoken to Jaron’s advisor on the expectations of terms, making it known it should be a 50-50 fight, and hopes they don’t deviate from it by requesting a higher percentage for themselves.

However, if the fight for undisputed does happen next year, the winner of the Boots-Kelly fight will be a three-belt holder bringing the WBA, WBO, and IBF titles to the table, with Fundora holding the single WBC belt. The undisputed showdown is a fight fans will want to see and will truly crown the junior middleweight king.

Hopefully both sides can come to an amicable agreement, and the fight won’t get derailed as were the contract negotiations between Boots and Vergil Ortiz Jr. For now, Sebastian will rest and wait for the Boots-Kelly winner and prepare for his next goal of becoming undisputed junior middleweight king.

Sports.title: Chris Algieri Doubts An 80% Canelo Alvarez Beats Christian Mbilli
Sports.content:
Chris Algieri argues that Canelo Alvarez must bring his absolute best to get past Christian Mbilli. His claim that Mbilli’s style naturally plays into Canelo’s hands doesn’t hold up, especially given the challenger’s relentless engine.

Algieri does give Canelo credit for stepping right into danger following surgery and significant time away, acknowledging the grueling physical test awaiting him.

“Can we give him a little respect for coming off a layoff and a surgery right into Mbilli?” Algieri pointed out to DAZN Boxing. “Yes, he has his faults. I think he falls right into Canelo’s style, but what Canelo are we getting? If Canelo is at all degraded, an 80% Canelo probably doesn’t beat Mbilli. He’s got to be top-notch for that fight.”

Even a peak version of Canelo might have struggled with this matchup. While aggressive fighters give Canelo plenty of targets, Mbilli refuses to give up the breathing room Canelo usually buys with crisp counterpunches.

Gennadiy Golovkin applied pressure behind a stiff jab, leaning on heavy single shots. Miguel Cotto relied on movement during the twilight of his prime. Neither fighter swarmed with the sustained, multi-punch bursts that define Mbilli’s game.

Canelo typically hurts opponents until they freeze. They back off, rethink their strategy, let him rest, and wait for his next opening. Mbilli simply ignores that script.

Mbilli isn’t invincible, of course. Charging forward recklessly leaves massive openings, and eating flush counter hooks could quickly check his enthusiasm. Canelo has the precision to make him pay for being aggressive. Yet landing clean shots is vastly different from dictating the tempo. If Mbilli walks through fire and keeps throwing, Canelo has to scramble back into a defensive shell before his lungs catch up with the previous exchange.

Managing that volume would test any elite fighter in his prime. Asking a 36-year-old coming off major surgery and ring rust to endure it is an entirely different proposition. Algieri is spot on about the danger here. His warning that an 80% Canelo falls short might ring true, but treating an ultra-high-volume brawler as tailor-made for him severely understates the threat.

If Canelo cannot discourage Mbilli inside the first four rounds, the math turns ugly very quickly. By round six, when Canelo’s output routinely dips and his feet go flat, he will be forced to shell up against the ropes while Mbilli pounds away at his arms, shoulders, and ribs. Heavy volume wears down legs just as fast as clean headshots, especially for an aging fighter carrying thirteen months of inactivity and repaired joints.

Surviving that kind of physical tax requires supreme conditioning and fluid defensive pivots. If Canelo is stuck playing defense just to survive the onslaught, he will not have the legs or the gas tank left to mount a mid-fight rescue. When a fighter relies strictly on finding one perfect counter shot to bail himself out, every missed swing empties the reserve that much faster.

In 2019, Canelo capitalized on a faded, battle-worn Sergey Kovalev, whose gas tank was depleted, waiting out Kovalev’s tired arm punches until round eleven to land the finishing blow. Now, the dynamic has flipped, and Canelo finds himself occupying the aging fighter’s corner against a younger, relentless pressure puncher.

Kovalev came into the fight at 36 with heavy miles and well-documented physical wear, and Canelo is carrying an even larger cumulative toll. With more than two decades in the professional ranks, chronic joint issues, and elbow surgery following a year on the shelf, the engine simply cannot turn over the way it once did.

The pattern across the Jaime Munguia, Edgar Berlanga, William Scull, and Terence Crawford bouts showed a fighter relying almost entirely on bursts, resting for extended stretches, and depending on defensive posturing to steal rounds on ring generalship. Against Crawford, the inability to sustain offense or dictate the terms of engagement laid bare what happens when elite opposition refuses to grant Canelo those customary rest periods.

Against Mbilli, relying on selective counterpunching becomes a dangerous gamble. Landing a crisp left hook or a sharp uppercut only helps if it forces the incoming fighter to step back, reset, and second-guess their entry. If Mbilli treats every clean counter as a cue to unload another four-punch salvo to the body, Canelo will never get the pauses he needs to recharge.

Sports.title: Abdullah Mason Targets William Zepeda Or Joe Cordina
Sports.content:
Abdullah Mason is targeting a December return against William Zepeda or Joe Cordina, with a lightweight unification fight or another defense of his WBO title under consideration.

Mason says nothing is signed, but those are the two names emerging for his next appearance. He is also willing to travel to the UK to face Cordina after being told visa issues prevented the British fighter from meeting him in the summer.

“Right now it’s looking like it could be a unification with Zepeda or a defense with Cordina,” Mason said to Brian Custer’s channel. “That’s what it’s looking like it could be. So I’m definitely ready to face anybody in that position.”

Zepeda would give Mason the opportunity to add the WBC belt and test himself against a pressure fighter who believes he can wear the young champion down. Asked about Zepeda’s claim that he would struggle to last 12 rounds, Mason declined to make a counterprediction.

“Two fighters got to step in the ring to really see how it’s going to go down,” he said.

That would be the harder physical test. Zepeda’s volume would force Mason to decide when to trade and when to use his feet. Mason’s willingness to fight aggressively could make it an action fight, but he would need to avoid letting Zepeda dictate how much work he does every round.

The Cordina option offers a different route, and Mason has no objection to defending on the challenger’s side of the Atlantic.

“If he’s had visa issues in the summer, I’m ready to go over there,” Mason said. “It’s a huge fight card in December in the UK. Why don’t I fight him over there if they can’t come over here?”

Mason did not identify the event or confirm a place on it. His December plans remain a target rather than a completed deal.

“Nothing confirmed, nothing signed off on, but that’s what it’s looking like, and that’s what we’re pushing for.”

Mason’s promoters at Top Rank rarely throw a young fighter into a risky fight when they can take an easier route to build an international footprint. Zepeda represents pure peril right now. His punch output breaks people down, and Top Rank knows Mason is far too young to be taking that sort of physical punishment if it can be delayed.

Letting Zepeda put more miles on the odometer before signing off on a unification makes total promotional sense.

Cordina is the soft landing spot. He gives Mason a recognizable British name to put on the record, introduces the young champion to UK fans on a big DAZN card, and presents minimal stylistic danger. Cordina likes to pick his spots from the outside and does not push a blistering pace, which plays right into Mason’s hands.

It would be a low-risk voluntary defense disguised as a big overseas trip, keeping Mason active, winning, and out of harm’s way while Zepeda’s prime ticks down.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Departure Brings Relief Within Zuffa
Sports.content:
Some inside Zuffa Boxing actually welcomed Shakur Stevenson walking away. When the planned Devin Haney matchup collapsed, the company found itself staring down massive financial obligations with zero marquee headliner to show for it.

Dan Rafael noted that parting ways worked out for both camps, despite the optics sting of Zuffa dropping a prized marquee acquisition right out of the gate.

“There are some people that are sort of relieved that they’re not going to, you know, go down that pit of that money,” Rafael said to Total Boxing.

The broadcast setup explains plenty about why Zuffa executives felt that way. Per Rafael, even if Haney versus Stevenson crossed the finish line, the US broadcast rights belonged to DAZN instead of Zuffa’s domestic partner Paramount+. Zuffa faced bankrolling an enormous purse just to drive its biggest potential viewership straight to a competing network.

Rafael pointed out that securing both men in the ring demanded north of $20 million just for the main event. Spending that kind of cash to cement Shakur as the promotion’s central figure, while asking Paramount+ subscribers to tune in elsewhere, looked like bad business.

When the Haney talks cratered, backup plans looked rough. Zuffa put a hold on Newark’s Prudential Center for January 23, but finding a credible dance rival for a hometown showcase proved tough. Footing an astronomical bill for a soft touch would leave Zuffa paying elite rates without the blockbuster that validated signing Shakur initially.

“I don’t think that everybody involved with Zuffa Boxing and/or their parent company TKO was that upset that they were able to separate because I think they might have had some buyer’s remorse,” Rafael said.

Shakur exiting before ever fighting under the banner definitely hurts Zuffa’s reputation, especially after hyping up the Haney clash. Still, the numbers explain the decision. Retaining Shakur only worked if Zuffa locked down the right opponents alongside favorable platform deals to balance the books. Once Haney slipped away, cutting ties cost far less than trying to patch up an expensive mistake.

Shakur commands elite, eight-figure purses, but his track record does not show independent pay-per-view drawing power or the ability to move tickets outside of a localized Newark gate. When a promoter guarantees that kind of money, the fighter has to generate massive subscription spikes, sell out neutral venues, or command major foreign site fees. Shakur has not done any of that on his own.

His safety-first, low-volume style makes that financial gap impossible to bridge. Fans want drama, sustained action, and knockouts. Shakur is technically brilliant, but his emphasis on distance control and minimal engagement often draws boos from casual crowds and turns off broadcast executives looking for viral, highlight-reel content. Promoting a fighter with that approach is an uphill battle, especially for an outfit tied to the UFC and TKO brand, where audiences expect relentless pressure and decisive finishes.

Paying top-dollar purses for Shakur to out-point mismatched opponents in tactical dull contests would have eroded fan interest and bled capital fast. Zuffa avoided footing the bill for an expensive, low-entertainment asset who brings little commercial leverage to the table.

Ghana News.title: SIMI summit reaches 1,000 people with health screenings, NHIS registrations in Bono
Ghana News.content:
Sustainable Impact Makers International (SIMI) says its 2026 Health Equity Summit reached more than 1,000 people in the Bono Region, combining community advocacy, health education and preventive services to address barriers to healthcare access.

The three-day initiative, held in Sunyani from July 23 to 25 under the theme “Health Equity in Action: From Periods to Parenthood, For All,” recorded more than 420 screening encounters across 13 service categories and completed over 500 National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) registrations.

About 800 secondary school students also participated in a film screening and facilitated discussion on issues including menstrual health, consent, early marriage and school retention.

In its newly released 2026 summit report, SIMI says the activities were designed to bridge the gap between people’s understanding of preventive healthcare and their ability to access services.

The report cites research indicating that only 10.3% of breast cancers in Ghana are diagnosed at Stage I or II, compared with the Global Breast Cancer Initiative benchmark of at least 60%.

It also references a study of male teachers aged 45 to 60 in the Sunyani Municipality, which found that although 95% recognised the benefits of prostate screening, 90% had never been screened.

SIMI says the findings highlight the need to address barriers that prevent people from translating health awareness into action.

The report further notes that adolescent pregnancy in the former Brong-Ahafo Region, which included the present-day Bono Region, remained above the national average across three decades of surveys.

It also identifies the limited representation of traditional and religious authorities in formal health governance as a concern, given their influence on community attitudes and health-seeking behaviour.

SIMI organised the summit around three priorities: mobilising communities, empowering people through education and dialogue, and enabling access to preventive health services.

The programme opened with a 5-kilometre community advocacy walk intended to raise awareness of health equity and encourage collective responsibility for community wellbeing.

A subsequent policy dialogue brought together health professionals, policymakers, educators, traditional authorities and faith leaders to discuss community health priorities and possible responses.

At Sunyani Senior High School, a screening of NAWI, followed by a facilitated discussion, provided students with an opportunity to engage with issues including menstrual health, consent, early marriage and school retention.

The summit’s service component was delivered in partnership with the Ghana Health Service, Bono Regional Hospital and other clinical teams. It offered health screenings, health promotion activities and NHIS registration.

According to SIMI, bringing the services closer to residents provided practical opportunities for participants to act on health information and access preventive care.

SIMI calls for stronger referral pathways

Beyond the immediate activities, the report emphasises the need for effective referral systems to ensure that people who undergo screening can access further assessment and appropriate treatment when necessary.

It also introduced the Sunyani Pledge: 90-Day Health Equity Challenge, inviting participants to commit to achievable actions within their communities and institutions.

SIMI says the initiative provides a foundation for continued collaboration among communities, healthcare providers, policymakers and traditional and religious leaders.

The full report outlines the summit’s delivery figures, priorities identified by community members, limitations and recommendations for advancing health equity in the Bono Region and beyond.

Ghana News.title: Asutifi North sound system operators demand justice for allegedly assaulted colleague
Ghana News.content:
Sound system operators in the Asutifi North District of the Ahafo Region are demanding the arrest and investigation of two prison officers and three inmates allegedly involved in an attack that left their colleague, Opoku Afriyie, severely injured.

The group is calling on the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), the Minister for the Interior and national security authorities to intervene, saying more than a month after the incident, the suspects have not been arrested.

Afriyie, a sound system operator, commercial motorbike rider and farmer, was allegedly attacked with machetes by the two officers and three inmates from the Kenyasi Settlement Camp Prison over allegations of yam theft.

The operators say the absence of arrests and a public update from the Ahafo Regional Police Command has heightened frustration among residents and could deepen tensions between the community and law enforcement.

Speaking to JoyNews in Kenyasi on Tuesday, Clement Austin, a social event moderator with Emmanuel Sounds, said the suspects should be held accountable under the law.

He said the Constitution guarantees equality before the law and the protection of human rights and dignity, adding that the allegations against Afriyie did not justify the reported attack.

Mr Austin called on the police to arrest the suspects, insisting that no one should be treated as guilty without evidence and due process.

Kwame Bandasco of Great Vim Ventures warned that further delays could trigger legal action and sustained civil pressure on the Ghana Prisons Service in the district.

He said the group had been demanding arrests and justice since the incident and insisted that the two prison officers should be investigated immediately.

DJ Slim of Pomaa Sounds also questioned why no arrests had been made, arguing that a civilian accused of attacking prison officers and inmates would likely have faced swift police action.

The operators further alleged that management of the Kenyasi Settlement Camp Prison had approached traditional leaders, religious figures and politicians in the region to mediate an out-of-court settlement on behalf of the suspects.

They have cautioned those leaders against intervening to settle the matter outside the formal justice system, citing what they describe as a history of unresolved abuses involving security personnel in the district.

The group wants the police to investigate the incident and allow the legal process to proceed, saying accountability is necessary to restore confidence and prevent further tensions.

The allegations against the prison officers and inmates have not been established in court. The group’s account of the incident and the alleged attempts at mediation could not be independently verified from the information available.

Afriyie, who is recovering slowly at home, says the injuries have left him unable to work and provide for his family.

In an interview with JoyNews, he said he now relies on the support of neighbours and loved ones to care for his wife, children and 80-year-old mother.

The father and farmer, who owns three farms, said the attack had disrupted his livelihood and left his family struggling to meet their daily needs.

The operators say they will continue pressing the authorities to act until the case is investigated and justice is pursued through the formal legal system.

Ghana News.title: US citizen Stephen Hubbard freed by Russia as Trump envoy meets Putin
Ghana News.content:
Russia released a 74-year-old American citizen who was jailed for allegedly fighting on behalf of Ukraine, as President Vladimir Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg for talks.

Stephen Hubbard had been taken to the city's Pulkovo Airport, Putin said during the meeting early on Wednesday.

President Donald Trump later said the former teacher was "on his way back home" and "there was no 'swap' necessary". Following the release, Witkoff called Putin a humanitarian.

Hubbard, who was sentenced to almost seven years in a penal colony in 2024, was accused of serving in a defence unit in eastern Ukraine when he was captured in 2022, shortly after Russia's full-scale invasion.

CBS News, the BBC's US media partner, reported that Hubbard had been in poor health and was expected to be flown to Texas for treatment.

Witkoff gave praise to Putin for releasing Hubbard, saying: "You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian - you are a humanitarian also sir, and I salute that. I commend you."

His comments sparked a backlash from lawmakers in the Republican party, with Representative Don Bacon posting on social media that it was "another embarrassment". Senator John Cornyn said Putin "is a stone cold killer".

In response to a question from the BBC about the backlash, Vice President JD Vance said Witkoff's "job is to go over there and get a job done".

"I care much less about what Steve said than about the fact that he is bringing an American hostage home to his family," he said during a press conference in Ohio on Wednesday.

Hubbard was later seen thanking Witkoff as they met separately. Putin's financial adviser Kirill Dmitriev was also present.

Writing on social media after Russian state media reported the release, Trump said it had followed a request he "made directly" to Putin last week.

In the past, detained Americans have primarily been released from Russia through prisoner swaps.

Trump also appeared to defend his recent decision to suspend sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to come into force, writing that "if sanctions would have been placed", negotiations for Hubbard's release "would have come to a complete and total halt".

The US state department had previously classified Hubbard, from Michigan, as "wrongfully detained" and Trump on Tuesday had suggested that his release may be imminent.

"Watch what happens," Trump told reporters, "we have been focused ⁠on ​Hubbard".

The state department said in a statement that the release was "a welcome step that we hope leads to the release of all Americans unjustly held in Russia". It also said that "there are currently no Americans determined to be wrongfully detained in Russia".

Russian prosecutors had accused Hubbard of joining a Ukrainian military unit and receiving training and weapons. But his sister, Patricia Fox Hubbard, previously told Reuters that this was unlikely because of his older age and his disinterest in the military.

Hubbard's son, Joseph Coleman, who is an Orthodox priest, said in a statement that he had prayed for many years for his father's release.

"As I await the blessing of embracing him again, I receive his freedom not as a political victory, but as a gift of mercy," Coleman said.

A lawyer for Hubbard, Martin De Luca, posted on social media on Wednesday: "The road to peace is difficult, but its human dividends need not wait for a final agreement."

A spokesman for Putin, Dmitry Peskov, told Russian media that American officials had been seeking Hubbard's for some time, and Putin decided to do it for humanitarian reasons.

Witkoffalsothanked Putin for the deal struck with Washington earlier this month to import Russian diesel, saying Trump was "deeply grateful" for it. Ahead of the US midterm elections in November, where affordability is top issue for many voters, Trump has sought to bring down fuel costs.

The first shipment under the agreement will leave Russia "in two to three days", Putin said during the meeting, as quoted by state news agency TASS.

The diesel dealinfuriated Zelenskyand triggered a tumultuous few weeks of deteriorating relations during which Trump suspended a number of sanctions and said it was time for Ukraine to elect a new leader.

Kyiv meanwhile accused Washington of halting intelligence sharing on deadly Russian strikes, and claimed a sudden restriction to the Starshield internet service in its war effort had been deliberate. Zelensky said on Tuesday that intelligence sharing had resumed.

As talks were under way in St Petersburg, Zelensky posted on social media that "much depends on whether the American side can hear something new from Russia today – about peace, and not about continuing the war".

Ghana News.title: Mustapha Gbande, Joseph Yammin file nominations to retain NDC positions
Ghana News.content:
Deputy General Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Mustapha Gbande, and National Organiser Joseph Yammin have filed their nominations to contest for re-election in the party’s upcoming National Executive Elections scheduled for December 19.

The two party executives are seeking to retain their respective positions on the NDC’s National Executive Board as the party prepares for the internal elections.

Speaking at the maiden edition of the Campaign Trail, an initiative by the NDC’s Elections Directorate, the two outlined their reasons for seeking another term in office.

Mustapha Gbande used the platform to tout what he described as the achievements of President John Mahama’s administration since returning to power in 2025, while criticising the previous Akufo-Addo government.

He said the NDC government had made progress across various sectors, adding that he was proud to have contributed to the party’s return to power.

The joint press briefing provided both executives an opportunity to make their case for re-election as they seek to maintain their positions within the party’s national leadership.

The December 19 elections are expected to determine the composition of the NDC’s National Executive Board as the party continues its internal reorganisation.

Ghana News.title: Arrupe Jesuit Institute to strengthen advocacy and youth empowerment
Ghana News.content:
The Arrupe Jesuit Institute (AJI) has outlined plans to expand its advocacy and youth empowerment programmes under a new strategic plan aimed at increasing its impact on Ghanaian society.

The Institute’s Director, Fr Bernard Jado, SJ, and Head of Programmes, Gifty Appea, presented the priorities to the Superior General of the Society of Jesus, Fr Arturo Sosa, SJ, during his visit to the Institute in Accra on 13 October 2026.

The presentation reviewed AJI’s work, traced its origins and outlined its priorities under the 2026–2029 Strategic Plan.

Its advocacy programmes will focus on human rights, gender-based violence, child protection, safeguarding, refugee and migrant rights, education and environmental protection.

AJI plans to advance these priorities through policy dialogues, public advocacy campaigns, institutional training and contributions to public debate. It also intends to translate research findings into policy briefs and create opportunities for engagement with policymakers.

Youth empowerment, the second pillar of the plan, will cover leadership development, ethical and civic education, financial empowerment, livelihood initiatives and youth-led community projects.

The Institute also plans to strengthen its alumni network to sustain engagement with young people beyond individual programmes.

AJI has already undertaken environmental advocacy through its Environmental Policy Dialogues, organised in collaboration with the Catholic Youth Network for Environmental Sustainability in Africa (CYNESA-Ghana).

These engagements have addressed illegal small-scale mining, ecological responsibility and the vision outlined in Pope Francis’ encyclical, Laudato Si’.

The Institute’s research has also explored migration, integral ecology and Christianity in Africa, examining structural injustices and possible responses.

Through its formation programmes, AJI engages Catholic lay professionals and young people on Catholic Social Teaching, ethics and leadership. Its IYNIGO initiative supports youth empowerment, while its Faith in the Public Sphere programme provides a platform for dialogue on Christian witness, professional engagement and the common good.

However, Fr Jado identified limited and unpredictable programme funding, lean staffing and gaps in organisational systems as constraints on the continuity and expansion of the Institute’s work.

To address these challenges, he said AJI was seeking to diversify its funding sources beyond individual projects and strengthen staffing, governance, monitoring and evaluation, knowledge management and its digital presence.

He also highlighted the importance of strategic partnerships with universities, other Jesuit institutions, dioceses, Catholic professionals, youth networks and policy actors.

Fr Sosa commended the Institute’s work and encouraged its leadership to pursue financial sustainability to ensure the continuity of its programmes and the long-term fulfilment of its mission.

Conceived in November 2018 as an initiative of the Society of Jesus’ North-West Africa Province, AJI was established as a platform for research, formation and social action.

Named after Jesuit priest Pedro Arrupe, the Institute seeks to analyse challenges facing Ghanaian and African societies and propose solutions informed by Catholic Social Teaching.

Ghana News.title: ‘Corporate Ghana must step up’ – Bel Aqua urges business community to invest in youth mental health
Ghana News.content:
Corporate Ghana is being challenged to step up investment in mental health support for young people facing depression, grief, and societal pressures, warning that many lack safe spaces to speak openly or access professional help.

The call from premium bottled water brand Bel Aqua coincides with its 15th anniversary of operations in Ghana.

The company's push follows the fourth edition of its mental health initiative, which brought together students, corporate workers, and members of the public for free consultations with psychologists and psychiatrists.

Speaking at the fourth edition of Bel Aqua’s mental health outreach—which provided free, confidential consultations with psychologists and psychiatrists for students, workers, and the general public—Head of Marketing Chris Addo Sarkodie urged the business community to intervene.

“I think 60 per cent of the people that we've had today are coming from the universities. And if you listen to them sharing their testimonies and their challenges, I think as a country we need to pay attention to them,” Sarkodie said.

To address the gap directly, Bel Aqua announced plans to roll out mobile mental health clinics, taking certified psychologists and psychiatrists directly into educational institutions and workplaces across the country.

According to World Health Organization (WHO) estimates, roughly 13 per cent of Ghana’s population—over 4 million people—live with a mental health condition. However, due to severe infrastructure shortages and high social stigma, an estimated 98 per cent of Ghanaians requiring mental healthcare receive no formal medical treatment.

Ghana currently operates with fewer than 60 practicing psychiatrists nationwide, creating a critical shortage of professional support for young people facing depression, grief, and societal pressures.

Ghana News.title: Bel-Aqua’s Healing Together Vigil draws over a thousand for an evening of music and mental health dialogue
Ghana News.content:
Over a thousand people gathered at Alliance Française in Accra on Friday, 16 October 2026, for Bel-Aqua’s Healing Together Vigil 4.0, an evening combining mental health conversations with live music, comedy and community connection.

Held under the theme “Every Mind Has a Story… Respond with Hope”, the fourth edition formed part of Bel-Aqua’s Take a Break initiative. It followed the Healing Together Walk on 3 October, extending the campaign’s call for people to make time for their mental well-being and support those around them.

At the heart of the vigil was a message that went beyond encouraging people to speak about their struggles: the response they receive matters just as much. The campaign called for listening without judgment and approaching difficult conversations with empathy, care and hope.

Guests were welcomed into an experience zone featuring a Story Wall, hydration and red-carpet interviews before Kwan Pa opened the stage programme with a musical performance.

A mental health conversation moderated by Yaa Bitha brought together Fafa Gozo, founder of the Dzidula Pink Foundation; Dr. Seth Mawusi-Asafo, clinical psychologist and lecturer; Dr. Masha Bashiru, senior clinical and health psychologist; and Jahara Osman, founder of Mental Health Forum. The session brought professional and advocacy perspectives into the evening’s programme, placing mental health dialogue alongside entertainment.

Host Lekzy DeComic guided proceedings with comedy interludes, while performances by Mr. Drew, Kojo Blak and Efya added to the evening’s entertainment.

The evening also featured addresses by Christopher Addo-Sarkodie, Head of Marketing, and Oscar Adaadaare, Regional Sales Manager, both of Bel Aqua, as well as Dr. Vivian Aba Dadzie, Deputy CEO of the Ghana Mental Health Authority.

DJ Sleek led the after-party, giving guests an opportunity to unwind and connect.

The vigil complemented the campaign’s earlier walk from Ayi Mensah to Peduase, where activities included health screening and access to psychologists and psychiatrists. Together, the two events placed mental well-being within community life, combining opportunities for connection with conversations about support.

Through its Take a Break initiative, Bel-Aqua continues to encourage people to make room for their mental well-being. This year’s vigil reinforced the campaign’s central appeal: beyond asking someone to share their story, be prepared to listen and respond with hope.

Ghana News.title: NACOC takes drug education campaign to Diabene SHS
Ghana News.content:
The Western Regional Command of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) has launched a drug education and sensitisation campaign targeting newly admitted Senior High School (SHS) students to raise awareness of the dangers of drug use.

The initiative seeks to equip students with accurate information to help them make responsible decisions as they adjust to the academic and social demands of senior high school.

As part of the campaign, the Commission engaged students of Diabene Senior High School, educating them on the risks associated with drug use, the influence of peer pressure, and the importance of safeguarding their health, education, and future aspirations.

The Commission is focusing on students at the early stages of their SHS education, recognising that the period presents an opportunity to build resilience against negative influences and encourage healthy lifestyles.

The campaign forms part of NACOC’s preventive approach to tackling substance abuse, with emphasis on educating young people before they are exposed to its potential consequences.

The Western Regional Command says the sensitisation exercise will be extended to other educational institutions across the region, with school authorities and relevant stakeholders expected to play a role in promoting a safer and healthier learning environment.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Tunisia jails opposition politician for four years over social media posts
World.content:
Olfa ⁠Hamdi, a US-Tunisian national, was convicted of ‘plotting’ and ‘inciting’ military to disobey orders.

Share Tunisia jails opposition politician for four years over social media posts on social media

A Tunisian military court has sentenced an opposition ⁠leader to four years in prison on charges of plotting against state security and inciting the ⁠military to disobey orders, her lawyer has said.

The charges against Olfa ⁠Hamdi, a dual Tunisian and United States national, stemmed from social media posts, her lawyer Akram Moussa said on Wednesday. Hamdi has repeatedly criticised Tunisian President Kais Saied’s rule and called for a transitional government and early presidential elections.

Critics say the case against Hamdi is the latest in a crackdown on opponents of Saied.

In Tunisia’s 2024 elections, Hamdi, who was then 36, sought to run for president. Her candidacy was rejected for not meeting the 40-year age minimum for candidates.

Hamdi, the leader of the Third Republic Party, was detained at Tunisia’s main airport after disembarking from a flight in February.

She ‌had been living abroad, running a consulting firm in the US after briefly serving as the head of Tunisia’s national airline Tunisair.

Hamdi’s sentence comprises two separate two-year prison terms from two additional convictions and 80,000 dinars ($26,000) in fines, her lawyer said.

Hamdi was also sentenced in March in a separate case to two years in prison. Global human rights organisations have widely criticised the cases against her.

A US Department of State spokesperson told the AFP news agency that Washington was “closely tracking the situation”.

“The [President Donald] Trump Administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of American citizens,” he said.

Rights groups have criticised Saied, accusing him of rolling back freedoms in a 2021 power grab.



Thousands of ‌Tunisians joined the largest protest against Saied in years on Saturday, accusing him of undermining democracy and ‌mishandling ‌the economy. Opposition leaders, activists ⁠and journalists have been imprisoned during his rule.

Saied rejects accusations that he is targeting political opponents and critics, saying the law applies to everyone regardless of their position.
