World.title: Iran determined to keep uranium amid increased war odds, flurry of meetings
World.content:
Tehran had ‘nothing new’ to tell Washington after latest nuclear proposals reportedly offered by mediators.

Tehran, Iran – There has been a flurry of diplomatic activity in the Middle East in recent days, with hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough to end the United States and Israel war on Iran.

Pakistan’s army chief Asim Munir was in Tehran on Wednesday to discuss the war and recent tensions in Yemen. It comes against the backdrop of fears of a new breakout in conflict in the region.

Despite this, Tehran has held firm to its position that the war will not end, and the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen, until the US accepts its conditions.

Iran maintains an unyielding stance on its contentious nuclear programme, which was a factor in the Trump administration’s decision to launch the war on February 28.

“Not a single gram of enriched uranium will be removed from Iran,” Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said late Tuesday after meeting Munir.

But he did not rule out downblending the highly enriched uranium inside the country under supervision from monitors, something Iran has offered before.

Iran’s authorities present the decades-old nuclear programme as a sovereign right and an achievement gained despite strikes, sabotage and assassinations. Rezaei described it as “national wealth” on Tuesday.

Iran has also used low-enriched uranium for civilian purposes like manufacturing radiopharmaceuticals and for power generation at the Bushehr plant in cooperation with Russia.

The authorities argue that surrendering the nuclear programme under military pressure would amount to capitulation, if it did not guarantee that Iran would not be left exposed to more attacks.



US President Donald Trump has repeatedly emphasised since the start of the war that he wanted to dismantle the Iranian nuclear programme. US Vice President JD Vance, however, suggested earlier this month that a “meaningful” reduction in the level of enrichment capacity may satisfy US demands.

Nuclear issue

Before Israeli and US attacks on Iran’s nuclear facilities in June 2025, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) estimated that Tehran possessed 440 kilogrammes (970 pounds) of uranium enriched up to 60 percent. A nuclear bomb would need enrichment of more than 90 percent.

The attacks, followed by further US-Israeli strikes on nuclear sites in 2026, severely damaged Iran’s nuclear infrastructure. With the IAEA unable to inspect key facilities, the current size, condition and whereabouts of much of Iran’s enriched uranium stockpile remain unverified.

Tehran has refused access to the IAEA to inspect its nuclear facilities since the war started, accusing the agency of advancing Western interests through adopting resolutions and referring the nuclear file to the United Nations Security Council.

Iranian authorities maintain they are not pursuing a bomb. But senior Iranian officials, like Rezaei, have publicly questioned the validity of being a party to the international nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty if Iran’s nuclear facilities and other infrastructure continue to be attacked.

Still, Iranian officials have hosted numerous foreign diplomats this week. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov was in Tehran on Monday after attending a meeting with Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries a day earlier. There were also indications of visits to Tehran by other Arab officials.

US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth is also reported to have met Israeli security officials earlier this week. These meetings did not appear to have decreased the prospects of renewed war.

But speaking at a conference for Iranian exporters in Tehran on Wednesday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi cautioned that the country faces threats of more attacks and expansive economic sanctions.

“The reality is that the country is truly in war conditions and the war continues. We have not reached peace conditions and are away from it, so all decisions must be made within war conditions,” he said.

Parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf told Munir that Iran had “nothing new” to tell Washington and expected realisation of conditions offered in New York last month to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days.



Mediators did not publicly divulge details of their proposals to Tehran this week, but were told the US needed to build trust by accepting Iran’s conditions. These include returning to the June memorandum of understanding and recognising an Iran-Oman deal over temporary transit in the Strait of Hormuz.

In addition to a pledge for immediate talks on a bigger deal regarding Iran’s nuclear issue, the memorandum included removing the US naval blockade on southern Iranian ports, waivers for oil sanctions, unfreezing Iranian assets and halting military action in Lebanon and other regional hotspots.

Ellie Geranmayeh, a senior policy fellow and deputy head of the Middle East and North Africa programme at the European Council on Foreign Relations, said it was clear that Tehran would be unwilling to give up its enriched uranium without guarantees of sanctions relief.

“The Iranians have made it very clear, and I see no evidence that’s changing, that they are willing to negotiate over the fate of the highly enriched uranium or access for international monitors, but that has to be directly linked with a very clear implementation protocol for US sanctions relief,” she told Al Jazeera. “We are very far from those types of negotiations at this stage.”

US media cited unnamed officials as saying on Tuesday that the Pentagon was sending the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and a Marine unit to the Middle East. That would present President Trump with a range of strike options after the US midterm elections on November 3.

Over recent weeks, Trump and his officials have further discussed a range of military operations, including hitting Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain to diminish nuclear facilities inside, and dropping the “mother of all bombs” on nuclear and energy facilities. They have also previously raised the idea of seizing Iran’s southern islands on the Strait of Hormuz and assassinating more Iranian officials.

Iran’s state-run Press TV cited an unnamed security official as saying on Wednesday that decision-makers in Tehran have chosen to advance “without any limitations or restraint” if there are more US and Israeli attacks or assassinations.

Geranmayeh pointed out that Tehran had also helped its ally, the Houthis in Yemen, with their advances along the Bab al-Mandeb strait, and even considered potential preemptive strikes to rattle the US ahead of the election.

“One thing we should be watching out for is Israel and the US combining forces on military attacks after the Israeli elections and the US midterms,” she said, after Trump backed Netanyahu’s election bid.

World.title: Thousands march for school funding in Greece
World.content:
Thousands of students and teachers ‌have rallied across cities in Greece, demanding more funding for ⁠education, including better facilities and smaller ⁠class sizes.

The demonstrations echo a wave of youth-led protests across Europe this month, including in France and Albania, where anger over rising costs and alleged corruption has led to clashes with police and major property damage.

Greek police said about 10,000 demonstrators, including school and university students, rallied peacefully in central Athens and the capital’s suburbs on Wednesday.

“From Greece to France, we want public, free education,” protesters chanted as they gathered outside Parliament, where students staged an overnight sit-in nearby before the rally.

Others joined the protests in Thessaloniki, Patras, Larissa and other cities ⁠across Greece in solidarity with growing demonstrations in France and elsewhere in Europe, where rallies demanding educational resources have morphed into angry demonstrations over soaring living costs.

Cost-of-living crisis

In Greece, the protests add pressure to ⁠Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis and his centre-right government as the country prepares to hold elections in mid-2027 amid a weakening economy.

Greece struggled with a serious debt crisis from 2009 to 2018, during which the government agreed to spending cuts in exchange for three European Union and International Monetary Fund bailouts worth about 290 billion euros ($326bn).

But the measures have impacted Greek workers, who are among the poorest in Europe and struggle with stagnant wages, high rents and rising energy costs.



The average monthly salary of 1,500 euros ($1,685) sits at 2009 levels, with many young Greeks having been priced out of housing in ⁠cities by skyrocketing rents.

“Surviving here is very difficult; the ⁠rent is really high, the houses are really small. Our parents can’t make ends meet to pay for our rent, the electricity, for our life here,” university student Georgia Foukidou, 21, who joined the protest in Athens, told the Reuters news agency.

The protests on Wednesday included strikes by primary and secondary school teachers protesting low pay and staff shortages, while substitute teachers demanded permanent positions and reduced class sizes. Public sector workers and other unions also joined the demonstrations.

Education Minister Sofia Zacharaki said prior to the protests that she was listening to student demands, noting that the government was spending more than 733 million euros ($823m) on new student residences and facilities upgrades.

Mitsotakis’ government has also pledged about one billion euros ($1.12bn) in state subsidies and other benefits to offset increased energy costs for households and businesses due to the Iran war and inflation.

World.title: Russia says it is ready to resume talks with Ukraine and US to end war
World.content:
Russia is "ready in principle" to resume talks with the US and Ukraine on ending the conflict, Vladimir Putin's top aide has said.

Yuri Ushakov was speaking after Putin met US President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff in the Russian city of St Petersburg.

Ushakov said a new round could be held next month, and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky later said he wanted this to happen as soon as possible. Kyiv and its European allies have long been pressing Moscow for resumption of the talks halted in February.

Russia has for months refused as it believes it is winning on the battlefield with Ukraine facing an acute shortage of interceptors against deadly Russian missile attacks.

Witkoff went to St Petersburg after meeting Zelensky as well as the leaders of Norway and Finland in the Norwegian capital, Oslo, on Monday.

It is not clear what specific proposals Witkoff brought to Putin, but Zelensky said after talks in Oslo that "strong" security guarantees for Ukraine and energy ceasefire proposals had been discussed.

Ushakov said their ideas were not very "useful".

Top officials from Russia, Ukraine and the US have held several rounds of talks aimed at ending the war that began in February 2022 when Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Russia blamed last month's "massive" Ukrainian strikes during its general elections for their disruption.

Speaking to reporters after Wednesday's talks in St Petersburg, Ushakov suggested that a new round could be held around 10 November in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates.

He stressed that the talks must focus on "building a security system for Russia and Ukraine after the end of the conflict."

A US official later told the BBC that Witkoff and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, another key negotiator, had proposed at Tuesday's talks in the Norwegian capital "a trilateral meeting at the technical level between the US, Russia, and Ukraine".

"This was accepted by the Ukrainians in Oslo yesterday and by the Russians in St Petersburg today," said the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity.

Late on Wednesday, Zelensky told reporters: "We received feedback that Russia... supports a trilateral meeting between our teams. The American side is proposing to do this as soon as possible. We are in favour of it."

Ushakov also told reporters that President Putin reiterated to Witkoff that Russian troops were advancing everywhere across the vast front line and had a "strategic initiative".

Ukraine and its European allies are disputing Putin's claim, pointing to a virtual stalemate on the front.

On Wednesday, Zelensky said he would accept a deal that would freeze the war along the current front line.

"We call it 'ceasefire' or 'stop killings' like President Trump called it. Freeze and stop. And of course this is minimum what we need from Russia today," he told Fox News, adding that security guarantees for Ukraine could be discussed after this.

World.title: Macron accuses foreign leaders of exploiting French riots
World.content:
French President Emmanuel Macron has accused foreign leaders of exploiting the riots which erupted across the country on Saturday for electoral purposes.

Without naming them, he said they were campaigning for forthcoming elections "at France's expense" with their comments on the violence, which erupted on the fringe of cost-of-living protests.

Speaking on a visit to the Middle East, he referred to them as "leaders who are in campaign mode, whether here in the region or on the other side of the Atlantic".

It was an apparent swipe at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces parliamentary elections next week, and US President Donald Trump, for whom mid-term polls fall next month.

Macron said the unnamed leaders had been influenced by fake videos generated by AI about the riots.

Nearly 150 people have been jailed and more than 800 brought before the courts since the riots which gripped Paris and other cities including Lyon, Marseille and Nice.

Video of running battles between masked rioters and police, as well as property being destroyed and stores being looted, spread across social media.

The government admitted the police had "lost control" during the violence, which came after weeks of protests by students over conditions in high schools.

Macron vowed afterwards that the authorities would be "uncompromising" towards "agitators from ultra-left fringe groups", which he blamed for much of the trouble.

World.title: 'Targeted' attack on much-loved MP leaves Australian town heartbroken
World.content:
Wangaratta has been thrust into an unwelcome spotlight this week. Residents in this rural Victorian town are used to catering to tourists passing through on their way to regional wineries, or music lovers visiting its annual jazz and blues festival.

Instead, locals are fielding endless questions about their MP - and having to explain to strangers what it all means for the town's nearly 30,000 people.

They are clearly in shock about what police say was a targeted and deliberate attack on Helen Haines on Monday afternoon, when she was struck by a car just outside her office.

"People are simply dumbfounded and finding it very hard to fathom the scale of this tragedy," Australia's Governor-General Sam Mostyn, who represents King Charles, said at a press conference on Wednesday.

The independent federal MP had to have both legs amputated after she was airlifted to Melbourne. But the "two most important parts of Helen", her heart and her mind, were in "good shape", her husband Phil Haines said.

The MP isn't a divisive figure, locals tell the BBC, and no one can understand why she was allegedly targeted.

"Everyone knows Helen," says Jane Hill, who owns a party supply shop a few hundred metres down the town's main street from where Haines was hit.

"She is a such a good person in our community. She'd go to everything - celebrations, funerals, she's one of those genuinely kind people - and so are her family."

Local man Brendan Nugent, whose father has been good friends with Haines for decades, faces at least three charges over the alleged attack including intentionally causing harm and appeared in court on Wednesday. Police say they are considering further charges, including attempted murder.

World.title: Australian MP loses both legs after alleged car attack, husband says
World.content:
Helen Haines, the Australian MP who was hit by a car in what authorities say was a deliberate attack, has lost both her legs, her husband has confirmed.

Phil Haines said the "horrendous incident" caused his wife significant injuries but "her heart and her mind are in good shape". He added that the "good news in all this is that she's alive".

The alleged attacker, 43-year-old Brendan Nugent, faces multiple charges and appeared in court for the first time on Wednesday.

Nugent was arrested moments after he allegedly drove his Toyota LandCruiser into the independent MP outside her electorate office in the regional town of Wangaratta, about 240km (150miles) northeast of Melbourne.

Haines' "road to recovery will be long and difficult, but we know she is a fighter," her husband said at a press conference in Melbourne where she is being treated.

"She is a determined person who will do her best, with our support and love, to recover. And that is what we hope for."

He thanked hospital staff and people, both in Australia and internationally, who have shown their concern for Haines, and urged those who want to show their support to donate to the Save the Children fund.

"Please keep sending Helen your love," he added.

Earlier on Wednesday, Nugent appeared at the local court to face three charges: dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury, and causing harm to a Commonwealth public official. Police said more charges may be laid, including attempted murder.

Nugent - a local from the nearby town of Tarrawingee and known as an environmental campaigner - remained silent and emotionless during his brief court appearance.

He did not apply for bail and is due back in court in February. Court documents show he was also charged with cultivating and possessing cannabis.

World.title: Family of prison officer killed by IRA receives state apology
World.content:
The family of a senior Irish prison officer murdered by the IRA has received a state apology on Wednesday for failings in investigations into his killing.

Brian Stack, a father of three, was crossing a street in Dublin, after leaving a boxing match in 1983, when he was shot in the back of the neck.

Stack, who was the chief prison officer at the high-security Portlaoise Prison, was left paralysed and died 18 months later, aged 49.

There were three separate garda (Irish police) investigations into Stack's death, but no-one was brought to justice for his killing.

The Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) MicheÃ¡l Martin offered an apology on behalf of the state during a sitting of the DÃ¡il (Irish parliament).

Stack's wife Sheila and her sons Austin, Kieran and Oliver were in the chamber for the apology.

Martin said the Provisional IRA is "still in the possession of all the facts" on this case.

World.title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy
World.content:
Meta, the company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp has been hit with the largest ever fine against it for its business practices.

A judge in New Mexico on Wednesday ordered the company to pay $25bn (Â£18.6bn) following a two week trial earlier this year that found it had spent years lying to the public about how it handled Facebook user data.

"The lies extend beyond Facebook's data practices as well," the judge said, adding they went to "the heart of Facebook's core business practices."

The fine is the largest to date against Meta, which has either been fined or agreed to settle several other lawsuits this year, including an $18bn deal with California over child safety.

The lawsuit stemmed from the role of Meta, then known as Facebook, in what became known as the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

That firm utilized data and information from millions of Facebook users as part of its work in political consulting, including on work related to the 2016 US Presidential election, which saw Donald Trump elected for the first time.

The US Federal Trade Commission in 2019 levied a $5bn fine against the company over its data privacy practices.

Lawyers for New Mexico sued the company over many statements Meta executives had made over the years that user data was never shared with or accessed by third parties without a user's permission, when in reality it had been.

They claimed that the entire population of the state, roughly 2 million people, was impacted by Meta's dishonesty regarding the way it controlled user data. A jury found that Meta had violated state laws more than 40 million times.

"For too long, powerful technology companies have operated as though their size and influence put them beyond the reach of the law," New Mexico Attorney General RaÃºl Torrez said Wednesday.

"Today's result makes clear that no corporation is too powerful to be held accountable."

The state lawyers sought up to $40bn in fines against Meta. Meta had argued anything beyond $3.4bn would be unconstitutional.

Judge Francis Mathew on Wednesday was direct in his decision to fine Meta an amount roughly equal to its profits each quarter.

He said Meta's violations of law and misrepresentations to the public about how their Facebook data was used and shared were "willful" and spanned "more than 11 years," stretching from 2010 to 2021.

Communications between senior executives, including Mark Zuckerberg, were "designed to mislead the public," Judge Mathew wrote in his order.

While the full amount of the penalty against Meta, based on thousands of violations of state law, was calculated as $219bn, Judge Mathew reduced the penalty to the $25bn fine.

A spokesperson for Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

New Mexico has been one of Meta's most notable adversaries in court. The state this year also fined Meta almost $1bn for misleading the public about the safety of its social media platforms for children.

The judge overseeing that lawsuit ultimately compared Meta to an industrial polluter of the air, with its form of pollution being "the psychological harm and sexual exploitation of children."

California and several other states had collectively sued Meta over similar issues related to a lack of child safety features on Meta's platforms and resulting harms to children.

Meta and the states reached a mutual settlement deal, which did not include a fine or any admission of wrongdoing, to end that case only a few days into what was expected to be a multi-week trial.

World.title: Pakistan arrests man wanted by US over $126m postage fraud case
World.content:
Pakistan's cybercrime agency has arrested a man accused of running a counterfeit operation that caused $126 million (Â£94m) in losses to the US Postal service.

Faheem Akram is accused of having sold fake stamps via a fraudulent website in the US since 2023.

He was indicted by a federal grand jury in Florida last month for selling more than five million counterfeit shipping labels to thousands of US customers over the years. Authorities have now shut down the website.

Earlier this month, the US Postal Inspection Service offered a reward of up to $100,000 for information leading to his arrest.

According to the US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida, the 33-year-old from Khanewal, Pakistan, operated LabelsBank.com.

US prosecutors alleged that he sold counterfeit US postage at a fixed rate regardless of a package's weight, size or destination.

The counterfeit labels, usually sold at $2 each, allegedly allowed customers to ship packages at rates far below legitimate prices, resulting in substantial lost revenue and shipping costs to the Postal Service.

An investigation found that more than 5,200 individuals purchased more than 5.1 million counterfeit shipping labels, the office said in a press release.

Akram is charged with one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States and to make and sell counterfeit postage stamps, five counts of making and selling counterfeit postage stamp labels, and four counts of wire fraud.

If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison on the conspiracy and counterfeit postage counts, and 20 years in prison on each wire fraud count, the office said.

World.title: India 'cockroach' leaders who called on election chief to quit are freed from jail
World.content:
Two leaders of the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) have been freed from jail a week after they were arrested for trespassing at a banned protest site in Delhi.

Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka walked out of Tihar jail hours after a magistrate ordered their release. They had been detained by police and jailed after they crossed barricades and climbed over the locked gate at Jantar Mantar.

The historic venue was recently removed from a list of designated protest sites.

The men, who denied wrongdoing, have been calling on India's chief election commissioner to resign. Critics accuse the commission of manipulating voter rolls to benefit India's governing party, charges the commission rejects.

A special executive magistrate court in Delhi, passed their release order, legal news website Bar and Bench reported.

After bail was granted, Das told reporters from a police van: "Truth alone triumphs. Long live the revolution."

Das and Ranka are key leaders of the CJP, which began as an internet joke in May after India's top judge compared unemployed young people to "cockroaches".

World.title: Cheaper chicken, vegetable oil drive 11.5% fall in jollof rice cost – Report
World.content:
The cost of cooking a pot of jollof rice in Nigeria fell by 11.5 per cent between June and September 2026, driven largely by declining prices of chicken, beef and vegetable oil as the main harvest reached markets, according to a report by SBM Intelligence.

The National Average Jollof Index dropped from N29,578 in June to N26,178 in September, marking the largest quarterly decline since the geopolitical research and strategic communications firm began tracking the cost in July 2016.

In its third-quarter 2026 report, titled ‘The Pot Cools, but Not Everywhere’, SBM Intelligence said the decline was concentrated in protein and oil prices, while rice prices remained largely unchanged.

SBM’s index prices the ingredients for one pot of jollof rice in fixed quantities across 13 Nigerian markets in the country’s six geopolitical zones.

The quantities include rice, chicken, tomatoes, vegetable oil, red pepper, tinned tomatoes, onions, beef, salt, curry, thyme and seasonings.

“Chicken and beef together account for N13,800 of the fall,” the report said, noting that protein had been the dominant driver of rising jollof rice costs in its second-quarter report.

The report attributed the sharpest decline to the period between June and July, when the index fell by N2,312, coinciding with the arrival of the main harvest in markets. Prices were relatively stable in August before falling further by N984 in September.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The movement was consistent with inflation data according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), as food inflation eased to 19.57 per cent in August from 20.31 per cent in July, its first decline in six months. Headline inflation also fell to 15.39 per cent in August.

The report said vegetable oil prices fell in nine of the 13 Nigerian markets monitored, with the largest decline recorded in Lagos, where the price of 90 centilitres dropped from N5,000 to N3,000.

“Oil and protein together account for more than half the national decline,” the report said.

Price fall drivers

However, the report cautioned that the decline was uneven across the country, with Lagos and Ibadan accounting for much of the reduction.

Nine of the 13 markets recorded declines of less than 10 per cent, while two barely moved.

Port Harcourt was the only market where the cost of preparing a pot of jollof rice increased, rising from N31,200 in June to N32,000 in September, a 2.6 per cent increase.

SBM Intelligence linked the increase to flooding in Port Harcourt and Obio/Akpor in late September, which disrupted conditions in the city while other parts of the country benefited from the harvest.

The report also identified a recording error in Ibadan’s Bodija and Dugbe markets, where curry and thyme prices had been recorded at about N3,500 each between January and June before dropping to N650 each from July.

It said the apparent reduction in the spice prices was a unit-related error rather than a genuine market movement, meaning the reported 21.3 per cent decline in the cost of jollof rice in the two markets overstated the actual price reduction.

Despite the quarterly relief, the cost of preparing a pot of jollof rice remained 5.8 per cent higher than in September 2025 and 540 per cent above the July 2016 level.

The report also noted that rice prices contributed little to the latest decline, with the staple’s combined price movement across the 13 markets amounting to just N50.

“This clearly shows a point the index has made for years: the Jollof Index is not a rice-price measure. Everything but the grain sets the cost of the pot,” it said.

Regional breakdown

The South-South remained Nigeria’s most expensive region for preparing jollof rice, with Calabar Municipal closing September at N34,600 and Bayside Mbakpa at N34,500. Both markets recorded declines of just N150 from June.

In contrast, the Southwest recorded some of the steepest reductions. Prices in Lagos’s Trade Fair and Balogun markets fell from N34,700 in June to N22,350 in September, a 35.6 per cent decline.

In the Southeast, the cost fell by 5.3 per cent in Onitsha to N21,350 and by 3.2 per cent in Awka to the same amount.

SBM Intelligence said household responses also suggested that consumers were adjusting their food choices as prices changed.

One respondent in Kumbotso, Kano State, who had stopped buying chicken, resumed buying one chicken a week after the price of a kilogram fell from N7,000 to N4,500.

Another respondent in Gwale said the price of a cup of pepper fell from N2,500 to N1,400 the previous year, making it possible to resume cooking stew daily.

The report, however, warned that one quarter of falling prices had not reversed the longer-term increase in food costs, with the national index still substantially above its level a year earlier.

World.title: 2027: Obidient Movement members quit group, endorse Tinubu
World.content:
Some members of the Obidient Movement, a group that championed Peter Obi’s Labour Party presidential bid in the 2023 election, have endorsed President Bola Tinubu as their preferred candidate for the 2027 presidential election.

The members, who adopted a new name, “Batified Obidients”, announced their decision at a press briefing in Abuja on Wednesday.

Adesina Fagbenro-Byron, a former director of Operations of the Obidient Movement, spoke on behalf of the group, saying its members concluded that Mr Obi, now seeking the presidency under the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), lacks the capacity to lead Nigeria.

Mr Fagbenro-Byron said the group had come to the conclusion that the demands of governing Nigeria were beyond Mr Obi’s preparedness.

“Looking back with clear eyes, we have come to see that the demands of leading a country as complex and demanding as Nigeria may have been beyond what Mr Peter Obi was prepared for. This is not to say he did not try, or that his intentions were not sincere. But it became clear to those of us inside the campaign that he was, in many ways, out of his depth without fully realising it,” he said.

He also accused Mr Obi of failing to utilise the expertise and resources of professionals who volunteered their time and skills to support his presidential campaign.

“He did not seem to recognise the extraordinary resource of volunteers around him — professionals who had willingly offered their time, skills, and expertise, eager to help build something better. That vast pool of talent was largely left untapped. The opportunity was there. It was not seized,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Fagbenro-Byron added that the group’s decision was not motivated by bitterness but by its assessment of Mr Obi’s leadership capacity.

“We say this not with bitterness, but with a measure of sympathy for a man who found himself in a role for which he was not fully equipped, and who may not have understood how much support was within his reach. We gave him the opportunity. We gave him the encouragement. Some of us provided the resources. What we could not give him was the capacity he did not have,” he said.

Why the group is backing Tinubu

The group acknowledged the economic hardship, insecurity, corruption and challenges facing Nigeria’s education and healthcare systems under Mr Tinubu’s administration. However, they said that the president’s reforms were gradually producing positive results.

“We saw his government begin, and we saw the regime of reforms he set out to deliver. We have watched those reforms with open minds. They have been difficult. They have been painful for many households,” Mr Fagbenro-Byron said.

He acknowledged that hunger and the rising cost of living had placed pressure on households, while primary healthcare and public schools required significant improvements.

“Terrorism and insecurity are a grave cause for concern. Corruption has not vanished. And we cannot ignore the millions of children who are still out of school — a crisis that threatens the future of our nation,” he said.

Despite these challenges, he said the administration’s policies were laying the groundwork for economic recovery and greater financial capacity for subnational governments.

Mr Fagbenro-Byron referenced the removal of the petrol subsidy, increased allocations to state and local governments, a decline in debt servicing as a share of revenue, stronger foreign reserves and easing inflation as evidence of progress.

“We do not dismiss these realities. We live among them. Yet we have also seen a deliberate direction: the end of the practice of borrowing billions every year to keep petrol artificially cheap; higher allocations reaching states and local governments; debt service as a share of revenue coming down; reserves strengthening; and inflation easing from its earlier peaks,” he said.

He also referenced the Electricity Act, which allows states to establish their own electricity markets, and the Supreme Court’s affirmation of local government financial autonomy as examples of reforms it considered significant.

Mr Fagbenro-Byron further pointed to the federal government’s student loan scheme and the expansion of local fertiliser production as measures it said could support economic development.

“The Electricity Act has opened the door for states to develop their own power markets. Local government financial autonomy has been affirmed by the Supreme Court. Student loans are already supporting hundreds of thousands of young Nigerians. Local fertiliser production has expanded.

“These are not finished victories. They are the foundations of a country that can produce more of what it needs instead of living forever on imports and artificial prices,” he stated

Group adopts new name

As part of its decision to support Mr Tinubu, former members of the Obidient Movement announced they would change their name from Obidients to Batified Obidients and adopt the All Progressives Congress (APC) as their political platform for the 2027 elections.

“We are coming together again. We are former Labour Party and Obidient supporters. We are now shifting our support to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and adopting the All Progressives Congress, the APC, as our political vehicle for 2027, under the name Batified Obidients,” Mr Fagbenro-Byron said.

He said the group’s desire for good governance and sustainable development drove the decision, adding that it considered Mr Tinubu and the APC the most credible option to continue the country’s reform agenda.

“We do not make this choice lightly. We make it because of our common goal: good governance and sustainable development for Nigeria. We believe that, at this moment in our national journey, President Tinubu and the APC offer the most credible direction, the most tested resolve, and the most viable platform to continue the work of rebuilding Nigeria,” he said.

Group pledges mobilisation for Tinubu

The group said it would mobilise voters and campaign for the APC ahead of the 2027 general elections.

It also endorsed Vice-President Kashim Shettima for a second term alongside Mr Tinubu, praising his capacity for teamwork and intellect.

“Therefore, we unequivocally endorse President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for a second term. This endorsement naturally extends to Vice-President Shettima, who has equally demonstrated a huge capacity for teamwork and intellect, and who has so far largely dispelled the fears that many had about a Muslim-Muslim ticket,” Mr Fagbenro-Byron said.

He said the group would reach out to former members, undecided voters and other Nigerians to seek competent and inclusive governance.

He also pledged that they would work to increase the president’s electoral support, particularly in states where opposition candidates defeated him in the 2023 election.

“We will register, organise, campaign, attend rallies, and vote for the APC and for President Tinubu in 2027,” he said.

Mr Fagbenro-Byron acknowledged that not all former Obidient supporters would join the new movement, noting that some had aligned with the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the NDC or the Labour Party.

“We may not be able to bring every Obidient onto this platform. Some have since moved to the ADC, some to the NDC, and some remain with the Labour Party. We respect their choices and wish them well,” he said.

However, he expressed confidence that the new group would attract many former supporters of Mr Obi and help the APC mobilise ahead of the 2027 election.

World.title: Lawal, 14 other candidates sign peace accord in Zamfara ahead of 2027 polls
World.content:
Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal of Zamfara State and 14 other governorship candidates have signed a peace accord pledging to ensure peace and order in the forthcoming 2027 general elections. Lawal is candidate of the ruling All Progressive Congress (APC).

The accord, organised by the Zamfara State Police Command in Gusau, was signed at the Peace Accord and Election Security Summit held in Zamfara State.

The Peace Accord signing ceremony was meant to ensure peace and order for all political parties in the country as a preparation for free and fair 2027 elections.

Governor Lawal, along with all contestants in the governorship, national and state assembly elections, were invited to sign and promise that no one will violate or work against any election processes before, during and after the elections.

The governor signed the accord and prayed for peace, free and fair elections, and all the political parties fielding candidates did the same.

In his speech, Zamfara State Commissioner of Police, Ahmed Mohammed Bello Daga, called on all the contestants to shun, avoid, and not try to violate any election processes before, during and after elections.

He warned that any political aspirant or member of any political party found violating the law will be decisively trailed and charged before the court of law.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Also, the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Zamfara State Command, Kabir Abdul Randawa, assured political parties and residents of the command’s commitment to providing adequate security and ensuring peaceful political activities in the state.

He urged all political parties and candidates to shun intimidation, violence and other acts capable of threatening the peace. Since assuming office on 29 May 2023, Governor Lawal has been in the vanguard of the campaign for general peace and security in Zamfara State.

World.title: Enugu begins surveillance at airport, council areas to curtail Ebola spread
World.content:
The Enugu State Government has begun intensive disease surveillance across the 17 local government areas of the state and at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Emene, to prevent the spread of Ebola in the state.

The Commissioner for Health in Enugu State, George Ugwu, disclosed this during a press conference in Enugu on Wednesday.

Mr Ugwu, a professor, explained that the intensified surveillance followed the recently confirmed case of Ebola in Abuja and the ongoing outbreak of the disease in parts of Africa.

The commissioner stressed that there was no confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease in Enugu at the moment.

He added that the Enugu State Government has been vigilant and prepared because of the state’s “strategic position as a major travel and commercial hub” connecting the South-east with other parts of Nigeria and the international community through the airport.

The official said the state government, through the Ministry of Health, has been undertaking preparedness activities in collaboration with federal agencies, including the Federal Ministry of Health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, and the airport authorities.

“Specifically, the State has intensified disease surveillance across the 17 local government areas of Enugu State and strengthened coordination with relevant agencies and partners.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Surveillance activities around the Akanu Ibiam International Airport are also being strengthened in collaboration with Port Health Services and other relevant stakeholders,” he said.

Mr Ugwu said the government was further maintaining its Rapid Response Teams and relevant technical personnel on standby, while measures were being reviewed to ensure prompt response in the event a confirmed case was identified.

“Public awareness and risk communication activities are also being strengthened to ensure that members of the public receive accurate and timely information,” he said, assuring that his ministry would continue to work with other federal agencies to prevent possible Ebola spread in the state.

Warning to private health facilities, professionals

Mr Ugwu called on all public and private health facilities across the state to remain on heightened alert and maintain a high index of suspicion for suspected cases, particularly among persons with relevant travel or exposure history.

“I urge all health facilities to cooperate fully with the Enugu State Ministry of Health and other response agencies, as early detection and prompt notification are critical to preventing transmission,” he said.

The commissioner urged all healthcare workers in Enugu State to recognise that they are the first line of defence in protecting our communities and strictly observe infection prevention and control measures.

“The public is advised to maintain good hand hygiene, avoid contact with the body fluids of sick persons, seek medical attention promptly when necessary, and report suspected cases to the appropriate health authorities,” he added.

World.title: Shettima to Governors: End states’ reliance on FG over electricity issues
World.content:
Vice President Kashim Shettima has urged state governments to take full advantage of the Electricity Act 2023 by establishing functional electricity markets, attracting private investment and ending their dependence on the federal government for solutions to local power challenges.

He said Nigeria’s ambition to build a competitive industrial economy would remain constrained unless electricity reforms translated into reliable power for businesses, households and public institutions across the country.

Mr Shettima stated this on Wednesday while declaring open the National Stakeholders’ Workshop on the Electricity Act 2023 at the State House Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja.

The workshop, themed “Unlocking the Opportunities of the Electricity Act 2023 for Sustainable Energy Development and Economic Growth in Nigeria,” brought together federal and state institutions, regulators and other stakeholders to review the implementation of the legislation.

Represented by Deputy Chief of Staff to the President, Ibrahim Hadejia, the vice president said the Act had created an opportunity to decentralise electricity governance and enable states to develop power markets suited to their economic needs and available resources.

“The Act empowers states to develop and regulate intrastate electricity markets within the applicable constitutional and statutory framework. The size, diversity and endowments of this nation demand this decentralisation.

“Electricity supply must become a shared responsibility, pursued with innovation and accountability across the Federation. Our States must shed the habit of waiting for Abuja to provide every answer,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Shettima identified the country’s diverse energy resources as a major opportunity for expanding electricity access, citing solar potential in Sokoto, Borno and Katsina, gas resources in Delta, Rivers and Bayelsa, and hydroelectric opportunities in Niger and Kebbi.

He urged states to translate these advantages into investments capable of powering agriculture, manufacturing, healthcare and education.

The vice president, however, warned that legislation alone would not guarantee improved electricity supply, calling on states yet to establish their regulatory institutions to begin the process without delay.

“Legislation cannot implement itself. States yet to act must begin their legislative and institutional preparations promptly. They need to establish functional electricity regulatory bodies with technical competence and capacity,” he said.

To strengthen implementation, VP Shettima proposed a National Electricity Reform Peer Review and Implementation Framework involving the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC), Federal Ministry of Power, Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) and state electricity regulators.

He explained that the proposed voluntary framework would allow states to exchange experiences, strengthen regulatory institutions and assess progress in market development, investment readiness, consumer protection and electricity access.

“No state needs to purchase with failure the knowledge another State has already acquired,” he said.

According to him, annual voluntary reviews should identify implementation challenges, facilitate technical assistance and promote practical solutions without undermining the constitutional powers of states.

The vice president also emphasised the importance of private sector participation, noting that government funding alone could not meet Nigeria’s electricity infrastructure requirements.

“Government cannot finance this transformation from the treasury alone; private capital must arrive with technology and expertise. Transparent licensing, predictable regulation, commercially viable markets, investment safeguards and credible dispute resolution will earn investors’ confidence,” he stated.

He reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to expanding electricity access through policies that encourage investment, strengthen institutions and improve service delivery.

“Under His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, the Federal Government will sustain policies and partnerships for accessible, reliable, efficient and progressively affordable electricity for households and businesses,” Mr Shettima said.

He also called for stronger consumer safeguards against arbitrary billing, poor service and unfair commercial practices, insisting that electricity operators must be held accountable for service quality.

“The final verdict on this law will be delivered wherever a Nigerian reaches for a switch. Entrepreneurs need dependable power, young Nigerians need employment, and investors need transparent rules under which enterprise can prosper,” he added.

Earlier, the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Power, Mahmuda Mamman, who represented the Minister of Power, said the success of the Electricity Act would depend on the capacity of states to establish credible institutions and commercially viable electricity markets.

He noted that state-level electricity planning would allow governments to respond more effectively to local demand and infrastructure requirements.

Also speaking, the Director-General of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum, Abdulateef Shittu, said the forum was working to strengthen coordination between federal and state institutions in implementing the legislation.

He disclosed that efforts were underway to develop a standard tariff framework for states to protect consumers while promoting investment and commercial sustainability.

Mr Shittu urged stakeholders to ensure that any amendments to the existing legal framework strengthened progress already recorded in electricity regulation.

In her remarks, the Deputy General Manager (Compliance) and Head of Compliance at NERC, Hauwa Yakubu, disclosed that the commission had issued regulatory transfers to 17 states, with Akwa Ibom being the most recent.

She said the commission had continued to support emerging state electricity regulators through peer-to-peer training and technical engagement.

According to her, the Electricity Act 2023 introduced a new era of multilevel electricity regulation, bringing regulatory responsibilities closer to consumers and allowing states to address their peculiar electricity challenges.

Stanley Nkwocha

Senior Special Assistant To The President on Media & Communications

(Office of The Vice President)

21st October, 2026

World.title: Ekiti Assembly passes bill to establish state police
World.content:
The Ekiti State House of Assembly on Wednesday passed the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, to establish State Police Services in Nigeria.

The bill scaled second and third readings during plenary, with all 21 members present supporting its passage, signalling the Assembly’s endorsement of the proposed constitutional framework for decentralised policing.

After the passage, the Speaker, Adeoye Aribasoye, directed the Clerk of the House to transmit the document to the National Assembly, along with the state legislature’s observations.

Speaking on the bill, Mr Aribasoye said the proposed establishment of State Police had remained at the forefront of national discourse for more than two decades, and that the Ekiti Assembly had a historic opportunity to make its position known on the issue.

The speaker stressed the need for effective and responsive security, noting that the challenges of policing in Nigeria required practical solutions capable of addressing the concerns of citizens.

He observed that Nigerians had repeatedly expressed concerns about delayed responses to distress calls, limited operational reach, and the distance between law enforcement agencies and the communities they were meant to protect.

According to him, inadequate and poorly coordinated local policing in some areas had contributed to insecurity, threatening livelihoods, disrupting education, undermining business confidence and eroding public trust.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Aribasoye explained that a properly structured State Police system could strengthen accountability by bringing policing leadership and oversight closer to the people and their elected representatives, subject to constitutional safeguards.

He maintained that the country could not afford unnecessary delays in addressing security challenges, describing State Police as a long-overdue practical necessity rather than a mere theoretical preference.

In its report on the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, the Committee of the Whole House recommended that the Assembly grant concurrence to the proposed constitutional alteration, subject to an amendment to Section 317A(5).

The committee reported that it had considered the bill clause by clause and deliberated on the proposed constitutional framework for the establishment and operation of State Police Services.

Specifically, the committee proposed the insertion of the words “an Act of the National Assembly or a Law of the State House of Assembly, as applicable” after the words “this Constitution” in the newly inserted Section 317A(5).

The observation is intended to expressly recognise the legislative authority of the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly, within their respective constitutional jurisdictions, in authorising relevant security arrangements.

The committee subsequently recommended that the House grant its concurrence to the bill subject to the observed portions, which was among the observations directed to be transmitted to the National Assembly by the Clerk of the House.

World.title: ‘We’ll replace them,’ NDC accuses APC of bribing its candidates to defect
World.content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of bribing NDC candidates to defect to the ruling party ahead of the 2027 general election.

The NDC spokesperson, Osa Director, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday.

Mr Director alleged that the APC had been scheming to lure NDC candidates with inducements, “obviously for pecuniary reasons.”

“The NDC is fully aware of the desperate and malicious tactics of the APC, which has resorted to offering money, political appointments, and other material incentives to induce some money-minded candidates of our party to jump ship and defect to its sinking fold,” he said.

The spokesperson said some NDC members and candidates “who have fallen for this bait” clearly lack the values, virtues, and ideological commitment associated with the opposition party.

“They were never truly of us. To them, we say good riddance to bad rubbish, and we wish them luck in their political misadventures,” he said, without mentioning names.

‘We’ll replace them’

Mr Director vowed that the NDC will replace those who had left the opposition party for another party.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“In line with the provisions of the Electoral Act, 2026, the party will immediately conduct fresh congresses to elect credible, competent, and trustworthy candidates to replace the defectors in the affected constituencies,” he said.

He asked the NDC supporters and members, as well as all Nigerians, not to be perturbed by the antics of the ruling APC in “bribing a few of our members.”

“These are the last kicks of a dying horse that has seen the handwriting on the wall of its imminent defeat,” he said.

The NDC spokesperson added: “The NDC remains resolutely committed to its historic mission of rescuing our country from the vice grip of the buccaneers in power and giving Nigerians the good governance, security, and prosperity they so richly desire.”

APC silent

When contacted on Tuesday for comments on the allegation, APC spokesperson Felix Morka asked a PREMIUM TIMES reporter to forward his questions via WhatsApp because he does not permit phone interviews.

But Mr Morka was yet to respond to the questions forwarded to him via WhatsApp as of the time of filing this report.

Background

The latest accusation comes shortly after the NDC governorship candidate in Bauchi State, Ibrahim Kashim, resigned from the party.

Additionally, speculations were rife on Tuesday that Mr Kashim was plotting to switch to the APC.

Apart from Mr Kashim, Rufa’i Hanga, the Senator for the Kano Central District, had resigned from the NDC in August.

Mr Hanga, the only NDC senator in Kano State, defected to the APC in September.

Kano is the home state of the NDC’s vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Kwankwaso.

Similarly, six House of Representatives candidates and three State House of Assembly candidates from the NDC and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) reportedly left their parties and defected to the APC in late September.

The candidates reportedly came from Taraba, Jigawa, Kaduna, Kano and Plateau states, but their names were not made public.

They were said to have been led into the ruling APC by Aslam Aliyu, who presented them to the party’s leadership in Abuja.

However, the ADC later disowned the defectors, saying the politicians who switched to the APC were never its members.

World.title: Why I get scared whenever Funke Akindele calls me for a job — Jide Kosoko
World.content:
Veteran Nollywood actor Jide Kosoko has revealed that he gets scared whenever filmmaker Funke Akindele calls him for a role because of her demanding approach to filmmaking and attention to detail.

The 72-year-old actor disclosed this during an interview on the African A-List podcast, where he praised Akindele’s work ethic and described her as exceptionally hardworking and energetic.

“Funke is very hardworking; even if you are a man, you can’t match her energy. Whenever Funke calls me for a job, I am always scared. You can shoot a scene 15 times,” Kosoko said.

He explained that the filmmaker’s insistence on getting every detail right sometimes requires actors to reshoot scenes they have already completed.

According to him, Akindele could arrive on set the following day, intending to film a different scene, but decide to revisit an earlier one because of a detail she considered unsuitable.

“She may come the following day thinking of shooting another scene, but then she will say, ‘We have to shoot those scenes again because of the plates they brought’,” he recounted.

Kosoko’s remarks highlight the demands of working with Funke, who has achieved record-breaking success as an actress, director and producer.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Dance strategy

Kosoko also weighed in on the actress’ strategy to push her productions.

Funke’s dance-driven promotional strategy has become a major feature of her film marketing, with the actress and her cast creating choreographed social media videos to generate publicity for cinema releases. The filmmaker reportedly developed the approach after running out of money for traditional marketing following the production of Battle on Buka Street, turning a low-budget idea into a recognisable promotional formula.

However, the strategy sparked debate within Nollywood, with some filmmakers questioning whether dancing and creating social media skits should become an expectation for promoting films. Filmmaker Kunle Afolayan described the demands as “draining” and “unsustainable” at the Lagos Business of Film summit, later clarifying that he was expressing personal reservations about the approach rather than attacking Akindele. Veteran actress Omotola Jalade-Ekeinde has also criticised the expectation that actors must dance on social media to promote films.

But Kosoko, who has featured in Funke’s Jenifa productions, said her approach to promoting her films, particularly her frequent use of dance videos to generate publicity, works for her.

He said other filmmakers have followed Funke’s promotion strategy.

The award-winning actress reacted to the interview clip on X, sharing it with laughing and face-covering emojis.

Funke’s box-office success

The 49-year-old is one of Nollywood’s most commercially successful filmmakers, with several productions hitting major box-office milestones.

Her films include Omo Ghetto: The Saga (2020), Battle on Buka Street (2022), A Tribe Called Judah (2023) and Everybody Loves Jenifa (2024).

Her productions have drawn large cinema audiences, while her energetic promotional campaigns have become a recognisable part of her filmmaking brand despite criticisms.

Kosoko’s account offers a glimpse into the production process behind her films, where repeated takes and close attention to seemingly minor details form part of her pursuit of the desired result.

The veteran actor, who has worked across Yoruba- and English-language productions for decades, remains an established figure in Nollywood, with a career spanning acting, directing, and producing.

World.title: Nigeria, Uganda collaborating to contain Ebola — Health Minister
World.content:
Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare.

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

The Presidential Task Force on Ebola said on Wednesday that the Nigerian government is collaborating with its Ugandan counterpart to contain any outbreak of Ebola.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this while fielding questions from journalists at the end of a meeting at the Office of the Chief of Staff to the President, Rt. Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila.

Asked to react to the statement credited to Ugandan authorities that the country does not have any case of Ebola, contrary to reports that a Nigerian woman contracted the virus in Uganda, the Minister said:

“All I can tell you is that we are collaborating with our sister African nation, Uganda. What is important is that we have found this one case. We are doing contact tracing, and we are putting containment measures in place to ensure that it does not enter our population.”

He said the Federal Government has competent authorities to deal with the development, adding: “We have done it in 2014, and we have good public health institutions.

“Nigerians should be reassured. We must be vigilant, but not panic. People should respect public health information from trusted sources and not spread misinformation and false rumours.

“We would be truthful to Nigerians with the information that we receive on a daily basis. I will be receiving a report. The NCDC has an incident management system.”

The Minister said the NCDC is working hard and that the task force is also active.

“So, we have things in place that give us confidence that Nigeria can weather this public health crisis, which has taken five months without happening, and we have seen other countries also deal with it.

“So, let us not fall into the trap of hysteria or panic. It is one case. It is an imported case, and we are containing it. And we will continue to take measures. If the situation changes, we will come out and inform Nigerians.”

He said that at the last Security Council meeting, there was a push, with the President, to review response plans.

“The truth of the matter is that we have a very good response coordination mechanism involving the Office of the NSA, public health measures and the task force, and that has served us well.

“In fact, we are a large country, and I travel a lot. We have one case, and even that one case came from outside our country. We have been able to detect it, report it and take efforts to contain it. We should not fall into the trap of panic or hysteria, which is counterproductive.

“But we have to be vigilant, and that is what we are doing. In the last 24 hours, we have been on top of it. I am going back to a meeting. We will have another meeting tomorrow (today), so we are on top of it because health security is very important, and we will continue to do that.

“We will be focused. There is a lot of noise from even those who have no idea. Today, just a couple of hours ago, I spoke to the person who discovered the virus 50 years ago.

“It is a 50-year-old virus, and it has had multiple outbreaks in the past. There have been almost 10 or 11 different outbreaks, and they were able to contain them.

“Kenya has been able to contain it. Uganda was able to contain it. France was also able to contain it. But in Nigeria, because people do not think beyond Nigeria, whenever they hear of something new, everybody panics. We cannot be complacent.

“Absolutely, we have to focus. We have to execute. It requires discipline. It is not talk; it is actually doing what is needed. We have the resources, we have the backing of our President, and we have the mechanisms across institutions.

“So, we will continue. Now, it is also left for people to behave responsibly, because if somebody knows something and you say, ‘Oh, isolate yourself,’ and then you hide behind the door and go out to the market, that is not in the government’s hands.”

World.title: Osimhen scores as Galatasaray defeat Lille 4-2 in Champions League thriller
World.content:
Nigerian striker Victor Osimhen scored a crucial second-half goal as Galatasaray came from behind to defeat Lille 4-2 in the UEFA Champions League league phase on Wednesday.

The Turkish champions recovered from a first-half deficit to secure all three points in an entertaining encounter in France, with six goals scored by both sides.

Galatasaray took the lead in the second minute through Yunus Akgün, who converted a rebound from close range after Baris Yilmaz’s cross caused problems in the Lille penalty area.

Lille responded five minutes later as Soriba Diaoune equalised in the seventh minute. The forward received a pass from Alexsandro, drove into the box and fired past Galatasaray goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir.

The French side continued to threaten and took the lead in the 39th minute when Diaoune scored his second goal of the evening. Assisted by Hakon Arnar Haraldsson, he found space inside the penalty area before sending a first-time effort into the top-right

corner.

However, Galatasaray restored parity just before the break. Alexey Batrakov rose unmarked to head home Roland Sallai’s delivery

in the 44th minute, ensuring both teams went into half-time level at 2-2.

The visitors moved ahead again in the 52nd minute when Lille goalkeeper Berke Özer inadvertently turned the ball into his own net.

Osimhen extended Galatasaray’s lead nine minutes later, finishing a swift counterattack with a first-time shot from mid-range after receiving a pass from Yilmaz.

The goal made it 4-2 and gave Galatasaray a comfortable advantage as they sought to see out the contest.

The Nigerian forward had earlier missed a promising opportunity in the 20th minute, while another effort was ruled out for offside in the 69th minute. However, his second-half strike proved decisive in the visitors’ victory.

Lille attempted to mount a comeback, bringing on experienced striker Olivier Giroud and making further substitutions in search of goals.

Galatasaray, however, remained organised defensively, with Cakir making important saves to frustrate the hosts.

Despite late pressure, including a volley from Maurits Kjaergaard that narrowly missed the target, Lille could not find another goal as Galatasaray held on for a 4-2 victory.

The result gave the Turkish side a significant boost in their Champions League campaign, while Osimhen’s goal underlined his importance to the team’s attacking threat.
