World.title: Nigeria, Uganda collaborating to contain Ebola — FG
World.content:
…Health minister urges Nigerians not to panic, says response coordination in place

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — The Federal Government has said it is collaborating with Uganda to contain the risk of an Ebola outbreak, assuring Nigerians that public health authorities are coordinating response measures.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this on Wednesday while fielding questions from journalists after a meeting at the Office of the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila.

Pate was asked to react to reports that Ugandan authorities had said there was no Ebola case in their country, despite reports that a Nigerian woman had contracted the virus in Uganda.

He said Nigeria was working with the East African country while taking steps to contain the reported case and prevent further transmission.

“All I can tell you is that we are collaborating with our sister African nation of Uganda. What is important is that we have found this one case. We are doing contact tracing, and we are putting containment measures to ensure that it doesn’t go into our population,” the minister said.

Pate said Nigeria had competent public health institutions capable of responding to the situation, citing the country’s experience managing the 2014 Ebola outbreak.

“We have done it in 2014, and we have good public health institutions,” he said.

He urged Nigerians to remain vigilant but avoid panic, advising the public to rely on information from trusted public health authorities rather than circulate unverified reports.

“Nigerians should be reassured. We must be vigilant, but not panic, and people should respect public health information from trusted sources, and not spread misinformation and false rumours,” he said.

The minister assured Nigerians that the government would continue to provide updates as more information became available.

“We would be truthful to Nigerians with the information that we receive on a daily basis. I will be receiving a report. NCDC has an incident management system,” he added.

Vanguard Newspaper

World.title: Ebola: Oyo activates surveillance network in 33 LGAs
World.content:
By Adeola Badru

The Oyo State Government has activated disease surveillance networks across its 33 local government areas and prepared its Infectious Disease Centre at Olodo as part of emergency measures against a possible Ebola Virus Disease outbreak.

The government, however, assured residents that no confirmed case had been recorded in the state.

The Commissioner for Health, Dr Oluwaserimi Ajetunmobi, gave the assurance on Wednesday during an interview with journalists in her office, according to a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information, Prince Dotun Oyelade.

Ajetunmobi urged residents to remain calm but vigilant, stressing that the absence of a confirmed case should not lead to a relaxation of preventive measures.

She disclosed that the Ministry of Health had begun preparations since June 2026 to strengthen the state’s readiness to respond to potential outbreaks of Ebola and other infectious diseases, including diphtheria.

According to her, the government had adopted the One Health approach, which promotes collaboration across human, animal and environmental health sectors, to improve disease surveillance, preparedness and emergency response.

She said the initiative involved collaboration with the Ministries of Information, Agriculture and Environment, as well as the Epidemiology Unit of the University College Hospital, Ibadan.

The commissioner explained that the coordinated approach was designed to strengthen disease monitoring and response mechanisms across the state’s 33 local government areas.

As part of the preparedness measures, she said disease surveillance units had been activated across the local government areas, while Information, Education and Communication materials on Ebola transmission, prevention and emergency contact channels had been distributed to health facilities.

Ajetunmobi added that infection prevention and control measures had been reinforced in healthcare facilities, with health workers directed to maintain a high index of suspicion for patients presenting symptoms that could indicate Ebola infection.

She emphasised that strict compliance with infection prevention protocols, including the appropriate use of personal protective equipment, was essential to protect healthcare workers and prevent possible transmission within medical facilities.

The commissioner warned that Ebola symptoms could initially resemble those of malaria and might be mistaken for a less serious illness.

She urged anyone experiencing sudden fever, severe headache, joint or muscle pain, vomiting, diarrhoea, extreme tiredness, abdominal pain or unexplained bleeding to seek medical attention promptly.

According to her, the incubation period for Ebola Virus Disease ranges from two to 21 days, making it important for people who develop suspicious symptoms to report to a health facility or the appropriate public health authority without delay.

On the state’s capacity to manage suspected infections, Ajetunmobi said trained healthcare personnel, including laboratory teams responsible for sample collection and testing, were available to respond to potential cases.

She added that the Infectious Disease Centre at Olodo had been prepared as part of the state’s emergency response arrangements.

The commissioner said the ministry was also intensifying public enlightenment and risk communication to educate residents on how Ebola spreads, the precautions required to reduce infection risks and the importance of promptly reporting suspected cases.

She stressed that effective prevention and containment would require sustained cooperation among government agencies, healthcare workers, the media and communities.

“The Government of Oyo State is taking proactive steps to ensure that the state is adequately prepared to respond to any potential outbreak,” she said.

Reiterating that no confirmed Ebola case had been recorded in Oyo, Ajetunmobi urged residents to avoid spreading unverified information capable of causing unnecessary panic.

She advised residents to wash their hands regularly with soap and water or use alcohol-based hand sanitisers where appropriate.

Residents were also cautioned against direct contact with the blood and other body fluids of suspected or confirmed Ebola patients, as well as materials that might have been contaminated.

The commissioner further urged anyone experiencing symptoms suggestive of Ebola to contact a health facility or the relevant public health authority immediately rather than attempt to manage the symptoms without professional medical advice.

World.title: Tunji-Ojo mourns Fasoranti, says his wisdom will be missed
World.content:
Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA — The Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, has said the wisdom and moral clarity of the late Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti will be greatly missed in Nigeria’s political landscape.

Fasoranti, an elder statesman and leader of the Yoruba socio-political group, Afenifere, died at the age of 100.

In a tribute, Tunji-Ojo said he joined the nation in mourning the late statesman with a heavy heart, describing his death as a significant loss to the country.

“In him, Nigeria has lost a true leader and an enduring symbol of our democratic journey,” the minister said.

He described Fasoranti’s century-long life as one anchored on selfless service, adding that his legacy stood as a testament to principled leadership.

According to Tunji-Ojo, the late elder statesman was a lifelong disciple of the sage, Chief Obafemi Awolowo, and a longstanding leader of Afenifere.

He said Fasoranti remained steadfast in his advocacy for justice, true federalism and the dignity of the Yoruba people, while also upholding national unity and democratic values.

The minister said the late Afenifere leader’s contributions to the political evolution of Ondo State and Nigeria would remain indelible.

He recalled that Fasoranti was recently celebrated in Lagos on attaining the age of 100, describing the occasion as a rare honour that reflected the respect he commanded across generations and political divides.

“Only recently, we gathered in Lagos to celebrate him as a centenarian; a rare honour that underscored the depth of respect he commanded across generations and political divides. That celebration of a life well lived now turns to solemn reflection,” he said.

Tunji-Ojo extended his condolences to the Fasoranti family, the people of Ondo State, members of Afenifere and all those inspired by the late elder statesman’s life.

“May the Almighty grant his soul eternal rest and comfort those he left behind. Adieu, Pa Fasoranti. Your legacy of courage, service, and integrity endures,” the minister said.

World.title: Misinformation, false promises fuel irregular migration — FG
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA — The Federal Government has identified misinformation and false promises as major drivers of irregular migration, warning that decisions based on misleading information can expose prospective migrants to serious risks and devastating consequences.

The warning was contained in a speech by the Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS), Kemi Nandap, at a Stakeholder Sensitisation and Engagement Seminar in Abuja on Wednesday.

Nandap, who was represented by the Deputy Comptroller-General in charge of Visa and Residency, Dr Franca Usiwoma Nwanneka, said people migrated in pursuit of education, employment, safety and better opportunities, but stressed the need for accurate information to guide their decisions.

“Every day people choose to migrate in pursuit of education, employment, safety, and better opportunities. While these aspirations are legitimate, decisions based on misinformation, false promises, or limited awareness of safe and lawful migration pathways can expose individuals to serious risks and devastating consequences,” she said.

The seminar was themed “Bridging the Information Gap: Promoting Informed, Safe and Regular Migration.”

Nandap said human trafficking, migrant smuggling, travel fraud and irregular migration underscored the risks posed by inadequate information and intelligence-sharing among operational stakeholders.

“Preventing these risks requires more than border control. It begins with equipping prospective migrants with accurate, timely, and reliable information to make informed decisions and pursue safe, lawful migration pathways,” she said.

The NIS chief described the service as the agency with statutory responsibility for immigration control and migration management, adding that it continued to strengthen its operational capacity through institutional reforms, modern border management technologies, intelligence gathering and improved service delivery.

She cited the recent deployment of the border control and immigration management system, alongside other technology-driven platforms, as evidence of the service’s efforts to build a modern, responsive and intelligence-led immigration service.

However, she acknowledged that technology alone could not address the underlying factors driving irregular migration.

“Nevertheless, we recognise that even the most sophisticated border management systems cannot on their own address the underlying factors that encourage irregular migration,” she said.

Nandap said the seminar was organised to develop actionable solutions to emerging challenges associated with irregular migration.

She stressed that public sensitisation, community engagement and cooperation among relevant institutions must remain central to efforts to promote safe and lawful migration.

“Migration sensitisation is a shared responsibility that cannot be left to the Nigeria Immigration Service alone,” she said.

The comptroller-general urged government agencies, security institutions, development partners, traditional and community leaders, civil society organisations, educational institutions, transport operators and the media to move beyond discussions and take coordinated, practical steps to combat misinformation and raise public awareness.

“Together, we must ensure that accurate migration information reaches every community, particularly those most vulnerable to exploitation and irregular migration,” she added.

Also speaking, the Senior Programme Associate of the International Organization for Migration (IOM), Nnenna Onuoha, who represented the organisation’s Chief of Mission in Nigeria, Mrs Sharon Dimanche, said the partnership between the IOM and the NIS had continued to grow stronger and produce tangible results.

Onuoha wished participants fruitful deliberations and actionable outcomes, expressing hope that their discussions would help make regular migration a more common and accessible option in Nigeria.

Manchester United’s players react as Como’s players celebrate team’s fourth goal during the UEFA Champions League, league phase matchday 3, football match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia in Como, northen Italy on October 21, 2026. World.title: Ebola: Edo urges calm, compliance with safety guidelines
World.content:
By Ozioruva Aliu

BENIN CITY — The Edo State Government has urged residents to remain calm and comply with public health guidelines following reports of a confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in Nigeria.

The Commissioner for Health, Dr Cyril Oshiomhole, made the call on Wednesday during a press briefing on the reported case.

Represented by the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health, Dr Eighemherio Ikhumosa, Oshiomhole said the state government was monitoring developments in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC).

He described the development as a serious public health concern, adding that the ministry was engaging relevant health agencies and partners to strengthen preparedness and response measures.

The commissioner advised residents to avoid contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of infected persons, wash their hands regularly with soap and water, and use appropriate alcohol-based hand sanitisers.

He also warned against handling the personal belongings of confirmed cases without proper protective measures.

Oshiomhole urged anyone who developed symptoms such as fever, weakness, headache or muscle pain, particularly after possible exposure to the virus, to seek immediate medical attention and follow the guidance of health professionals.

He further cautioned residents against spreading unverified information that could cause unnecessary panic or undermine public health efforts.

The commissioner urged the public to remain vigilant, stay calm and adhere to preventive measures as health authorities monitor the situation.

World.title: Osun Sensitises Transport Operators on New Law, Targets Multiple Taxation
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The Osun State Government on Wednesday sensitised transport operators, vehicle owners, drivers, riders and other stakeholders on the state’s Integrated Transport, Traffic and Park Management System Law, 2026, with emphasis on reducing multiple taxation, curbing illegal collections and improving road safety.

The sensitisation programme, organised by the state Ministry of Transportation, brought together transport union leaders, park managers, commercial vehicle operators, government officials and other stakeholders to explain the provisions of the law and their responsibilities under the new transport management framework.

Addressing participants, the Accounting Officer for the Ministry of Transport Osun State, Olumide Taiwo, said the law was designed to establish a more organised, transparent and technology-driven transport system, adding that the engagement would help operators understand both their obligations and the protections available to them.

“The purpose of this sensitisation is therefore not simply to announce a new law. It is to ensure that the people who will work with the law every day — drivers, riders, vehicle owners, transport associations, park managers and other stakeholders — understand its provisions, their responsibilities and, equally importantly, the protections and benefits available to them,” the Permanent Secretary said.

He explained that the new framework provides for the registration and identification of commercial operators and vehicles, the use of approved parks and loading points, proper display of number plates, roadworthiness checks and improved traffic management.

The law also provides for the use of technology, including electronic identification, QR and NFC credentials, digital payment records, cameras and Automatic Number Plate Recognition systems, to support verification and enforcement.

The ministry said the Daily Operation Levy would be linked to verified commercial operations, with the aim of distinguishing between days vehicles operate commercially and days they remain inactive. The framework is also intended to reduce arbitrary assessments and multiple collections.

Also speaking, the Acting Chairman of the Osun Internal Revenue Service, Solanke Hamzat, said the reform aligned with efforts to make tax administration simpler and more transparent while addressing multiple taxation.

“If you look at the 2025 NTA, that’s the Nigerian Tax Act, Tax Administration, you’ll see that what we are trying to do is to bring tax to be more open, transparent, and eradicate multiple taxation. So simplicity is the key word,” Hamzat said.

He said the new system would also help the government reduce revenue leakages by preventing ticket duplication and other irregularities associated with revenue collection.

“Almost all the collections, the revenue of the government, go directly into government coffers. That’s number one. It will block all leakages, people duplicating tickets and all kinds of antics that people play in terms of collecting government revenue,” he said.

Hamzat added that digital payment records and official receipts would help protect transport operators from repeated demands for payment after they had fulfilled their obligations.

“Once you have paid and you have your digital receipt, nobody can come and harass you again and say, ‘Bring money,’ and all these touts that harass people on the road will now be eradicated,” he said.

On the implementation timeline, Hamzat said the law was already in effect and required commercial vehicle operators to register within 60 days of the governor signing it into law.

“The law is already in effect because in one of the provisions of the law it says that sixty days from the time the governor signs this law into an Act, all road users who are operating commercial vehicles must be duly registered. So it’s already counting,” he said.

World.title: Ogun East 2027: Abiodun’s Performance over Populism
World.content:
Femi Ogbonnikan

The ultimate measure of visionary leadership lies not in partisan posturing or electoral bravado, but in an unyielding record of structural reforms, economic transformation, and tangible project execution.

In an era where public trust is earned through results rather than rhetoric, the electorate has become more discerning in separating performers from mere power-seekers.

As the political landscape of Ogun East Senatorial District shifts toward critical legislative contests ahead of 2027, the imperative for tested, strategic, and forward-thinking representation at the National Assembly has never been more urgent.

Ogun East, comprising nine Local Government Areas and blessed with vast industrial, agricultural, and maritime potential, stands at a historic inflection point.

What it needs at this moment is not a political novice learning on the job, but a tested executive with national clout and international credibility.

Since assuming office as Governor of Ogun State in 2019, Prince Dapo Abiodun has demonstrated an exceptional grasp of governance, turning the Gateway State into an industrial powerhouse and an economic model for sub-national governance in Nigeria.

By methodically upgrading infrastructure, attracting domestic and foreign direct investments, and expanding social safety nets for local enterprises, his administration has fundamentally altered the development trajectory of Ogun East.

His profile for the Senate is therefore grounded not in speculative promises, but in a verifiable and unassailable track record of performance that makes a compelling case for his senatorial ambition.

At the heart of Governor Abiodun’s economic vision for Ogun East is the ambitious $7 billion Gateway Deep Seaport and Blue Marine Special Economic Zone in Ogun Waterside Local Government Area.

Formally sealed through landmark investment agreements signed in Paris, France, with international maritime operator DP World, in the presence of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, and the leadership of the Nigerian Ports Authority, this project stands as a monumental leap for Ogun State’s maritime and industrial capacity.

It is the single largest foreign direct investment (FDI) ever attracted to Ogun East.

Projected to generate over 50,000 direct and indirect jobs in its first phase, the deep seaport complex will establish Ogun East as a prime maritime logistics hub, relieving the perennial pressure on Apapa and Tin Can ports in Lagos while providing direct access to international commercial shipping routes for industries in Ogun, Oyo, and the entire hinterland.

The economic multiplier effect for host communities in Ogun Waterside, Ijebu East, Ijebu North-East, Odogbolu and Ijebu Ode cannot be overstated. Beyond port operations, the adjoining Blue Marine Special Economic Zone will host shipbuilding yards, container fabrication plants, petrochemical storage, and agro-processing clusters, effectively turning the coastal corridor into a new economic city.

To describe a project backed by formal international agreements, federal endorsements, sovereign guarantees, and structured execution timelines as a “broken promise” as political detractors have attempted reveals a total disregard for the mechanics of modern economic governance. Responsible leadership understands that large-scale infrastructure of this magnitude requires meticulous pre-construction phases, including bathymetric surveys, environmental and social impact assessments, regulatory clearances from the Nigeria Ports Authority (NPA) and Federal Ministry of Transportation, and complex financial structuring before physical groundbreaking.

Governor Abiodun’s firm, systematic execution of the seaport agreement, from the initial Memorandum of Understanding to the final investment agreement witnessed by the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, proves his capacity to structure and deliver mega-projects that bring generational prosperity.

This is governance at its most strategic, where patience in preparation guarantees permanence in performance.

Further cementing Ogun East as Nigeria’s preferred industrial destination is the upcoming 450-hectare ultra-modern industrial park by the Lee Group conglomerate, situated along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway near the Sagamu Interchange. Scheduled for its official groundbreaking ceremony on Thursday, November 12, 2026, by Governor Dapo Abiodun, this massive complex will house 29 multi-sector manufacturing factories alongside world-class commercial, hospitality, and recreational facilities.

It is, in essence, a self-contained industrial city. The industrial park is set to produce a wide range of goods including footwear, leather products, plastics, packaging materials, personal care items, and household goods, driving localized manufacturing, expanding supply chains, reducing import dependence, and creating thousands of direct jobs for youth across Sagamu, Remoland, Ikenne, and the wider Ogun East corridor.

Its strategic proximity to major transportation arteries, the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, the Sagamu-Benin Expressway, and the Gateway International Airport, guarantees seamless distribution across Nigerian consumer markets and the West African sub-region under the African Continental Free Trade Area framework.

Rather than relying on mere policy announcements, Governor Abiodun has consistently created an environment conducive to private-sector investment through quiet but impactful reforms such as the Ogun State Investment Promotion Agency, the automation of Certificates of Occupancy (CofO), the establishment of the Ogun State Business Environment Council, and the stable power supply framework via the Ogun State Light Up Project.

The entry of multinational conglomerates like Lee Group, Arise Integrated Industrial Platform, and others reinforces the state’s status as a manufacturing titan, proving that Ogun East under Abiodun’s stewardship possesses the regulatory stability, infrastructure, and institutional support required to attract and retain global capital.

Economic growth under Governor Abiodun has not been limited to heavy manufacturing and maritime logistics; it has actively reached micro, small, and medium-scale enterprises at the grassroots level, ensuring prosperity is democratized. Recognizing MSMEs as the backbone of local commerce, which employs over 70 percent of the district’s workforce, the Abiodun administration launched a targeted ₦1 billion small business operational support fund to empower small business owners across all 20 Local Government Areas, including all nine LGAs in Ogun East.

Through direct operational grants disbursed in structured phases and devoid of political patronage, thousands of small business owners ranging from market traders in Ijebu-Ode, boutique operators in Sagamu, beauty artisans in Ijebu-Igbo, to small-scale agricultural processors in Ago-Iwoye and Ogun Waterside have received capital injections of between ₦100,000 and ₦500,000.

This programme has alleviated financial stress, shielded vulnerable businesses from macroeconomic shocks, reduced dependence on high-interest commercial loans from microfinance banks, and stimulated micro-level economic activity.

Beneficiaries have been verified through their trade associations and cooperatives, ensuring transparency and accountability.

By pairing grand industrial infrastructure with direct economic support for small business owners, Governor Abiodun has proven that his administration’s growth model is inclusive, equitable, and designed to lift citizens across every economic stratum. It is a dual-track strategy that works: big capital for big industry, small capital for small enterprise.

A core argument for Governor Abiodun’s senatorial candidacy is his unprecedented road and infrastructure intervention record across the nine Local Government Areas of Ogun East. Since 2019, his administration has constructed and rehabilitated over 243.3 kilometers of roads in the district as part of a statewide network exceeding 1,600 kilometers, the largest road infrastructure intervention by any administration in the history of Ogun State. Critical transport links that had suffered decades of neglect have been transformed into modern arterial corridors. They include the 14km Ijebu-Ode–Mojoda–Epe Road, a vital dual-carriage commercial gateway linking Ogun East directly to Lagos State, reducing travel time from over 90 minutes to less than 45 minutes and boosting cross-border trade, and the Sagamu–Iperu–Ode–Sapaade Road, which serves as a crucial corridor unlocking economic activity across Remoland and hosting the new airport.

Other pivotal developments include the Ejirin–Idowa–Ibefun–Itokin Road in Odogbolu which opens up the rice-producing belt, the iconic Tam Balogun Road in Ijebu-Ode, the Imodi–Imosan Road, and the newly approved J4–Ogbogbo–Ibu–Gao Road in Ogun Waterside to open up agricultural and coastal hinterlands previously cut off during the rainy season. These road networks are complemented by strategic multi-modal assets, led by the flagship Gateway International Airport at Iperu-Remo.

Designed to handle regional freight, passenger traffic, and agricultural exports, the airport which has already secured its aerodrome certification integrates seamlessly with proposed logistics hubs such as the conversion of Ogere Trailer Park into a modern dry port and cargo sorting facility, establishing Ogun East as a key distribution and export node in West Africa.

In addition to physical transport infrastructure, the administration has delivered over 150 renovated primary school classroom blocks under the Ogun State Universal Basic Education programme, modernized over 80 primary healthcare centres across all wards in Ogun East to reduce maternal mortality, and spearheaded sustainable urban planning initiatives to ensure industrial growth does not compromise environmental health.

The role of a Senator requires more than regional popularity or populist slogans; it demands an individual with national influence, policy expertise, a deep understanding of economic development, legislative drafting capacity, and an established ability to collaborate with federal authorities and international partners.

Governor Dapo Abiodun has repeatedly demonstrated these qualities. His ability to secure federal alignment with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration has already attracted strategic national assets to Ogun State, from the inclusion of Ogun in the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones programme to the siting of federal technical institutions and road interventions.

As Ogun East prepares to capitalize on its expanding industrial zones, energy prospects, cargo airport, and coastal trade, it needs a representative in the Senate who can draft effective legislation to protect its special economic zones, attract federal funding for its coastal infrastructure, and defend the district’s commercial interests at the highest level against competing interests.

His experience as a former Chairman of the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC), his private sector background as a boardroom guru who built one of Nigeria’s most successful oil and gas conglomerates, and his calm, methodical approach to governance provide the perfect temperament for the Senate, a chamber that rewards wisdom over noise and strategy over sentiment.

Supporting Prince Dapo Abiodun’s senatorial ambition is therefore not merely an electoral choice. It is a strategic decision to consolidate years of unprecedented development, safeguard multi-billion-dollar investments already in the pipeline, and secure a prosperous future for the people of Ogun East.

In the final analysis, the choice before Ogun East in 2027 transcends party loyalty and sentimental affiliations; it is a choice between continuity and reversal, between consolidating a proven developmental momentum and gambling with untested rhetoric.

Prince Dapo Abiodun represents that rare blend of executive competence, private sector ingenuity, and national access that the Senate demands. He has not only built roads, airports, and industrial parks, he has built confidence — confidence that Ogun East can compete, lead, and prosper in a fiercely competitive federation. To elevate him to the Senate is to protect the investments already made, to guarantee that the Gateway Deep Seaport, the Agro-Cargo Airport, and the sprawling industrial corridors do not become abandoned dreams. It is a vote to secure the future, to ensure that the prosperity started under his governorship finds its fullest expression in law, policy, and federal representation.

*Ogbonnikan is a Senior Special Assistant (SSA) on Media to Ogun State Governor

World.title: UNODC: Africa Must Close Gap Between Evidence Generated on Substance Use, Policy Decisions
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) has said that Africa must close the gap between evidence generated on substance use and the decisions made by governments, warning that the disconnect has serious policy and human consequences.

The UNODC Country Representative in Nigeria, Dr. Akanidomo Ibanga, stated this on Wednesday in Abuja at the 16th Biennial International Conference on ‘Drugs, Alcohol and Society in Africa,’ organised by the Centre for Research and Information on Substance Abuse (CRISA) in partnership with the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

The two-day event was themed: ‘Substance Use Research and Data Systems in Africa; Advances, Relevance and Challenges.’

He questioned the value of research that does not influence decisions, data that is never used, and policies not informed by evidence, saying they are questions about lives, government priorities and the future of substance use response in Africa.

Akanidomo noted: “Africa does not lack researchers. We do not lack expertise. We do not lack institutions capable of generating knowledge. What we must continue to confront is the gap between the evidence we generate and the decisions we make.

“And that gap has consequences. When we do not know who is using which substances, where the greatest risks are emerging, who is being left behind, or whether our interventions are working, we are not simply dealing with a data problem.

“We are dealing with a policy problem, a public health problem and, ultimately, a human problem.”

Akanidomo maintained that the relevance of substance use research should not be measured by the number of surveys conducted or reports published, but by what changes because of it, including whether it helps governments allocate resources, identify underserved populations, reveal effectiveness of prevention programmes, and improve access to treatment.

According to him, research must not end when a report is launched. That is often where its most important work should begin. That evidence must reach decision-makers, service institutions, affected communities and professionals.

Akanidomo, therefore, called for reliable national data that reflects African contexts, saying Nigeria and other African countries must not be invisible in the global evidence base and should not have to make critical decisions using evidence that does not reflect their populations.

Also, the Commissioner for Human Development and Social Affairs, ECOWAS Commission, Prof. Nassirou Bako-Arifari, lamented that West Africa was shifting from being merely a transit hub for illicit drugs to becoming a growing consumer market, with serious socio-economic, public health and security implications.

Bako-Arifari, who was represented by the Head of ECOWAS Drug Prevention and Control Division, Dr. Daniel Amankwaah, said drug abuse, illicit trafficking and related crimes constitute severe challenges across several nations, including ECOWAS member states.

He cited the recently validated West African Epidemiology Network on Drug Use (WENDU) Report (2025) which underscored growing public health concerns associated with substance use in the region.

Bako-Arifari added: “Key highlights of the WENDU report – which will be presented shortly – indicate that West Africa is shifting from being merely a transit hub to becoming a growing consumer market.”

He pointed out that the changing dynamics demand enhanced international cooperation, improved treatment infrastructure and effective alternatives to incarceration.

To this end, he said the ECOWAS drug prevention and control programme continued to prioritize expansion of drug treatment and rehabilitation centres across member states.

“As of September 2026, 12 drug treatment and rehabilitation centres in 10 member states have completed renovations and received essential equipment upgrades to improve access to care for people with drug use disorders,” he said.

Bako-Arifari said that over 300 health and allied professionals have been trained as master trainers in their respective countries to champion evidence-based substance abuse prevention and treatment.

According to him, the initiatives reflect a deliberate strategic shift by the commission – moving away from a purely punitive response towards a compassionate, rehabilitative approach.

Bako-Arifari explained that another vital area of progress is the advancement of Alternatives to Incarceration (ATI), noting that traditional punitive measures often fail to address root causes of substance abuse.

“In line with this global best practice, ECOWAS has made significant strides since 2024 by advancing ATI frameworks that prioritize treatment, rehabilitation, and social reintegration. Through targeted pilot projects, ATI training has been successfully implemented in Ghana, Togo, Lagos and the Republic of Benin,” he said.

Bako-Arifari was of the opinion that emerging drug threats do not replace older ones but compound them, adding that while ECOWAS continues to combat cocaine trafficking, the escalating crisis surrounding synthetic opioids – particularly tramadol – requires member states to tackle multiple overlapping threats simultaneously.

He stressed that the ECOWAS Commission recognised the necessity of a balanced approach that addresses both illicit drug supply reduction and the public health and social consequences of substance use.

World.title: Fasoranti’s Death, a Loss to Yoruba Nation, Says Edu-Falade
World.content:
Tomisin Edu-Falade, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Akure North Constituency in the Ondo State House of Assembly, has described the death of Afenifere elder statesman, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, as a painful loss.

Edu-Falade expressed her condolences to the late statesman’s family and the Ondo State Government over his demise.

She said the death of the revered Yoruba leader was a moment of grief for his family, the people of Ondo State and the Yoruba nation.

The APC candidate extended her sympathy to the bereaved family, urging them to find solace in the life of the departed elder statesman.

She also commiserated with the Ondo State Government, expressing solidarity with it over the loss.

Edu-Falade acknowledged Fasoranti’s significance as an elder statesman and a prominent figure in Yoruba affairs.

“We mourn the passing of Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti and extend our heartfelt condolences to his family and the Ondo State Government,” she said.

She prayed that God would grant the bereaved family and the government the strength to endure the period of mourning.

Edu-Falade also prayed for the repose of the late statesman’s soul and comfort for all those grieving his death.

World.title: SWAGA’23 Mourns Fasoranti
World.content:
The South-West Agenda for Asiwaju (SWAGA’23) has mourned the death of the National Leader of Afenifere, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, describing him as a towering figure in Nigeria’s political history and a custodian of the progressive ideals of the Yoruba people.

In a condolence statement signed by its chairman, Senator Dayo Adeyeye, the group expressed deep sadness over the passing of the elder statesman, who died at the age of 100.

SWAGA’23 described Fasoranti as a teacher, educationist, former Commissioner for Finance of the old Ondo State, and a committed disciple of the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo.

The group also praised his contributions to Nigeria’s democratic development, noting that he remained a fearless pro-democracy activist who stood firmly for truth, justice and good governance during some of the country’s most challenging periods.

According to the statement, Fasoranti’s life was marked by sacrifice, integrity and selfless service, spanning his involvement in the Action Group, the Unity Party of Nigeria and his leadership role in Afenifere.

It said the late Yoruba leader consistently championed true federalism, social justice, good governance and national unity, adding that he risked his life in the struggle for the democracy Nigerians enjoy today.

SWAGA’23 also recalled Fasoranti’s support for the group during the build-up to the 2023 general elections, particularly his endorsement of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s presidential ambition.

The statement said Fasoranti received members of the group in Akure and offered his blessing, prayers and endorsement at a critical point in their political mobilisation.

“His gesture gave SWAGA’23 strength, legitimacy and confidence, and remains one of the defining moments in our movement,” the group said.

The organisation described his death as a major loss not only to his immediate family, the people of Akure, Ondo State and Afenifere, but also to the Yoruba race and Nigeria as a whole.

It further characterised Fasoranti as one of the last great figures of the Awoist tradition and a bridge between Nigeria’s First Republic and Fourth Republic.

Adeyeye, on behalf of the leadership and members of SWAGA’23 across the South-West and Nigeria, extended condolences to the deceased’s family, Afenifere, and the government and people of Ondo State.

The group prayed for the repose of Fasoranti’s soul and for divine comfort for all those mourning him, expressing hope that his legacy would endure.

“May his legacy live on forever,” the statement added

World.title: Sunbeth Activates N150b Commercial Paper Note Issuance Process
World.content:
Sunbeth Global Concepts Limited (Sunbeth) has signed the transaction documents for its N150 billion Commercial Paper note, the first series under its approved N500 billion Commercial Paper Issuance Programme.

The transaction will provide short-term working capital for Sunbeth’s cocoa procurement activities during the 2026/2027 cocoa season.

It will also support inventory requirements for the company’s 70,000-metric-tonne-per-annum processing facility, which is scheduled to commence operations in the first quarter of next year.

Speaking at the signing ceremony in Victoria Island, Lagos, Chief Financial Officer of Sunbeth Global Concepts, Adeyemi Aduwo, explained that the transaction would provide timely funding for the company’s procurement activities and broader processing ambitions.

“The 2026/2027 cocoa season presents a critical procurement window, and this transaction gives us the working capital to respond efficiently to that opportunity, supporting our transition towards greater value addition.”

Sunbeth has established a track record in the domestic debt capital market following the successful redemption of its debut Commercial Paper issuance, in which the first tranche was oversubscribed by 65 per cent.

The new N500 billion programme provides a structured framework for the company to access short-term funding in line with its seasonal working capital requirements.

The first tranche of N150 billion saw keen investor activity with an oversubscription of 45 per cent, further demonstrating Nigeria’s capital markets’ ability to provide sustainable financing models for productive activity in the agricultural sector.

Through the issuance, Sunbeth continues to strengthen its integrated agricultural platform, spanning sourcing, aggregation, and international trade, while advancing its plans to increase value creation within Africa’s agricultural economy.

The Commercial Paper issued in three series, with a minimum bid of N5 million and tenors of 180, 270, and 364 days. The timing and size of each tranche will align with cocoa procurement requirements and prevailing market conditions.

Sunbeth maintains national-scale credit ratings from established African rating agencies, with long-term ratings ranging from BBB to BBB+ and a short-term rating of A2.

World.title: UNICEF Seeks Curriculum Review to Bridge Graduate Skills Gap
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) Tuesday called for a review of Nigeria’s education curriculum to address the mismatch between graduates’ skills and labour market demands, stressing the need to equip young people with relevant digital and vocational skills.

The UNICEF Deputy Representative in Nigeria, Dr. Rownak Khan, made the call during a visit by UNICEF and Airtel Africa to schools in Agege, Lagos and Yaba College of Technology (YABATECH), to showcase their digital learning and youth skills development initiatives.

She emphasised the impact of the organisation’s partnership with Airtel and educational institutions on youth skills development.

Khan said although Nigeria had an established education system, much of its curriculum was outdated and failed to adequately prepare young people for the realities of the modern workplace.

“In many countries, and to some extent broadly in Nigeria, the education is there, but the curricula that have been followed are quite decades old. When these children come out into the real world, they are in shock because there is a mismatch between what they have learnt and what the market is asking for,” she said.

The UNICEF deputy representative stressed the need for stakeholders to work together to bridge the gap between classroom learning and industry requirements, noting that digital skills development should be linked to sustainable livelihood opportunities for young people.

According to her, the collaboration between UNICEF, Airtel and educational institutions demonstrates how partnerships can combine different areas of expertise to provide more comprehensive support for young people.

Khan described the initiative as a flagship programme, noting that its impact extended beyond digital training to preparing beneficiaries for employment and other livelihood opportunities.

She commended Yabatech for its commitment to skills development, particularly its efforts to integrate digital competencies into its programmes and provide young people with pathways to economic independence.

In her remarks, the Chief Field Office and Head of Private Sector Partnerships Unit, Celine Lafoucriere, said the telecommunications company had supported the organisation’s digital education initiatives for five years by providing connectivity to young people seeking to acquire digital skills.

The partnership, she noted, had enabled beneficiaries to access various learning platforms, including the Learning Passport and the Youth Agency Marketplace (YOMA), which provide opportunities for young people to develop skills and improve their employability.

Lafoucriere explained that UNICEF worked with different partners, each contributing expertise and resources to expand access to digital education.

She said Airtel’s contribution had been particularly significant in ensuring that young people could access skills development programmes provided through UNICEF’s network of partners.

According to her, Airtel initially focused on supporting access to the Learning Passport when it entered into a pan-African partnership with UNICEF.

However, discussions between both organisations led to the expansion of the initiative to cover other digital platforms that could benefit children, adolescents and young people.

She said Airtel subsequently agreed to whitelist the platforms, allowing beneficiaries to access the digital learning resources without the usual data constraints.

The UNICEF official expressed appreciation to the telecommunications company for its continued support, noting that the partnership had helped strengthen digital learning opportunities in Nigeria.

“The only reason why we are able to drive digital learning in Nigeria today is thanks to Airtel,” Lafoucriere stated.

She added that sustained collaboration among development organisations, technology companies and other stakeholders remained essential to ensuring that children and young people were not left behind in the digital learning ecosystem.

Also speaking, Head, Programmes, Airtel Africa Foundation, Esi Asare Prah, reaffirmed its commitment to bridging the digital divide across Africa, announcing plans to strengthen skills development initiatives aimed at equipping young people with competencies required in the labour market.

She stated that its partnership with UNICEF, backed by a $57 million investment across 13 African countries, was designed to expand access to digital education and skills training, particularly for young people who lack the opportunities to participate in the digital economy.

She added that the initiative was particularly significant in Nigeria because of its emphasis on equipping young people with practical skills they could use to secure employment and earn a living.

According to her, “Many young people graduated from schools with certificates but lacked the competencies required by employers, creating a mismatch between educational qualifications and labour market demands.”

The foundation, Prah noted, has four priority areas, with education occupying the foremost position, followed by digital inclusion.

She stated that the partnership with UNICEF remained a key part of the foundation’s commitment to addressing educational inequalities and expanding opportunities for young people across the continent.

“Our mission is to bridge that digital divide across the continent because our mother company drives the digital education agenda, and there are still a lot of young people who are left behind in that regard,” she said.

Prah also described its engagement with YABATECH as an opportunity to develop a model that could be adapted and replicated in other African countries where it operates.

“Nigerian initiative stood out because of its focus on practical skills development, supported by technical expertise to ensure that participants acquired competencies relevant to the needs of employers,” she said, adding that the approach went beyond providing access to digital learning platforms or offering training.

She stressed the importance of ensuring that the skills acquired could translate into employment and sustainable livelihoods.

The Rector of YABATECH, Dr. Ibraheem Abdul, represented by his deputy, Dr. Ismaila Badmus, said the institution was deliberate about building partnerships and strengthening town-and-gown relations.

He expressed appreciation to the partners for their support.

World.title: Movement Defends Tinubu’s  Reforms amid Hardship
World.content:
Amina Hassan in Abuja

Ahead of the 2027 general election, a group, Tinubu Must Stay Movement (TMS), has defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms amid persistent economic hardship in the country, urging Nigerians to focus on their projected long-term benefits.

The group’s Director-General, Marcel Ngogbehei, while addressing a press conference yesterday in Abuja, argued that abandoning the reforms without fixing the country’s longstanding economic challenges could leave future generations worse off.

Ngogbehei, who likened the situation to a family making sacrifices to secure its future, said Nigerians should be willing to make adjustments for the sake of their children.

He acknowledged the difficulties facing households, saying public debate should focus on the merits of government policies and possible alternatives rather than personal attacks. The director-general challenged critics to explain how they would have handled the country’s economic challenges differently.

Ngogbehei said: “Would you prefer to eat everything you have now, not caring what happens to your kids in the future? We cannot run it by propaganda, we cannot run it by lies.”

Also, the National Coordinator of the group, Ibrahim Uba, reeled out what he described as progress recorded by the administration across sectors, including economy, education, agriculture, security and infrastructure.

He noted that the economy had grown by about 4.43 per cent and claimed food prices had fallen.

Uba cited 1.5 million approvals by the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), a reported N500 billion allocation to the Bank of Agriculture to support farmers, and the absence of strikes in tertiary institutions since President Tinubu assumed office.

He further pointed to the procurement of military equipment, deployment of digital systems for security agencies and ongoing road projects as evidence of progress.

Uba urged journalists to independently investigate the government’s programmes and examine how the interventions were being implemented.

World.title: Hyron Andrews’s wife breaks silence: ‘Unimaginable pain’
World.content:
Hyron Andrews’s American wife, Maighlin, has broken her silence following his shock death last Friday. Her emotional comments come as the Lions player’s cause of death has been officially released.

The couple wed in 2022 and have welcomed two sons since.

HYRON ANDREWS’S WIFE BREAKS SILENCE

On her Facebook account, Hyron Andrews’s wife, Maighlin, posted a tribute to the late Lions player who collapsed and died last Friday in France ahead of the team’s game against La Rochelle.



Maighlin, a US citizen, shared: “I’m not sure if there will ever be enough words to describe how much you mean to me, our boys, and your family, friends, and teammates all over the world. You were the absolute BEST father, and they were your everything. I know your proudest achievement was our family.

“I’m so so grateful that we got to have you for the time we did, though the pain of having our time cut short is unlike anything I thought was possible. We had so many plans, so much life left to live, and so many things to experience. I feel so blessed for all we got to do together in our short time.

Maighlin recalled meeting Hyron Andrews in Durban a decade ago, when he was playing for the Sharks, and she was studying in South Africa as part of a university exchange programme.



The couple would endure a six-year-long distance relationship before finally getting engaged in Ireland in 2021.

Maighlin moved to Durban in 2022, and the couple wed in Michigan in the US the following year.

They then briefly moved to England, where Hyron played for the Sale Sharks, before returning to South Africa for the last few months playing for the Lions.



Maighlin went on to praise her late husband for his kindness and compassion, even to strangers.

She added, “I pray that God guides us through this unimaginable time.

“I pray that I can raise these boys to be good men like you. I pray that you passed peacefully and knew how much you were adored, and your final thoughts were of your family. I pray that you always look over us and protect us. 

“The devastation is beyond words, but the overwhelming love, support, and kindness we have received is incredible! I could write a million words and post a thousand pictures, but it would never be enough. I love you, I miss you. I’m lost without you. Rest easy, my love”.

CAUSE OF DEATH REVEALED

On Wednesday, 21 October, the Lions announced Hyron Andrews’ cause of death following an autopsy conducted by French authorities.

According to the report, the 31-year-old’s death was caused by an aortic dissection. Thi dissection most likely occurred on an aortic aneurysm.



French authorities described the medical incident as “a tear in the aorta, due to natural causes, which led to a significant accumulation of blood within the sac surrounding the heart.”

World.title: Triple murder suspect Tshuma ‘not eating or sleeping well’, court hears
World.content:
Triple murder suspect Ndodana Tshuma has reportedly been struggling to eat and sleep, prompting his lawyer to request a specialist medical assessment during his appearance at the Johannesburg Magistrate’s Court.

According to reports from the court proceedings on Wednesday, 21 October, Tshuma’s lawyer, Chrispin Machingura, raised concerns about his client’s condition as the defence and state attempted to resolve outstanding issues surrounding a plea and sentencing agreement.

The proceedings took a turn when Tshuma reportedly told the court that he could not remember pleading guilty or signing the document presented to him.



The case was postponed to 29 October to allow further consultations between Tshuma and his legal representative, SABC News reported.

lawyer requests sApecialist assessment

Machingura reportedly told the court that his client had not been eating and sleeping well. He requested that Tshuma be examined by a specialist for a medical assessment.

The request came as the defence sought to clarify Tshuma’s position on the plea agreement, which had been expected to be finalised during Wednesday’s proceedings.



According to the reports, Tshuma maintained that he was innocent and said he could not remember pleading guilty. When his lawyer showed him the document he had signed, he reportedly said he could not recall signing it.

The development raised further questions about whether the outstanding plea and sentencing arrangements could proceed as planned.

The court granted a postponement to allow the defence more time to consult with Tshuma.



His reported difficulties sleeping and eating should not, however, be taken as a medical diagnosis, and the request for an assessment does not establish that he has a particular condition.

Why Tshuma is appearing in court

Tshuma, a British national of Zimbabwean descent, is wanted in the United Kingdom in connection with the alleged murders of his wife, Zandile, and their two daughters, Natalie and Nala.

He was arrested in Johannesburg in July following an international manhunt.



South African proceedings include charges relating to unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition, as well as contraventions of the Immigration Act.

Tshuma had previously pleaded guilty to firearm-related and immigration offences in South Africa, with the state and defence working towards a plea and sentencing agreement.

However, outstanding documentation and discrepancies delayed the finalisation of the agreement.



His South African criminal proceedings are separate from the extradition process through which British authorities are seeking his return to face the murder allegations.

The next court appearance on 29 October is expected to allow further consultations between Tshuma and his lawyer as the local proceedings continue.

World.title: SAPS wants YOU: Applications open for 5 500 trainees
World.content:
The South African Police Service (SAPS) has opened applications for 5 500 entry-level police trainee positions for the 2026/2027 financial year.

This is an opportunity for the youth of South Africa to pursue a career in law enforcement.

SAPS opened the recruitment on Wednesday, 21 October and applications officially close on 13 November.



South Africans between the ages of 18-35 are encouraged to apply, with a particular emphasis on those who are fit, disciplined and committed to serving their communities.

Colonel Amanda van Wyk, the National SAPS spokesperson, said the recruitment drive aims to attract young people that are passionate about making a difference and contributing to a safer South Africa.

HOW TO APPLY

If you’re interested in applying, you can do so on the official SAPS recruitment portal here.

Applicants are required to create a profile and verify their account. Once the account has been verified, the applicant needs to follow the step-by-step application process to apply for the positions.

Applicants must not have a previous criminal record or a pending criminal case.

Graduates are encouraged to apply.



“Graduates in Law, Policing, Criminology, Law Enforcement, Forensic Investigation and Information Technology may be considered for placement within the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (DPCI), also known as the Hawks; Detective and Forensic Services; and Crime Intelligence,” said Van Wyk.

“The targeted recruitment process will also seek to identify suitably qualified young people from underrepresented racial groups who meet the prescribed requirements.”

SAPS warns against recruitment scams

SAPS also emphasised applications are completely free and warned candidates against individuals demanding money in exchange for employment or promising to influence the recruitment process.

Prospective applicants are encouraged to apply early and use only official SAPS recruitment channels.

During the academy institution phase, all trainees receive a monthly stipend of R5 000.

Upon completing basic training and advancing to the probation phase as permanent constables, officers receive a starting salary of R248 175 per annum alongside standard public service benefits.

During the previous recruitment drive closing in July 2025, SAPS received 1 021 563 applications for 5 500 roles, including 334 765 tertiary graduates, highlighting severe youth unemployment in South Africa.

World.title: Thinking of adopting a rescue dog? Here’s what it really costs in South Africa
World.content:
Adoption fees at most South African SPCAs range from about R900 to R1,400. Image: Pexels

Deciding to adopt a rescue dog is one of the most rewarding choices a family can make.

But the adoption fee is only the start.

Food, vet visits and flea treatment all add up.



And for first-time owners, those ongoing costs can come as a surprise.

Here’s what it really costs: adoption fees at most South African SPCAs and animal welfare organisations range from about R900 to R1,400, and usually include sterilisation, a first vaccination and a microchip.

After that, you’ll need to budget for food, regular vaccinations, parasite control and vet visits.

HOW MUCH ARE ADOPTION FEES?

Fees vary between organisations and regions. Here are some examples of published adoption fees for dogs:

Bloemfontein SPCA: R1,400

R1,400 Animal Anti-Cruelty League, Johannesburg: R1,240

R1,240 SPCA Randburg: R1,000 for adult dogs, and R1,100 for puppies under six months

R1,000 for adult dogs, and R1,100 for puppies under six months Animal Anti-Cruelty League, Cape Town: R1,000

R1,000 Vereeniging SPCA: R900, including a non-refundable R100 administration fee

WHAT DOES THE ADOPTION FEE INCLUDE?

You’re not paying for the animal itself.

According to the Vereeniging SPCA, the fee covers the expenses the SPCA has already paid, such as sterilisation, the first vaccination, deworming, an ID disc and a microchip.



Some organisations also include flea treatment or a collar.

The Durban and Coast SPCA says the adoption fee is heavily subsidised, and that the cost of vaccinations alone at a private vet is more than its fee.

WHY ADOPTING IS GOOD VALUE

Sterilisation is one of the biggest savings.

At a private vet, sterilisation can cost between R2,500 and R3,500 for a female dog, and between R1,800 and R2,500 for a male dog, according to industry estimates.

Since most adoption fees include sterilisation, adopting can save you more than the fee itself.

OTHER ONCE-OFF COSTS

Some organisations charge extra for:

Home inspections. The Animal Anti-Cruelty League in Johannesburg charges R88 for inspections within 40km of Johannesburg.

The Animal Anti-Cruelty League in Johannesburg charges for inspections within 40km of Johannesburg. Additional vaccinations, if your dog needs more than one at adoption.

You’ll also need to buy basics, such as a bed, bowls, a lead and toys.

ONGOING COSTS TO BUDGET FOR

Once your dog is home, you’ll need to budget for:

Food, which depends on your dog’s size, age and diet.

which depends on your dog’s size, age and diet. Booster vaccinations, usually once a year.

usually once a year. Deworming and flea and tick treatment, which need to be repeated regularly.

which need to be repeated regularly. Vet visits, for check-ups and unexpected illness or injuries.

for check-ups and unexpected illness or injuries. Grooming, especially for long-haired breeds.

TIPS TO KEEP COSTS DOWN

Ask your SPCA about low-cost services. Some SPCAs offer vaccinations, deworming and sterilisation at lower prices than private vets. The Bloemfontein SPCA, for example, lists sterilisation at R900 for a female dog and R600 for a male.

for unexpected vet bills. Consider pet insurance, and compare policies carefully.

and compare policies carefully. Buy food in bulk to save money over time.

BEFORE YOU ADOPT

Most organisations require:

a copy of your ID ,

, proof of residence ,

, proof that pets are allowed, if you rent,

and a home inspection.

Some also ask for a meet-and-greet with your family and any dogs you already have.

World.title: Medium-term budget in a nutshell: Everything to know in 30 seconds
World.content:
Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana announced temporary fuel levy cuts, billions in additional funding for social services and new resources to fight crime. Image: X @GovernmentZA

Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana has announced temporary fuel levy cuts, billions in additional funding for social services and municipalities, and new resources to fight crime as government seeks to ease pressure on households while stabilising South Africa’s public finances.

Delivering the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement (MTBPS) in Parliament on Wednesday, 21 October, Godongwana said the government’s fiscal consolidation measures were beginning to deliver results, despite weaker economic growth and ongoing global uncertainty.

“The difficult choices of the past few years were made for a purpose. To restore stability today so that we can build a faster-growing, more inclusive and more resilient economy tomorrow,” he said.



However, South Africa’s economic growth forecast for 2026 has been revised down to 1.2%, from the 1.6% projected in February, reflecting pressure from higher fuel prices, geopolitical conflict and the effects of El Niño.

Growth is expected to improve to 1.6% in 2027 and reach 2% by 2029.

Tax revenue boost helps turn debt tide

One of the key developments is the improvement in government’s debt trajectory.



The debt-to-GDP ratio stabilised at 78.4% in the 2025/26 financial year and has started to decline, marking a milestone after years of rising public debt.

The budget deficit is expected to narrow to 3.9% of GDP in the current financial year, better than the 4% forecast in February. It is projected to decline further to 2.5% by 2030.

Meanwhile, the primary budget surplus – the difference between government revenue and expenditure before debt-service costs – is expected to rise from 1.7% of GDP to nearly 3% by 2030.



Tax revenue estimates for 2026/27 have been revised upwards by R17.1 billion, supported by corporate income tax, VAT and stronger commodity prices.

Government expenditure is expected to increase from R2.7 trillion this year to R3 trillion by 2029/30.

The improved revenue outlook gives Treasury some room to provide targeted relief, although the government remains focused on containing borrowing and keeping debt on a sustainable path.



Fuel levy cuts offer temporary relief

One of the most immediate announcements for consumers was a temporary reduction in the general fuel levy worth R10 billion.

From 4 November to 1 December 2026, the levy will be reduced by:

Petrol: R1.50 per litre

R1.50 per litre Diesel: R3 per litre

The second phase will run from 2 December 2026 until 5 January 2027, with smaller reductions:



Petrol: R1 per litre

R1 per litre Diesel: R1.50 per litre

The funding will come from R10 billion in revenue overruns from the 2025/26 financial year that had been transferred to the Central Energy Fund. The money will be returned to the National Revenue Fund to finance the relief.

“This intervention will help ease cost of living pressures without compromising the sustainability of the budget,” Godongwana said.

The reductions are intended to cushion motorists and businesses against elevated fuel costs. Lower fuel levies can also help moderate transport and distribution expenses, although the final pump price will still depend on other fuel-pricing components.



Social grants and child nutrition receive support

Social spending remains a major part of the government’s budget, accounting for 60% of non-interest expenditure.

Government funding supports 18.1 million social grant beneficiaries through programmes including old-age, disability and child support grants.

More than 11 million households also benefit from free basic services, including water, electricity, sanitation and refuse removal.



The MTBPS includes R1.6 billion over the medium term for child nutrition, with a focus on maternal care and the first 1 000 days of a child’s life. The programme aims to help prevent malnutrition and stunting during a critical period of development.

Billions allocated to fight crime and GBVF

Government has reprioritised R3.8 billion over the 2027 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework period to appoint 3 552 social workers, strengthening the response to gender-based violence and femicide (GBVF).

A further R186 million has been allocated to improve forensic and investigative capacity.



Godongwana also announced plans to increase the number of sexual offences courts from 55 to 101 and expand Thuthuzela Care Centres supporting rape survivors from 72 to 80 by 2028/29.

An additional R157.4 million will go to the Department of Women, Youth and Persons with Disabilities to strengthen national coordination of the GBVF response.

Beyond gender-based violence, R810 million has been allocated to recapitalise the South African Police Service vehicle fleet. A further R823 million has been set aside for military deployments targeting gang violence and illegal mining.



The allocations are intended to strengthen law enforcement and improve support for vulnerable communities.

HIV and AIDS services get additional funding

The budget also addresses the financial pressure on HIV and AIDS programmes following the withdrawal of funding from the United States President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR).

Government will reprioritise R556.7 million over the medium term to sustain HIV and AIDS services. This will supplement R3.8 billion reprioritised through the district health programmes grant.



The funding is intended to help maintain essential services as South Africa adjusts to the loss of external support.

Municipalities receive billions for basic services

Local government is also set to receive additional support.

Municipalities will receive an additional R3.5 billion over the medium term for smart meter rollouts, aimed at improving billing accuracy and helping municipalities manage electricity distribution.



The local government equitable share will receive a further R21.8 billion to support basic services.

Godongwana stressed that funding must translate into visible improvements for residents, including more reliable services and better municipal management.

The challenge will be ensuring that the additional allocations result in practical improvements on the ground.



New digital platform planned for government services

Government also plans to spend R150 million developing the MyMzansi app, a digital platform intended to give citizens access to government services through their smartphones.

The initiative forms part of efforts to improve access to public services through digital channels.

Its impact will depend on how effectively the platform is implemented and whether people can access the services they need through it.



What the MTBPS means for South Africans

The 2026 MTBPS presents a balancing act for government.

Stronger tax revenue and a stabilising debt trajectory offer some encouragement, while the temporary fuel levy cuts provide immediate assistance to households and businesses facing high costs.

At the same time, billions have been directed towards social workers, crime prevention, health services, child nutrition and municipal infrastructure.



However, the downgraded growth forecast highlights the scale of the economic challenge. Sustained improvements in employment, investment and household living standards will depend on whether fiscal stability can be translated into stronger economic growth and better public services.

For now, motorists can look towards temporary fuel relief from November, while the longer-term test will be whether government can maintain its fiscal gains and deliver tangible improvements for South Africans.

World.title: 'Not on the fence' - ActionSA sets three non-negotiables for coalition partners
World.content:
JOAHNNESBURG - With just two weeks left until South Africans head to the polls, ActionSA has made its stance on coalition crystal clear.

Its leader and Johannesburg mayoral candidate, Herman Mashaba laid down three non-negotiable conditions for any potential coalition partners.

The first is a zero-tolerance approach to corruption, with Mashaba warning that nobody should be shielded from accountability.

“When Herman Mashaba steals a cent of public money, don't protect him because be assured, Herman Mashaba is not going to protect you. Secondly, we have a constitutional obligation as government to provide public services to all residents,” he said.

The second condition is that ActionSA highlighted the importance of constitutional obligation as a government to provide public services to all residents.

READ | IEC receives more than 700 complaints over election-related content

And finally, Mashaba said potential coalition partners must agree that undocumented foreign nationals are not welcomed in municipalities governed by Actions, either alone or in coalition.

“Action SA is happy to remain on their benches because if we enter into an agreement with you before resolving these three issues, we know that coalition is going to collapse. Therefore, we'd rather be on the opposition benches.”

Mashaba affirmed that the only time they will consider coalitions is after the elections.

World.title: Number Of The Day | R10 billion | 21 October 2026
World.content:
Cheaper Fuel Is A Reprieve. Why South Africa Needs More Than Temporary Relief

For South African households already struggling with rising living costs, a reduction in fuel prices offers something increasingly difficult to find: immediate breathing room. But the relief announced in the 2026 Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement also exposes a deeper vulnerability. When the price of a globally traded commodity can so quickly destabilise household budgets, the problem extends beyond what motorists pay at the pump.

Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana has announced R10 billion in temporary fuel levy relief, reducing the levy by R3 per litre for diesel and R1.50 for petrol from 4 November to 1 December 2026. Smaller reductions will follow until 5 January 2027. The intervention offers meaningful short-term support, particularly after fuel prices rose sharply amid the conflict in the Middle East. But the scheduled withdrawal of the

relief means households cannot assume that November's savings will continue into the new year.

Why Fuel Prices Reach Far Beyond Motorists

Fuel is not merely a cost for private vehicle owners. It affects the movement of food, manufactured goods, construction materials and essential supplies. Businesses that depend on road transport face higher operating expenses when diesel prices rise, while workers who travel long distances to earn a living must absorb additional commuting costs.

These pressures can compound. A household may spend more on transport while also facing higher prices for goods delivered by road. A small business may have to choose between absorbing additional costs, increasing its prices or reducing expenditure elsewhere. A temporary reduction in fuel levies can ease those pressures, but it cannot remove the underlying exposure to international oil markets.

The scale of the relief matters, yet its duration matters just as much. In November, motorists may experience a noticeable reduction in the cost of filling a tank. By January, the temporary levy intervention is scheduled to disappear. That makes the measure a bridge across a difficult period rather than a lasting solution to transport affordability.

The Budget's More Difficult Number

The medium-term budget contained another figure with potentially longer-lasting consequences. National Treasury reduced its forecast for economic growth in 2026 from 1.6% to 1.2%. This follows an extended period of weak growth that has constrained South Africa's ability to create employment and improve living standards.

A stronger fiscal position is welcome. Treasury reports that government debt relative to the size of the economy stabilised at 78.4% in 2025/26, while its revised fiscal projections point towards a narrowing budget deficit. These developments could eventually reduce borrowing costs and create more room for productive investment.

But fiscal stability does not automatically create jobs. Businesses need confidence to expand, infrastructure that works, reliable logistics and sufficient demand for their products and services. Even when government manages its finances more effectively, growth can remain weak if the wider economy cannot turn that stability into investment, production and employment.

The distinction is especially important for households without secure incomes. A reduction in fuel costs can improve disposable income for a limited period. A new job, sustainable wage growth or a more productive local economy can change a household's financial circumstances for much longer.

What Happens When The Relief Ends?

Temporary fuel relief is a legitimate policy response to an extraordinary price shock. It can prevent a difficult period from becoming more damaging, especially when households and businesses have little room to absorb further increases. But relief should not be mistaken for resilience.

The larger test is whether South Africa can use the space created by a more stable fiscal position to improve infrastructure, accelerate economic activity and expand employment. Those outcomes require sustained implementation, not merely favourable budget announcements.

The R10 billion intervention may ease the immediate pressure at the pumps. Its real significance will become clearer when the relief expires and South Africans discover whether anything more durable has changed.

References

· National Treasury, 2026 Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement, 21 October 2026.

· Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana, MTBPS Speech, 21 October 2026.

· South African Revenue Service, Revised 2026 Revenue Estimate, 21 October 2026.
