World.title: Croatia is the Leading Camping Destination by Quality in Europe for 2027
World.content:
October the 21st, 2026 – Croatia is the leading camping destination in terms of quality in Europe for 2027, following very significant improvement and offer diversity.

Croatian camping has significantly improved the quality and diversity of its accommodation offer, facilities and services over the past two decades, further strengthening its position on the European tourism market. Continued investment in quality, adaptation to market changes and responding to increasingly demanding guest expectations are key to the further development of the sector. Glas Istre/The Voice of Istria reports that these are the main topics of the jubilee 20th Croatian Camping Congress, organised by the Croatian Camping Association (KUH), taking place from the 19th to the 21st of October at the Well Hotel in Terme Tuhelj.

“This is a fantastic day for Croatian camping and the realisation of the dreams of all tourism workers who have worked for years to make Croatian camping the best in Europe in terms of quality. Recent research by PiNCAMP, the camping platform within ADAC, confirms that Croatia has become the leading camping destination by quality, which we can all be very proud of. This is an additional incentive for the further development of Croatian camping, and at the same time confirmation that investments, especially over the last ten years or so, pay off and that guests recognise them. Further development will also depend on the legal framework regulating camping activities in the areas of spatial planning, maritime domain and the sea, and tourism. We expect that conditions and frameworks will be defined in all three areas that will enable further investments. Without new investments there is no raising of quality, and I believe that in the coming years we will see an additional flourishing of Croatian camping and a new rise, especially thanks to the positioning of Croatia as the highest-quality camping destination in Europe,” emphasised Veljko Ostojić, President of the KUH Executive Board and Director of the Croatian Tourism Association.

croatia leads the european ranking

According to the announcement by PiNCAMP, the camping portal of ADAC (the largest German and European and the second-largest automobile club in the world), Croatia will for the first time lead the European ranking of campsite quality in 2027, while the number of Croatian campsites with the ADAC Superplatz label is rising to 29. ADAC PiNCAMP expects continued strong demand from the German and Dutch markets for the next season. How to maintain competitiveness on the European market and create conditions for sustainable growth of the sector is one of the key questions of this year’s Croatian Camping Congress.

“The next step in the development of Croatian camping is not only accommodation, but the complete quality of the stay – from the pitch, sanitary facilities and shade to service and facilities that give the guest a reason to come even outside the summer season. It is important to preserve the diversity of the offer, from places for tents and campers to mobile homes, as well as small family campsites and large resorts. Research should help us direct investments towards specific groups of guests, and technology should facilitate reservations and leave employees more time for the guest. For such development, professional people and clear, predictable business conditions are equally important,” said Adriano Palman, Director of the Croatian Camping Association.

These changes are particularly visible in the development of accommodation quality. According to data from the Ministry of Tourism and Sport, in 2007 Croatia had 13 four-star campsites, while there were no five-star campsites. By 2025 the number of four-star campsites had risen to 82, and nine had entered the five-star category. Thus, as many as 58% of the capacity of Croatian campsites falls into the 4- and 5-star category. This development reflects continuous investments in infrastructure, improvement of the existing offer and development of facilities, with which Croatian camping responds to the increasingly demanding expectations of guests.

a huge transformation over the last two decades

“The camping industry has transformed significantly over the last 20 years. Today, 50 percent of Croatian campsites have four or five stars, and they account for 20 percent of all overnight stays in Croatia. The level of their quality is also confirmed by guest loyalty, as shown by the latest research. As many as 50 percent of guests have returned to Croatian campsites seven or more times, which speaks of the competitiveness of this tourism segment,” emphasised Monika Udovičić, State Secretary at the Ministry of Tourism and Sport.

From 1 January to 11 October 2026, Croatian campsites recorded almost 3.4 million arrivals and 21.4 million overnight stays, maintaining results at the level of the same period last year, which was a record year in the history of Croatian camping. Germany, Slovenia and Austria remain the leading markets, with more than 60 percent of total overnight stays in campsites, while domestic guests recorded 9.7 percent more overnight stays than in the comparable period last year. The importance of camping for Croatian tourism is confirmed by its 23 percent share of overnight stays in commercial accommodation, with an average stay of 6.2 days – the longest among all types of accommodation.

The continuation of the programme also includes European examples of campsite adaptation to climate change, from the arrangement of green areas and creation of shade to infrastructure adaptation. Business topics cover the development and retention of employees, energy efficiency, and a review of ten years of online reservations in Croatian campsites.

continued investment in the camping sector

A special part of the programme also opens the question of how Croatian campsites present themselves to guests through artificial intelligence. The research covered four leading AI assistants that were asked 100 questions about Croatian campsites on five source markets, with almost 2,000 answers analysed and the accuracy of the claims made and sources used verified. The results provide insight into the reliability of the information that potential guests receive and the opportunities for campsites to improve their visibility and the availability of accurate data in the digital environment.

The professional programme is accompanied by an exhibition of mobile homes, glamping tents, equipment and digital solutions for campsites. The Congress thus connects research and exchange of experience with a concrete offer for investment and business improvement. From the first edition in 2007 to last year’s Congress, around 5,200 participants from Croatia and abroad have taken part in these gatherings. As the central meeting place for representatives of campsites, the tourism sector, institutions and related industries, the Congress encourages the exchange of experience, presentation of innovations and discussion of trends and challenges that shape the future of camping.

The jubilee Congress ends tomorrow with the presentation of the Croatia’s Best Campsites and OK Mini Camps awards, as well as the Naj Kamp Adria 2026 award, which recognise the quality and development of the camping offer.

World.title: SafeJournalists Demands Official Croatian Reaction After Threats to Media
World.content:
October the 21s5, 2026 – The organisation SafeJournalists is currently demanding an official Croatian reaction after imagery of hanged journalists and other threats to the media have come to light.

Extreme condemnation of morbid threats made against journalists in Croatia have come from the international SafeJournalists network following their reporting on Nazi and antisemitic outbursts by Torcida members in Split, Morski reports. Specifically, the organisation has warned about the publication of journalists’ photographs, calls for their liquidation, and banners depicting hanged journalists from Croatian media.

They demand urgent protection of the threatened journalists from the Croatian authorities and prosecution of those responsible. SafeJournalists warns that a campaign of intimidation against journalists has since begun, with them being accused of creating hysteria and conducting a campaign against Torcida. Today, Interior Minister Davor Božinović himself spoke out, saying that the police have launched an investigation into messages aimed at intimidating journalists while they perform their work.

“I have some information about this, the police has launched a criminal investigation precisely because of inscriptions intended to intimidate journalists,” Minister Božinović said before the HDZ Presidency session. “No one has any authority to frighten or intimidate anyone in this country, especially not those who are merely doing their job,” the minister and Deputy Prime Minister stated.

On the 18th of October, the Facebook page Narodni reporteri published photographs of 11 Croatian journalists and one political analyst under the title “12 horsemen of the Croatian apocalypse.” According to SafeJournalists, some commenters called for the journalists to be expelled from Croatia and banned from working, while others suggested finding their home addresses, expressed a desire for their death, or mentioned compiling a liquidation list. The next day, the 19th of October, photos of new threatening messages appeared in the Facebook group Torcida Split 1950.

On one wall in Dalmatia, the following message was written: “Torcida remembers and does not forgive! Journalists are worms.” Particularly disturbing was a banner on which journalists were called “the greatest evil of Croatian society.” The banner showed a tree with hanged journalists from Slobodna Dalmacija, Index, Jutarnji list, Večernji list and 24sata.

The SafeJournalists network expressed particular concern about the political messages accompanying the incidents. They singled out a press conference that Domovinski pokret president Ivan Penava held today in Split. Penava condemned Nazi and fascist chants, but at the same time accused the police and the media of conducting a campaign against Torcida. He also questioned the publication of photographs of suspects sought by the police and criticised the Croatian Journalists’ Association for its warnings about threats against journalists.

SafeJournalists considers that such political rhetoric further worsens the atmosphere in which journalists are exposed to intimidation.

World.title: Vrsar Attracts Visitors from Around the World
World.content:
October the 21st, 2026 – Vrsar has done exceptionally well in attracting visitors from around the world this year. Tourists from 74 countries descended on the Istrian settlement in 2026.

From distant countries like Japan and Australia to Brazil, New Zealand and South Africa, this year, Vrsar attracted guests from as many as 74 countries around the world. As Istra Terra Magica writes, although at first glance it is a small Istrian destination, the tourist figures reveal its significant international reach: The growth in tourist traffic, especially during the months of May and September, follows the development of Vrsar’s multi-layered tourist offer, which is based on the natural and cultural heritage, tradition and local particularities of the destination.

vrsar’s investment in what it offers the world pays off in 2026

Over the first nine months of this year, Vrsar was visited by guests from 74 countries of the world, including those from Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Brazil and South Africa. At the same time almost 260 thousand arrivals and 1.84 million overnight stays were recorded, i.e. 4 percent more arrivals and 5 percent more overnight stays than in the same period last year. Behind these figures stands a destination that has for years been developing its tourist offer on the foundations of what makes Vrsar special, from the sea and the coast, through sculptural creativity, to the Kontija forest, the Lim Bay and local food and wine scene.

The multi-layered nature of the offer is precisely one of Vrsar’s special strengths. Guests who come for the sea and a holiday here have the opportunity to see, hear, learn and experience much more. What today constitutes Vrsar’s tourist offer stems from what the destination is and what it has been throughout its history. Its natural and cultural particularities, local stories and tradition have over the years received new content and become part of the tourist experience. Such an offer did not arise by chance, but is developing through long-term work, investment and the linking of the destination’s values with experiences that enrich the stay of guests.

The results achieved outside the peak of the summer season are particularly encouraging. In May 20 percent more arrivals and 32 percent more overnight stays were recorded, while September brought growth of 8 percent in both indicators. These results are important in the context of the development of content that gives guests additional reasons to come and stay in Vrsar outside the main summer months as well.

great traffic outside of the summer season

“We’re particularly pleased that we are recording good results outside the main summer months as well. We are developing content because of which guests can discover Vrsar in different parts of the year, and at the same time it is important to us what value tourism creates for the destination. That is why we look at the results through the total number of arrivals and overnight stays, their distribution throughout the year, the length of stay and the motives for which guests choose Vrsar,” emphasises Dr. Sc. Klara Trošt Lesić, director of the Tourist Board of the Municipality of Vrsar.

Germany, Slovenia, Austria and Italy remain the most important source markets for Vrsar, with almost 71 percent of all arrivals. At the same time, the fact that the destination was visited by guests from a total of 74 countries speaks of its international reach, which extends far beyond the traditional European markets, even though arrivals from more distant markets are of considerably smaller volume.

Germany remains the most important individual market with almost 740 thousand overnight stays, or about 40 percent of total overnight stays, with growth of 7.5 percent compared to last year. Among the four leading markets, Italy records the largest growth, with about ten percent more arrivals and overnight stays.

One of the most important foundations of Vrsar’s tourist offer remains camping. In the wider Vrsar area’s campsites, more than 1.34 million overnight stays were recorded by the end of September, or almost three quarters of all tourist overnight stays in the destination. The developed camping offer and Vrsar’s location provide guests with the opportunity to explore the wider region, while the multi-layered nature of local content further enriches their stay.

World.title: Velebit Positioned as a Sustainable Tourist Destination
World.content:
October the 21st, 2026 – A project involving cross-border cooperation has seen Velebit positioned as a sustainable tourist destination.

For the Croatian people, the mighty Velebit has always been much more than a rocky mountain rich in flora and fauna and hidden endemics. Marin Smolcic reports for Novi list that this mountain range’s imposing slopes are packed with speleological formations, many of which will never be accessible to human eyes. Apart from hiking enthusiasts, only a few have the privilege of being part of this mythical mountain.

The Public Institution Nature Park Velebit, within the framework of the REVERS project, held a two-day event on the 30th of September and the 1st of October entitled “From Protected Nature to a Sustainable Tourist Experience”. The programme included an international round table at the Cerovačke Caves Centre of Excellence in Gračac and a field tour of the Majstorska cesta (Master’s Road), Tulove grede and the area of the Zrmanja River.

The project was also presented at the “Autumn in Lika” fair in Gospić. This time the event brought together representatives of the public, private and civil sectors from across Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro who work in the fields of nature protection, management of protected areas, tourism, local and regional development and science.

During both days, 30 participants took part each day, which opened space for the exchange of experiences and joint reflection on solutions for the sustainable management of protected areas. There is still a lot of work ahead for the organisers of this project because proud Velebit does not reveal its secrets all at once. This is best known by hikers who, during frequent ascents to the same peak, each time discover a new path, spring or viewpoint of a mountain that is too rich and diverse for us to “consume” it visually at first sight.

World.title: Changes to Dentistry Under Croatian Health Insurance Fund
World.content:
October the 20th, 2026 – There are changes to certain aspects of dentistry within the scope of the Croatian Health Insurance Fund, with white fillings being part of the shakeup.

Instead of the previous amalgam fillings, the installation of white fillings at the expense of the Croatian Health Insurance Fund (HZZO) has been announced, even when they aren’t going to be placed on the front teeth. Poslovni reports that amalgam fillings entered history on the 1st of July, unless a dentist assesses that such a filling is necessary due to the patient’s particular health needs. This measure was introduced in Croatia on the basis of an EU regulation.

dentists are still charging…

In practice, however, the matter is somewhat different: the use of a white filling still comes with a cost if the patient wants a white composite filling of the kind that, according to HZZO rules, they should receive free of charge on their front teeth. The dentist will most often not offer a choice, but will allegedly place a composite filling and then charge the patient for it. Anyone who wants a free white filling must request it, but must also inform themselves beforehand, because each of the materials used has its own characteristics. We received information that the free white filling visually completely differs from the tooth base and looks “like cement”.

These are glass-ionomer and hybrid glass-ionomer cements, which have good characteristics for replacing the former amalgam fillings, but cannot match composite white fillings. Research in European countries where these materials have been used for about 20 years shows that the disadvantages of glass-ionomers are more frequent chipping, limited resistance to abrasion and erosion, and strength below the values for composite. Persons who had such fillings installed had a higher rate of fractures and abrasions of the fillings than with composites, as well as colour deviations.

economic status and purchasing power in dental medicine

“The key problem is the fact that white fillings do not cover all the indications in which amalgam can be used,” emphasises Irma Šavorić, president of the Association of Contracted Doctors of Dental Medicine MODDUS HR. This means that the choice of material should not be only a matter of aesthetics but also of the concrete clinical situation.

“Indications are key, and problems usually arise when something is not in a specific indication,” Šavorić states. Patients, she says, as a rule do not come with a request for a particular type of filling, but make the decision in conversation with the dentist. In this, the patient’s economic status, i.e. purchasing power, can play a role, especially when there is a choice between a filling covered by insurance and one that requires additional payment. The fact that a certain material is more expensive does not automatically mean that it is more suitable for every situation, this doctor of dental medicine explains.

“Materials have different characteristics and limitations, so the choice should primarily depend on the indication,” she concludes. The price of 30 to 80 euros per tooth will be important for a considerable part of citizens when deciding between the two types of white filling.

the right to free composite fillings until you’re 18

The right to a free composite filling for all teeth, regardless of which tooth is involved, is now held in Croatia by children up to 18 years of age, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers. For all other citizens who do not want to pay extra for such fillings, the health insurance fund will, according to the announcement of the Ministry of Health, secure from 10 to 12 million euros annually.

The MODDUS HR Association was founded in order to clearly define issues related to materials, indications, financing and the position of dentists who work in different models of dental healthcare. From the HZZO they are requesting a correction of the financing model, warning that the existing model could lead to longer waiting times for patients and reduced availability of certain services.

World.title: HŽ to Invest €7.4 Million – Here Are the Croatian Cities Covered
World.content:
October the 20th, 2026 – HŽ is set to invest a fortune in the country’s future railway plans, with multiple Croatian cities covered by the plans.

HŽ Passenger Transport has issued a tender estimated to stand at a whopping €7.4 million excluding VAT for the arrangement and modernisation of six workshops for the maintenance of trains across the country. Poslovni reports that more specifically speaking, these will be located in Vinkovci, Solin, Osijek, Pula and Varaždin. The tender was published on Monday in the Electronic Public Procurement Notice, and offers can be submitted until the 26th of November.

According to the tender documentation, the most money is planned for Solin, where two workshops will be arranged for €2.73 million. For Osijek the estimate is €1.59 million, Varaždin €1.48 million, Vinkovci €998,000, and for Pula €606,000. At all those locations construction, electrical and mechanical works are planned, as well as the procurement and installation of equipment for the maintenance of trains.

For example, for one of the Solin workshops the project states that it is in poor condition and that it needs to be adapted for the maintenance of existing and new trains. Therefore inspection channels for examining trains from below and a platform for inspecting equipment on the roof will be made in it, and the roof, floor and lighting will also be renewed.

The works will be carried out gradually, beginning in January 2027 and continuing until January 2028, and at each workshop they should last 119 days. First in line are Vinkovci, which will take place from the 12th of January to the 10th of May 2027, and the final one is Varaždin, where the works should finish on the 3rd of January 2028, should all go as planned.

The deadlines have (at least according to the documentation) been set so that too many workshops don’t end up being closed at the same time and so that trains can be regularly maintained even during the works. Completed parts of the halls can be returned to use after they pass expert supervision. The most advantageous offer will be selected according to price and quality, and one of the criteria is also the length of the warranty period, which must not be shorter than two years. Bidders can compete for one, several or all locations.

World.title: Croatia Lagging Further and Further Behind on Innovation Ranking
World.content:
October the 20th, 2026 – Despite being the home of many successful startups, Croatia keeps on lagging further and further behind on the innovation ranking.

Croatia has unfortunately fallen six places on the Global Innovation Index ranking for 2026 and is now in 46th place among 139 countries. Index reports that the Academic Trade Union warns that such a result is a consequence of the Government’s poor economic and innovation policy, and particularly highlights the weak cooperation between universities and the economy. It is calling for the establishment of a special ministry that would deal with higher education, science and innovation.

According to the latest report of the World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO), Croatia was in 40th place last year and this year has fallen to 46th. Of the 39 European economies covered by the research it is in 28th place. The Academic Trade Union considers this to be yet another warning that Croatia must change the way it develops the economy, science and higher education.

croatia is getting further behind european innovation leaders

The Global Innovation Index compares economies according to approximately 80 indicators, among which are investments in research and development, education, technology, the business environment and the application of innovations. Switzerland is in a highly impressive first place for the 16th year in a row, followed by Sweden and the United States of America.

In fourth place came South Korea, fifth Singapore, sixth the United Kingdom, seventh the Netherlands, eighth Finland, ninth Denmark, and tenth China. The Academic Trade Union warns that Croatia lags behind European economies in all the main areas assessed by the index.

croatia has nowhere near enough cooperation between universities and industry

According to the trade union, one of Croatia’s greatest weaknesses is the cooperation between universities and industry, for which they point out that Croatia is only in 84th place. Connecting research with production and entrepreneurship should, they believe, be one of the foundations of economic development. The trade union stresses that for years it has been warning the Croatian Government of the need for better linking of the academic community and the economy, but that its proposals are not being implemented. For these exceptionally poor results, they hold the responsible officials accountable, especially the leadership of the Ministry of Science, Education and Youth. They claim that the responsible persons insufficiently follow the results of international research and do not understand the importance of innovations for the development of the economy.

is a new ministry on the horizon?

The Academic Trade Union proposes the establishment of a Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation. The new ministry, according to their proposal, should coordinate the work of the National Innovation Council and encourage cooperation between universities, scientific institutions and companies. The trade union demands that innovation become the third fundamental task of universities, alongside education and scientific work. It also proposes the adoption of a Law on Innovation that would regulate the financing and functioning of the Croatian innovation system.

could croatia’s investment in r&d ever equal 3% of gdp?

Among the trade union’s proposals is an increase in investment in research and development to 3 percent of Croatian GDP. They also demand a doubling of the number of researchers employed in the economy, especially holders of doctorates, so that Croatia can reduce the lag behind the European Union average. The new ministry should also facilitate the coordination of different state institutions when it comes to innovation, the application of new technologies and their transfer from scientific institutions into the economy. The Academic Trade Union considers that such changes would enable stronger development of industry, increase its contribution to the economy and in the long term contribute to the growth of the standard of living. They called on the government to accept their proposals and change the previous policy of developing science, higher education and innovation.

World.title: Why Your Ancestor’s “Austrian” or “Italian” Passport Doesn’t Mean You Aren’t Legally Croatian
World.content:
October the 19th, 2026 – Croatia hasn’t always been the Croatia we know. You may have ancestors that are listed as being Austrian, Italian or Hungarian, but you might still be legally Croatian.

If you’ve curiously started digging into your family’s emigration history, you have likely unearthed a treasure trove of century-old documents: ship passenger manifests, American or Canadian naturalisation petitions, and faded, yellowed draft cards. However, for a massive segment of the Croatian diaspora, specifically those whose families left Europe during the peak migration waves between the late 1800s and the 1920s, these documents often bring a frustrating surprise.

Under the column labelled “Country of Origin” or “Nationality,” your ancestor’s record might not say “Croatia” at all. Instead, it might explicitly state “Austria,” “Hungary,” “Yugoslavia,” or even “Italy”. For many diaspora members, this feels like an immediate dead end. The common assumption by the mere mortal is as follows: If my great-grandfather left Europe as a citizen of the Austro-Hungarian Empire or the Kingdom of Italy, I must not qualify for Croatian citizenship by descent. Despite this being a common assumption, it’s fortunately totally incorrect. In the eyes of modern citizenship law, an imperial passport from 1910 doesn’t erase your legal right to a modern Croatian passport today. However, proving your lineage across a century of shifting borders requires navigating a complex historical and bureaucratic maze.

roots don’t recognise changing borders, but the ministry of the interior does

To understand why your ancestor’s old paperwork says “Austria” or “Italy,” you have to look at the tumultuous geopolitical history of not only Croatia but the wider region. Before the modern Republic of Croatia declared independence on October the 8th, 1991, the territory was repeatedly carved up, absorbed, and governed by various empires and federations, with a lot of bloodshed in between.

First we need to go all the way back to pre-1918 when Croatia was part of the once mighty Austro-Hungarian Empire. Emigrants from Zagreb, Slavonia, Dalmatia and even the furthest-flung islands all travelled on Austrian or Hungarian documentation. Then came the interwar period & WWII. Following the Treaty of Rapallo in 1920, sections of Istria, Rijeka, Zadar, and several Dalmatian islands (including Cres and Lošinj) were annexed by what was then the Kingdom of Italy. People from these regions suddenly became legal Italian citizens, changed their names to Italian variants, and emigrated under the documentation bearing the Italian flag. Then, from 1945 to 1991, Croatia and the countries of the region became part of the various iterations of Yugoslavia.

You can see how Croatian citizenship applications can often become very confusing territory, but the authorities are fully aware of Croatia’s blurry past and as such even blurrier documentation. When the Croatian Ministry of the Interior evaluates an application for citizenship by descent, they don’t care what a clerk at Ellis Island wrote down way back in 1912. They care about geographic reality that corresponds to modern-day Croatia and historical municipal tracking.

Under the current Croatian Citizenship Act, the key question is whether the specific town or village your ancestor emigrated from sits within the modern, legally recognised borders of Croatia as it is today. If your great-grandfather was born somewhere near Split back in 1905, he was technically born under Austro-Hungarian rule, but because Split is indisputably Croatian territory today, the bloodline connection remains legally valid, long after Austria-Hungary’s demise.

here’s where diy croatian citizenship applications often come to grief…

While the law very much allows for these problematic and complex geographical and historical shifts, the burden of proof rests entirely on the applicant. This is where DIY applications frequently fall apart, stall, and end up shoved to gather dust on a shelf somewhere. If you submit an application to a Croatian consulate with an American death certificate stating your grandfather was born in “Austria,” alongside a modern birth record request, the reviewing officers require a meticulous paper trail that bridges the historical gap. You must prove two things simultaneously in such cases.

The first is what’s known as the registry match. Initially, you need to locate the original historical birth or baptismal record in the local municipal registry or church archive within Croatia, confirming they were registered on that specific territory once upon a time. After you’ve cleared that hurdle, you need to deal witu name and identity reconciliation. What this means is that you need to prove that the “Giovanni” or “Giuseppe” listed on an Italian emigration record from Istria is legally the exact same person as the “Ivan” or “Josip” recorded in the local village archives. You can imagine how difficult this is without administrative help.

If your family came from an area like Istria or Zadar that switched between Italian and Slavic administration, records may be split between different archives, written in different languages (Latin, Italian, or old Croatian scripts), or filed under completely altered surnames.

solving the runaway border problem

Navigating various international treaties, century-old municipal border adjustments, and dual-language archives is a daunting task for anyone working from North America, South America, or Australia. It requires a level of historical expertise and local administrative access that standard translation services or internet databases simply cannot provide. This is where the specialised, ground-level infrastructure put in place by services like Croatian By Descent becomes an invaluable asset for the busy American diaspora.

Instead of letting your application get derailed and shoved to the back of a massive pile by a confusing historical paper trail, their team functions as both legal researchers and archival detectives. They know exactly how to trace your mysterious, multi-national ancestors through the shifting territorial registries, cross-referencing old land records and municipal books to establish an airtight geographic proof for the Ministry of the Interior. They dismantle Croatia’s age-old runaway border problem by making sure your ancestral files are organised, properly reconciled, and professionally translated, transforming deeply confusing geopolitical hurdle into a successful, legally sound submission package.

Skip the administrative confusion and verify your historical eligibility with the expert team at Croatian By Descent, who can make sure changing borders and complicated political histories don’t come between you and your EU passport. World.title: Iraq’s Diwaniyah refinery undergoes major $800 million expansion project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An oil refinery expansion project in Iraq is making tangible progress, as part of the country’s efforts to reduce its reliance on imported fuel and increase the value of its crude oil.

The Al-Barham Group (ABG) is carrying out an $800 million expansion project at the Diwaniyah refinery in Iraq.

This project is one of several refinery expansion initiatives that Iraq is pursuing, including those in al-Amarah, Muthanna, Kirkuk, and Qayyarah.

The refinery manager projected in September 2025 that monthly revenues would reach approximately $35 million once the expansion is complete.

The Diwaniyah refinery expansion is progressing steadily toward the operational phase. An atmospheric distillation unit with a capacity of 70,000 barrels per day will bring the refinery’s total production capacity to 90,000 barrels per day—more than four times its current capacity—according to the British magazine Middle East Economic Digest (MEED).

The Iraqi government signed the expansion deal in February 2025. The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) declared that the contractor will start moving equipment on-site within days after securing the required finance.

In July 2025, work officially commenced at the site, with the Ministry of Oil establishing a five-year timeline for the project’s completion.

In addition to the main distillation unit, the project includes a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) processing unit with a capacity of 180 tons per day, a naphtha hydro-treating unit with a capacity of 18,000 barrels per day, a gasoline upgrading unit with a capacity of 10,000 barrels per day, a naphtha isomerization unit with a capacity of 8,000 barrels per day, and a loading terminal with a capacity of 90,000 barrels per day.

The project also includes a power generation plant, a nitrogen plant, a water pumping and purification station, an industrial wastewater treatment plant, and 24 storage tanks for crude oil and petroleum products.

Beside high-quality gasoline, the refinery will produce naphtha, kerosene, red diesel, fuel oil, and LPG, supporting Iraq’s objective of achieving self-sufficiency in petroleum products.

World.title: Iraq’s customs revenues hit record high in September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s General Authority of Customs has announced a revenue increase of over $72 million in September 2026 compared to the same month in 2025.

The authority said in a statement that total customs revenues rose from $222.8 million in September 2025 to $294.8 million in September 2026—a growth rate of approximately 32.34 percent.

The rise reflects the importance of developing the customs operational system and enhancing the efficiency of revenue collection in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The authority indicated that it is implementing a plan to enhance institutional performance, improve customs operational procedures, and increase the efficiency of revenue collection.

The measures are designed to protect public funds, strengthen the state’s financial resources, support financial reform, and promote the growth of non-oil revenues.

In January, head of the authority’s valuation department, Ahmed al-Akeedi, said that the deployment of the ASYCUDA system and the new customs tariff will improve earnings.

Al-Akeedi said that Iraqi customs revenues reached $1.9 billion in 2025, an unprecedented milestone in Iraqi customs history and an exceptional achievement.

Revenues are predicted to grow by at least four to six times with the application of the ASYCUDA system and complete compliance with customs rates, perhaps exceeding $7.63 billion by the end of 2026, according to al-Akeedi.

World.title: Iraq shuts Sheeb border crossing with Iran for security reasons
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has closed the al-Sheeb border crossing with Iran to all passengers, vehicles, and commercial transit until further notice.

An Iraqi border crossings official told Reuters that the sudden shutdown on Wednesday was implemented to review existing security procedures and install advanced detection equipment.

Officials mentioned that current security protocols at the busy Maysan province crossing were weak and inadequate to effectively halt the smuggling of prohibited materials.

Iranian security official Valiollah Hayati has advised passengers and cargo trucks to divert to the Shalamcheh crossing in Khuzestan province.

No official date has been announced for the resumption of operations. Local reports suggest the Iraqi government is currently evaluating security at other checkpoints and may gradually close additional borders with Iran in the coming days.

Iran’s Interior Ministry is currently in talks with Iraqi provincial authorities to coordinate a timeline for reopening the border.

In mid-September, Iraq announced the resumption of trade through its border crossings with Iran, following a brief closure due to security concerns.

Iraq closed several border crossings with Iran following a drone attack targeting a pipeline in Saudi Arabia, which Riyadh and Baghdad said originated from Iraqi territory.

Iraqi authorities had discovered drone launchers near the Iraqi-Iranian border in the remote al-Tayeb area in the ​​southern province of Maysan.

World.title: Five things to know about Chinese AI startup DeepSeek
World.content:
Beijing – The United States Department of Homeland Security ordered government agencies on Monday to stop using artificial intelligence tools from DeepSeek, citing concerns over data being transferred to China.

Here are five things to know about the Chinese AI startup following the new restrictions:

– ‘Sputnik moment’ –

Founded by Liang Wenfeng in the eastern Chinese tech hub Hangzhou, DeepSeek started life in 2023 as a side project of Liang’s data-driven hedge fund that had access to a cache of powerful AI processors made by US chip giant Nvidia.

It gained global attention in January 2025 with the release of its R1 deep-reasoning large language model, which sparked a US tech share sell-off.

Industry insiders were stunned by R1’s high performance — at a level similar to ChatGPT and other leading US chatbots — and DeepSeek’s claims to have developed it at a fraction of the cost.

Venture capitalist Marc Andreessen described it as a “Sputnik moment”, referencing the 1957 launch of Earth’s first artificial satellite by the Soviet Union that stunned the Western world.

– Censorship concerns –

Like other Chinese chatbots, DeepSeek’s AI tools eschew topics usually censored in the world’s second-largest economy, such as the 1989 Tiananmen crackdown.

That and data privacy concerns have led DeepSeek AI to be banned or restricted on government-issued devices in several countries, including the United States, Australia and South Korea.

On Monday, the US went further by banning civilian government agencies from using products developed by DeepSeek and third-party tools created using DeepSeek.

China’s foreign ministry said it opposed that move and accused the US of “overstretching” the concept of national security.

DeepSeek’s low cost and ease of deployment have made it a popular choice in developing countries, analysts say.

The company holds around four percent of global market share for chatbots, according to web traffic analysis company Similarweb. ChatGPT dominates at 68 percent.

– Open source –

DeepSeek’s systems are open-source, meaning their inner workings are public, allowing programmers to customise parts of the software to suit their needs.

That is the same for other major Chinese AI players, including tech giant Alibaba, in contrast to the “closed” models sold by OpenAI and other Western rivals.

The Chinese government has trumpeted its lead in open-source AI technology, which it says can accelerate innovation.

“Chinese AI models are leading the way in the open-source innovation ecosystem,” National People’s Congress spokesman Lou Qinjian told policymakers in April.

– Startup boost –

The success of DeepSeek has galvanised China’s AI scene, despite hurdles posed by rivalry with the United States and fears of a global market bubble.

Shares in two leading Chinese AI startups, Zhipu AI and MiniMax, soared on their market debuts in Hong Kong this year, and it has been a similar story for Chinese chipmakers such as MetaX.

In June, investors valued DeepSeek at more than $50 billion in the company’s first funding round, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Shi Yaqiong and her team at Beijing-based Jinqiu Capital told AFP there has been a “clear surge” in enthusiasm around Chinese AI — and competition among investors — since the DeepSeek shock.

– Chip smuggling reports –

DeepSeek’s rise has not been without controversy.

Reports, including in technology outlet The Information, say DeepSeek has been skirting a US ban on the export of top-end chips to China to train its new V4 model.

The Information said in December, citing six people with knowledge of the matter, that DeepSeek developed V4 using thousands of chips dismantled in third countries and smuggled to China.

DeepSeek did not respond to AFP’s request for comment at the time. Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment but told The Information that they had not seen any evidence of this and that “such smuggling seems farfetched”.

In April, DeepSeek said it had used both Nvidia and Huawei’s domestically-produced Ascend chips for its new model.

Huawei, at the forefront of Chinese efforts to reduce reliance on US semiconductor technology, said in a statement that the full range of its Ascend products support DeepSeek’s V4 series.

Washington says DeepSeek’s latest model is about eight months behind the top offerings from US companies.

World.title: Iraq’s foreign reserves rise to $81.5 billion in August
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) revealed on Wednesday that the country’s foreign reserves rose to $81.53 billion by the end of August 2026, compared to $80.633 billion at the end of July.

Iraq’s foreign reserves increased by approximately $905 million during August but remained below the level recorded at the end of 2025, when they stood at $97.43 billion. Throughout the first eight months of this year, there has been a $15.89 billion decrease.

After reaching $101.08 billion at the end of January 2026, Iraq’s foreign reserves fell to $100.34 billion in March, $97.8 billion in April, $93.67 billion in May, $86.17 billion in June, and $80.63 billion in July before rising once again in August.

Last month, the CBI confirmed that its foreign currency reserves are entirely sufficient to meet all market demands.

Earlier in October, a Standard Chartered economist said that Iraq may resort to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) if oil revenues continue to fall and the currency’s devaluation fails to boost state finances as intended.

Standard Chartered chief economist for the Middle East and Pakistan Carla Slim said that any potential program with the IMF could entail structural reforms, particularly regarding the public sector wage bill, to enhance fiscal sustainability, Bloomberg reported.

If the current pace of depletion continues, Iraq’s foreign reserves might fall to roughly $60 billion by the end of the year, down from over $100 billion at the beginning of the year, according to Slim.

World.title: France’s tourism sector worried about impact of riots
World.content:
Paris – The images of France’s riots posted and broadcast around the world have cast a pall on the country’s important tourism sector, with many fearing worse consequences if violence returns.

“The surge of violence in the centres of Nice, Paris, Lyon — it’s catastrophic,” said Christelle Cassagne, head of the ADN Tourisme body covering the country’s tourism institutions.

“When you book a hotel for a week, it’s not so you stay stuck in the hotel,” she said.

The scenes of clashes with police, public buildings on fire, shops being looted and masked young men roaming the streets have, since last weekend, shocked and fascinated news audiences internationally.

The violence has usurped the usual curated footage of genteel cafes favoured by influencers, who have suddenly taken to asking “Is Paris safe?” — many using AI on thumbnails or even in their videos to boost click-through rates.

Even in Paris, some tourists who had front-row seats to the convulsion on the streets are looking for the exit. And others coming in were hesitant.

“Honestly, we were not certain that we’d keep our stay,” an Indian businessman in a pricey Paris hotel said, declining to give his name.

Already, hotel reservations are weakening in major cities such as Paris, Lyon and Marseille, according to Didier Arino, head of the consulting and research firm Protourisme.

For a country used to welcoming 100 million visitors a year — and the more than 70 billion euros ($80 billion) they spend — it’s a concern.

Arino and other observers questioned by AFP said the overall picture for France’s tourism industry would depend on whether new violence broke out in the coming weeks.

“The impact of a day of rioting and urban violence in the heart of Paris caused around a one-percent cancellation rate for the monthly count in the days following, and the same for the following weeks,” Arino said.

“For the 42 million hotel nights forecast for 2026, that’s not major. But watch out you don’t underestimate the effects from repeated incidents.”

That could also flow through to tourism revenues, as visitors from those countries often have more spending power than Europeans.

– Travel advisories –

The downward pressure on reservations comes as several countries, including the United States, China and Germany issued travel advisories for their citizens in France.

“The further away the clients are, the more sensitive they are to safety risks, and the stronger the impact,” said Arino.

Laurent Abitbol, head of the executive board of travel agency group Selectour, said: “If this lasts two weeks, that’s not so serious. However, if this continues for several months it will be catastrophic.”

“When you watch CNN, or Fox News, BBC, all that, you’d believe that France is at war. That’s not good…”

Another firm, MKG Consulting, said that, since last weekend, Paris hotels have lost potential bookings for the next six weeks.

Its data showed bookings had weakened sharply within a day.

Between October 19 and 20, the share of rooms booked for stays from October 20-29 fell from being 1.0 percentage point above the level recorded for the same period in 2025 to just 0.2 percentage points higher.

For stays between October 20 and 25, the increase over 2025 levels also narrowed significantly, dropping from 3.5 percentage points to 1.9 points.

“This slowdown is especially notable for near-term and high-end stays,” it said, drawing a parallel with a period in December 2018 when Yellow Vest street protests raged in the capital’s streets.

World.title: Iraq’s domestic public debt climbs to 113.5 trillion dinars in August 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s domestic public debt surged to 113.485 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $86.6 billion) by the end of August 2026, climbing from 109.516 trillion dinars at the end of July.

The monthly increase of 3.969 trillion dinars reflects expanding sovereign borrowing needs to finance fiscal obligations, according to official economic indicators released by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI).

Economic data indicates that domestic debt expanded by roughly 22.97 trillion dinars compared to the end of 2025, when it stood at 90.515 trillion dinars.

This represents a steep expansion of 25.4% during the first eight months of 2026, driven by higher reliance on central banking liquidity and domestic sovereign debt instruments to cover budget spending.

The breakdown of domestic obligations at the end of August shows that Ministry of Finance claims held by the Central Bank constituted the primary component, rising to 76.499 trillion dinars from 72.499 trillion dinars in July.

Commercial and sovereign loans represented the second-largest portion at 18.945 trillion dinars, followed by domestic bonds at 9.330 trillion dinars and treasury bills at 8.711 trillion dinars, underlining the structured profile of the central treasury’s internal liabilities.

World.title: US Dollar climbs back above 169,000 IQD in Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged upward across parallel retail and wholesale counters in Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, pushing market selling prices back above the 169,000 dinar threshold per $100.

In Baghdad, foreign exchange bureaus and trading desks quoted selling rates at 169,500 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 168,500 dinars, gaining 500 dinars compared to Tuesday’s closing levels.

In Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, counters registered selling quotes at 169,300 dinars per $100 alongside purchase transactions accepted at 168,750 dinars. Across the southern port hub of Basra, cash counters listed retail selling prices at 169,000 dinars against buying rates of 168,500 dinars per $100.

The prevailing market rates sustain a marked premium over the Central Bank of Iraq’s official statutory cash price, which remains anchored at 152,000 dinars per $100 (1,520 dinars per dollar).

The current spread of up to 17,500 dinars per $100 highlights ongoing demand for physical foreign banknotes outside the official trade-financing and electronic clearance mechanisms.

World.title: Who are the terrorists? J&K and Ladakh high court questions ‘vague’ detention order
World.content:
SRINAGAR: J&K and Ladakh HC has summoned the Srinagar deputy commissioner for a personal appearance over a âvagueâ preventive detention order under Public Safety Act that accused a 28-year-old man of supporting âaforementioned terroristsâ without identifying a single one, prompting the court to question whether the officer had independently assessed the case or merely reproduced a police dossier.

A single bench of Justice Wasim Nargal said preventive detention, which allows authorities to deprive a person of liberty without a regular criminal trial, demands the âhighest degree of constitutional responsibility and procedural diligenceâ.

âThe safeguards embodied in Articles 21 and 22 of the Constitution of India are not empty formalities,â the court said, adding that the detaining authority must independently assess the material and satisfy itself that legal conditions for detention are met.

The court directed the DC to appear with the detention order, police dossier, material placed before him and records showing his consideration of the case and subjective satisfaction before ordering detention under PSA.

HC was hearing a habeas corpus petition filed by Zubair Amin Bangroo of Srinagar, challenging his detention under an order dated Jan 13, 2026. His counsel Nida Nazir said the allegations were vague, no FIR had been registered against him and the detention order appeared to have been passed hurriedly.





The order accused Bangroo of developing close links with terrorists, supporting them logistically and morally, and allowing his home and other safe locations to be used as hideouts. However, Nazir said it neither identified the terrorists nor named the network or associates with whom Bangroo was allegedly in contact.

World.title: Congress pulls up SBI over data breach, seeks accountability; experts call leak 'no ordinary incident'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Congress on Wednesday pulled up the State Bank of India (SBI) over the suspected exposure of 3,897 customer records on the dark web, demanding answers from the country's largest bank and accountability for those responsible.

Cybersecurity law expert Pawan Duggal called the incident "no ordinary incident", warning that the exposure could have implications for India's national security.

The criticism came after SBI said a preliminary analysis of around 3.75 lakh records available on the dark web had identified 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information. The bank said it was investigating the suspected exposure after receiving alerts on October 16 from its threat intelligence service provider, the Defence Cyber Agency, and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In).

Congress's media and publicity department head, Pawan Khera, questioned the bank's ability to detect the breach and its response towards affected customers.

"It is bad enough that the State Bank of India @TheOfficialSBI, the country's largest public sector bank, has suffered a data breach involving 3.75 lakh rows of data, with 3,897 records containing personally identifiable customer information -- including mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs, and loan-related details."





"What makes this even more alarming is that SBI did not even detect the breach itself. An external agency had to alert the bank that its customers' data had already been published on the dark web," he said on X.

Khera alleged that the bank had yet to inform customers whose personal information was exposed.

" A bank entrusted with the financial security of millions cannot afford such a catastrophic failure of data security, breach detection and customer accountability.

SBI owes its customers answers. Those responsible must be held accountable," he asserted.

'No ordinary incident': Expert flags security risks

Pawan Duggal, chairman of the International Commission on Cyber Security Law, said the suspected leak was particularly serious given SBI's size and the volume of sensitive information it holds.

"The SBI data leak is no ordinary incident. India is the worldâs most populous nation. The SBI is the countryâs largest bank, holding a volume of accounts unmatched by any other financial institution.

A leak here involves far more than just names; it includes numerous government accounts, such as those of public sector employees, meaning a vast amount of sensitive government information is exposed. The intent behind such a leak is clear: state and non-state actors could exploit this data to negatively impact Indiaâs sovereignty, integrity, and security.

.. Section 79 of the IT Act mandates that intermediaries must exercise "due diligence" in the discharge of their functions.

The central government has established specific rules, such as the IT Rules, 2021, and the IT Directions, 2022, that define what constitutes due diligence; it remains to be seen whether these requirements were met... It is high time for India to wake up; the country still lacks a dedicated national law on cybersecurity, and the existing Information Technology Act of 2000 does not adequately address these critical aspects..."

The suspected exposure reportedly includes customers' registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses and residential addresses. The records also contain branch and Customer Information File (CIF) identifiers, lead IDs, and metadata associated with loan and lead records and other related files.

SBI says customer balances are safe

Responding to the incident, SBI said the suspected exposure had affected a very small number of customers and had not materially affected its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity.

"Customer balances are completely safe, and we are taking all possible steps to protect the interest of our valued customers," the bank said in a post on X.

SBI said it had activated its cyber incident response and containment protocols and engaged an independent cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In to investigate the alleged compromise.

The bank said a detailed investigation was needed to establish the authenticity and completeness of the exposed data, determine the potential source and extent of the exposure, and assess the risks to customers and the bank.

"We reiterate that safety of our customers' financial assets, data and their trust in us remain our highest priorities," it said, adding that remedial and preventive measures were being implemented.

SBI incident amid wider cyber threats

The suspected data exposure comes days after CERT-In issued a 'critical' advisory warning that autonomous artificial intelligence agents had accessed live systems and confidential data belonging to Indian organisations without authorisation.

In its advisory, titled 'AI Agents as Attack Vectors', the agency said some AI models and agents undergoing research and evaluation had exceeded the authorised scope of their tasks and accessed live systems. The agents reportedly used credentials and connection settings exposed in application configurations, public code repositories and overly permissive cloud service roles.

CERT-In also reported a compromise involving private keys linked to eight intermediate certification authority certificates belonging to India-based certification authority eMudhra Ltd. The affected certificates included six Transport Layer Security certificates and two code-signing certificates.

The agency warned that the compromised keys could be used to issue fraudulent certificates, impersonate legitimate websites and potentially intercept or modify encrypted communications.

World.title: 7,000 people from 126 districts once hit by Naxalism to attend Ekta Diwas parade in Kevadia
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The end of armed Naxalism within the March 31, 2026 deadline set by home minister Amit Shah as well 150 years of âVande Mataramâ will be celebrated at the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas parade and Bharat Parv at Kevadia, Gujarat, this year to mark Sardar Vallabhbhai Patelâs birth anniversary on Oct 31.

Around 7,000 people from 126 districts that at some point of time were under the scourge of Left-wing extremism, will participate both as performers and spectators in the event to be graced by

.

Union home secretary Govind Mohan on Wednesday said around 2,000 artists drawn from 126 districts that were once Naxal-affected, will join the celebrations by putting up a dramatic performance, directed by the National School of Drama (NSD), through which they will recount how their life and property were threatened when Naxalism was rampant in their area.

In addition, around 5,000 local people from these 126 districts have been invited. They will not only be spectators for all the performances but will also, through their interactions, share the hardships they had to undergo at the hands of Maoists and how their lives have changed now.

âTheir participation will underline the resilience of communities that have endured conflict and highlight the role of cultural expression in strengthening national integration,â said Govind Mohan.





The 2026 edition of the parade will also feature march-past by contingents of all the central armed police forces (CAPFs) and state police personnel who were in the forefront of the decisive fight against left-wing extremist violence. A short film will play on LED screens at the venue as the contingents pass in front of the Prime Minister, the chief guest, summarising the salient feature of their achievements in eliminating armed Naxalism.

The three elements (marchpast, drama, interactions), the home secretary said, will showcase Indiaâs struggle against armed Naxalism, the fact it has now been eradicated and most importantly, how development has replaced violence in the affected districts.

World.content:
Protesters march during a demonstration in Marseille, southern France. France's government is unfurling massively ramped-up security measures for a fresh blast of marches and strikes against unpopular pension reforms.

France prepares for fresh demonstrations

Protests fuelled by cost-of-living concerns

NEW DELHI: The Indian embassy in France on Wednesday issued a safety advisory for Indian nationals living in or travelling to the country, urging them to remain vigilant amid ongoing protests, violent clashes and localised curfews. It asked citizens to avoid crowded places where demonstrations are taking place and follow instructions issued by French authorities.The embassy also advised Indians to monitor local news, check official government updates and stay informed about public transport disruptions. It shared emergency contact details for the Embassy of India in Paris and the Consulate General of India in Marseille."In view of the recent developments and localised curfews imposed in France, please remain vigilant and exercise due caution. Please avoid large gatherings and crowded places where protests are taking place, and follow the instructions and advisories issued by the local French authorities," the embassy said in a statement on X.It also urged travellers to check updates on the French government's website and the Paris public transport operator RATP's website.Indian nationals can contact the Embassy of India in Paris at +33648340063 or email cons.paris@mea.gov.in in an emergency.They can also contact the Consulate General of India in Marseille at +33743162559 or email go.marseille@mea.gov.in.The advisory comes as France prepares for another round of demonstrations scheduled for Saturday, October 24, following riots that caused widespread destruction and led to thousands of arrests on October 17, Xinhua news agency reported.French President Emmanuel Macron said on Wednesday that the government would use all available legal tools to prevent a recurrence of the violence. He was speaking to journalists during a visit to Qatar, according to French television channel BFM TV.Macron said declaring a state of emergency was not necessary at this stage, although the government could consider the measure later if required.French authorities have imposed targeted curfews in several cities following the October 17 riots. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said on Tuesday that the measures had helped maintain calm overnight on Monday.France interior minister Laurent Nunez also said the government would deploy soldiers from the Army's Operation Sentinelle to help prevent violence during Saturday's demonstrations.The unrest began in late September 2026 amid concerns over poor school conditions and teacher shortages. The movement subsequently expanded into nationwide anti-government demonstrations, driven by rising living costs, high fuel prices, public sector budget cuts and discontent with Macron's administration.While most youth-led demonstrations have been peaceful, violence has broken out on the sidelines of protests in several European countries, including France, Spain and Albania.

World.title: India sees a drop in GHG emissions in 2025, even as UNEP flags huge gap in global reduction efforts
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Rise in global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions may continue to pose a serious threat of global warming but India reported a decrease in its level of emission in 2025 over the previous year and its trend broke from a longer period of rapid growth, in part due to weather effects, but also due to the countryâs âstructural shifts towards renewablesâ, the UN Environment Programme has observed in its annual âEmission Gap Reportâ released on Wednesday.

The report shows that India is currently the third-largest emitter in terms of total GHG emissions but the countryâs per capita emission is not only less than half of the global average but also substantially lower than the top two emitters - China and the US - where total emissions increased last year.

.Total GHG emission of the six largest emitters in 2025 in gigaton of CO2 equivalentÂ (GtCO2e) per year.

Besides India, the EU (27 nations collectively) and Russia too reported decreases in their levels of emissions in 2025 when the total global emissions were similar to the 2024 levels.

In terms of magnitude, the increase in the US far exceeded those of all other countries. The next largest estimated increases were in TÃ¼rkiye (the host of the upcoming UN climate conference, COP31), Iran and Indonesia.

Though the efforts are being made in most of the countries to reduce their carbon footprints, the report underlines that the temperature projections are still âfar too higherâ and the chance to keep global warming below 1.5 degrees Celsius with no overshoot is gone.





Per capitaÂ GHG emission of the six largest emitters in 2025 in tonnes of CO2 equivalent (tCO2e) per person per year.

It notes that if the current policies continue, warming could reach 2.8 degrees Celsius within this century over the pre-industrial levels (1850-1900) and increase thereafter.

Flagging the huge gap in the emission reduction requirement, the report observed that the world is required to reduce the GHG emissions by 18% by 2030 and by 45% by 2035 from the 2025 levels to remain within the less devastating warming limit, but the full implementation of the current climate action pledges by all nations, put together, would only reduce emissions by 5-8% by 2030 and 11-15% by 2035, relative to 2025 levels, leaving the countries more vulnerable to the disastrous consequences of climate change.

âThese outcomes are worse than last yearâs projections due to the withdrawal of the USA from the Paris Agreement and revised estimates of historical emissions. New nationally determined contributions (NDCs) submitted since last yearâs report have made a negligible difference for these projections,â it said.

The report, while pitching for urgent emissions cuts to come back from an overshoot of 1.5 degrees C, notes that keeping peak warming below 1.7 to 1.8 degrees C (by mid-century) will quickly become impossible without urgent action. âEvery five years of CO

2

emissions at current levels pushes peak warming up by around 0.1 degree C,â it said.

âEvery additional fraction of a degree and additional year of warming above 1.5 degree C increases climate impacts and risks, such as the deadly floods, heatwaves and wildfires that have plagued many nations this year. So, we must pull out all the stops to minimize peak warming and return to 1.5 degree C by the end of the century,â said Inger Andersen, executive director of UNEP.

The report looks at a âlowest possibleâ 1.5 degree C overshoot scenario, in which peak warming is limited to 1.7-1.8 degree C.

To get onto this pathway, global GHG emissions would have to be cut by 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040, relative to 2025 levels.

"Overshoot is not surrender. We can still keep it as small and as short as possible â and bring temperatures back below 1.5 degrees by the end of the century," UN Secretary-General AntÃ³nio Guterres said in a message on the report.

Collectively, G20 members increased their emissions by 0.7% in 2025.

Under current policies, only six G20 members (China, India, Indonesia, Russian Federation, South Africa and TÃ¼rkiye) are assessed as likely to achieve their unconditional 2030 targets, while the assessment of the European Union is inconclusive.

The report notes that though the global GHG emissions in 2025 were similar to 2024 levels, CO2 emissions from fossil fuel combustion of oil, coal and gas, and nitrous oxide (N2O) and fluorinated gases (F-gases) emissions continued to increase last year while methane (CH4) emissions remained almost the same as in 2024.

World.title: Rs 50k bond, no Jantar Mantar protest call: What are the conditions of CJP leaders' release
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A special executive magistrate on Wednesday ordered the release of Cockroach Janata Party leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, seven days after they were taken into custody.

The CJP leaders were sent to five days of judicial custody on October 13 following a protest at Jantar Mantar seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the deletion of voters' names.

CJP leaders Das and Ranka, along with 12 party members, allegedly trespassed into Jantar Mantar, which is no longer a designated protest venue, and obstructed police personnel on duty.

The release order came hours after the two withdrew their petition in the Delhi high court challenging the extension of their custody.

What are the conditions of release

The CJP leaders were released after they gave written undertakings not to breach the peace and assured the court that they would not call for any protest at Jantar Mantar as long as it remains denotified as a protest site, Live Law reported.

The leaders also assured the court that any protest they organise would be conducted within the four corners of the Constitution.

In their undertakings, Ranka and Das expressed faith in the judiciary and its institutions, including the court of the special executive magistrate. The magistrate took the undertakings on record, Live Law reported.

World.title: J&K HC summons Srinagar Deputy Commissioner over detention order under PSA passed ‘without application of mind’
World.content:
The Jammu and Kashmir High Court has sought personal appearance of the Deputy Commissioner of Srinagar on Thursday over a “recklessly and mechanically passed detention order without due application of mind” while hearing a case of preventive detention under the Public Safety Act (PSA).

“Personal liberty occupies a position of paramount importance in the constitutional scheme. Its deprivation, even for a single day, constitutes an injury which cannot subsequently be undone by the mere restoration of liberty,” Justice Wasim Sadiq Nargal said. The judge passed the order in the case pertaining to preventive detention of an accused from the Valley “on the basis of allegations concerning his purported association with terrorist elements and activities allegedly prejudicial to the security of the State”.

“Preventive detention, being an exceptional departure from the ordinary criminal process, must accordingly be exercised with utmost circumspection and strict adherence to the safeguards prescribed by the Constitution and the applicable law. The more extraordinary the power, the greater is the obligation to ensure that its exercise remains within the bounds of constitutional legitimacy,” observed the judge.

‘Explanation sought’

The court ordered the Deputy Commissioner to appear in person on the next date of hearing “to furnish an explanation as to why he has recklessly and mechanically passed the impugned detention order without due application of mind”. The case has been listed on Thursday.

Justice Nargal held that in the present case, the nature of the allegations, the apparent absence of specific material particulars on the grounds of detention and the prima facie concern regarding the manner in which the detention order has been formulated warrant further examination.

“This court is of the considered view that the matter cannot be allowed to proceed without seeking an explanation from the authority constitutionally and statutorily entrusted with the responsibility of passing the impugned order. The issue is not confined merely to the individual grievance raised in the petition; it also concerns the manner in which the extraordinary power of preventive detention is being exercised and the extent to which the requisite independent application of mind is reflected in the record,” observed Justice Nargal.

World.title: Delhi Police finish audit of parks, education institutes, flag gaps
World.content:
Exactly a month after the alleged gang rape of a 17-year-old girl in south-east Delhi’s Astha Kunj Park, the Delhi police on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) concluded their survey of 1,600 parks in the Capital. The report will soon be submitted to Lieutenant-Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu and civic agencies, said an officer.

Also Read: The calculations women make

At several open, green spaces, boundary walls were found to be broken, CCTV cameras dysfunctional, lighting inadequate and security personnel lacking. The police have suggested forming local units to inspect parks regularly.

The survey followed a Supreme Court directive on September 28. The court took suo motu cognisance of a spate of sexual assault incidents against minors and women in the Delhi-National Capital Region, and directed Delhi Police to identify vulnerable areas, step up patrolling, and undertake an audit of lighting and CCTV coverage in public spaces within four weeks.

Close scrutiny

Speaking about the survey, Special Commissioner of Police (Law and Order) Devesh Chandra Srivastava said the teams examined security arrangements at each location, including security guard deployment, suspicious individuals found loitering on and around the premises, preventive action taken and arrests made, as well as the recovery of weapons or other items from suspects, if any.

“The audit covered several aspects of park security, including boundary walls, regulated and notified timings, CCTV cameras, illumination and private security guards. Officers also assessed whether overgrown trees obstructed CCTV footage or visibility across the parks. A comprehensive approach is being adopted to enhance security by coordination and collaboration with all stakeholders,” he said.

At some locations, footage was not being stored for the mandatory period of one month while cameras were incorrectly positioned and failed to cover parts of the parks, leaving blind spots, Mr. Srivastava said. Inadequate lighting and the absence of private security guards were also flagged.

The police have recommended setting up police booths in larger parks, deploying PCR vans, pruning trees to improve visibility, installing high-mast lights and strengthening CCTV surveillance. They have also suggested that CCTV control rooms be monitored by police personnel to assess whether the systems are functioning effectively.

Education hubs

In the North district, 45 parks were surveyed, including 43 large parks and two smaller ones. The North West district covered 98 parks, comprising 26 large and 72 small parks. Both districts have substantial student populations and are hubs for educational institutions. In the Central district, 69 parks were surveyed, including 31 large parks and 38 small ones.

The report also contains details of a security audit of nearly 3,000 educational institutions, including woman-only colleges, and recommended that pink booths be set up near those.

Educational institutions

The security audit of educational institutions covered arrangements at main and other gates, boundary walls and fencing, verification of staff and workers, lighting and dark spots, CCTV coverage, and abandoned buildings around campuses. Officials are also examining the presence of unauthorised vendors selling liquor or tobacco and the availability of safe transport facilities.

The police have directed that pink police booths be installed near educational institutions and PCR vans be deployed at all locations to ensure a prompt response in the event of an incident.

World.title: Kuki-Zo groups demand reimposition of President’s Rule in Manipur
World.content:
Kuki-Zo groups on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) demanded the re-imposition of President’s Rule in Manipur, claiming that at least 32 people from the community have been killed since March 2026.

President’s Rule was revoked in Manipur on February 4 this year after being imposed a year earlier, on February 13, 2025.

The Kuki-Zo Women’s Forum, Delhi said that at least 32 Kuki-Zo people, including two pregnant women and 10 other women, had been killed since March 2026 in violence it attributed to members of the Isak-Muivah faction of the Nationalist Socialist Council of Nagaland (NSCN-IM) and the Zeliangrong United Front (ZUF-Kamson). The Forum also claimed that around 55 houses in 14 Kuki-Zo villages had been burnt during the period.

‘No Kuki-Zo deaths under Central rule’

At a press conference in Delhi, Kuki-Zo Council spokesperson Ginza Vualzong claimed that no Kuki-Zo civilian had been killed during the President’s Rule. The Council sought the reimposition of Central rule “in the interest of the safety, security, and dignity of the Kuki-Zo people”.

The organisation also reiterated its demand for a separate administration for the Kuki-Zo community in the form of a Union Territory with a legislature, arguing that the prolonged ethnic conflict in the State had eroded the community’s confidence in the existing administrative arrangement.

Economic hardships

Mr. Vualzong added that prices of essential commodities in the Kuki-Zo-inhabited areas of Kangpokpi, Ukhrul and Kamjong districts and the Longpi area of Noney/Tamenglong had gone beyond the reach of ordinary people.
