World.title: Life 'closed in' as woman hits barriers getting pet registered as disability assist dog
World.content:
A deaf woman with a health condition has hit barriers getting her toy poodle registered as a disability assist dog.

There are eight organisations that certify and train disability assist dogs, allowing the animals and their handlers access rights in public places, such as supermarkets, libraries and on public transport.

But only one organisation will consider dogs that are already in a disabled person's house and Joanne Marshall said that needs to change.

She started training Kiko when she adopted him as a puppy about two years ago and he responds to her signs and voice commands.

Video player removed for printing https://players.brightcove.net/6093072280001/default_default/index.html?videoId=6407158719112

At her request he often helps her to undress by pulling gently on her socks and trousers.

"He's blown me away many times," Marshall said.

When she's out walking, Marshall said he alerts her to the presence of cars and other things she cannot hear but needs to avoid.

"Kiko actually picked us and we had to ask the breeder to change. It was through that, that we could see something in Kiko that was different, that we could work with."

Marshall's disability is complex, she is able to talk because she once could hear, sometimes loses mobility and has to monitor her blood pressure.

She talked to RNZ on video, with an interpreter, and said Kiko can sense changes in her blood pressure, through smell, and alerts her with nose nudges or pawing.

Supplied

"Having somebody that's constantly there alerting to when there's a change chemically, it has saved me many trips to the doctor, it has saved me money, she said.

"Even my neurologist says that Kiko is actually saving the government money because there's less hospital, less MRIs, less procedures that have to happen."

Perfect Partners Assistance Dogs Trust is the only organisation that considers dogs for certification that have been trained by a disabled person, including those who are deaf - but Marshall's application was declined last month.

She lodged a complaint with the Health and Disability Commissioner - in its response this month, the trust said videos provided show Kiko is not ready and needs to complete an independent dog obedience training programme before they will consider taking on the pair.

The trust asked a veterinary behaviourist to review the videos.

"Based on the video footage, [the vet] identified concerns about the levels of stress he showed, and avoidance and anxiety-related behaviour, particularly outside the home," the decision letter said.

"She noted that repeatedly exposing a dog to settings that overwhelm him can increase fear over time, and that stress at this level is likely to affect whether he can reliably perform tasks when they are needed. This is consistent with the concerns identified by our assessment team."

Perfect Partners Assistance Dogs Trust apologised that the process has been difficult for Marshall.

"We recognise how important Kiko is to you, and how much you feel not having a certified assistance dog affects your daily life, your safety and your access to the community."

Marshall said it limits her activities.

"I can't take him into the galleries, I can't take him into the library, I can't do my research with books I'm basically online at the moment. The life that I used to have is pretty much closed in."

A letter from her GP states Kiko is her disability assist dog and is required as a service animal - but that's not official process.

Marshall would like to see more options for those who have dogs helping them, to get them certified as service animals.

She said it feels like no disability dog coat fits her situation.

Hearing Dogs for Deaf People New Zealand specialises in certifying disability assist dogs and support for people who are deaf or hard of hearing but does not certify client-trained dogs.

"Hearing Dogs rightfully said that I had a right to question the coat because they only do the deafness for the sounds and noise around the home they don't do the neuro. So the biggest barrier at the high level is the silo of all these organisations doing a singular disability," Marshall said.

The Ministry for Cities, Environment, Regions and Transport administers the Dog Control Act, which sets out the legislative framework for disability assist dogs.

Its general manager for local government policy and partnerships, Richard Ward, said the ministry is considering whether there are any gaps and challenges in the disability assist dog regime.

"This includes looking at the oversight of authorised organisations, barriers to access and inclusion, and how to maintain public confidence in disability assist dogs recognised under the act."

Its latest tally shows in late 2025, six of the eight organisations certifying disability assist dogs had wait lists with a total of 78 people waiting for a disability assist dog across those organisations.

"Organisations have told us that capacity and resourcing can make it difficult to meet demand. They rely on a mix of funding, donations and volunteers to train dogs and support clients," Ward said.

Perfect Partners Assistance Dogs Trust programme manager Belinda Simpson said they are currently training - or have placed - more than 40 dogs owned by disabled people and did not have a waiting list.

She said an assistance dog's primary job is to stay focused on its handler, so it can perform tasks or medical alerts when they're needed.

"Every application is assessed by experienced people, with the dog's welfare front of mind."

Simpson said they would welcome more organisations working with disabled people's own dogs, with the right mix of health and disability expertise and assistance dog training experience.

"We don't believe the pathway should be opened up so that anyone can take their own dog into public places without training to minimum standards and organisational oversight, as that would be risky for the dog, the person and the public."

She said the dog's welfare is important.

"Any level of stress, fear or anxiety affects a dog's ability to process its environment, respond to cues and prioritise its handler's needs," she said.

"Putting an anxious dog into busy, complex public places isn't fair on the dog or the person, and it creates risks for the dog, the handler and the public."

Simpson said the trust will be providing feedback to the ministry's review of the the disability assist dog regime.

World.title: Refuge facing 'unprecedented demand' seeks new safe house
World.content:
Audio player for " Dunedin refuge faces record demand as it marks 50 years " removed for printing Visit page to play audio: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9._f0.YIZs2-J2FpwgcBcJJb29s1vXmFAWHLh_p1oUyv-l-RA/community/2071443%2Frefuge-facing-unprecedented-demand-seeks-new-safe-house

Dunedin refuge faces record demand as it marks 50 years Morning Report Download MP3 3m

A Dunedin refuge is facing unprecedented and escalating demand as it marks 50 years of supporting women and children.

Ōtepoti Dunedin Whānau Refuge triaged close to 150 referrals in September alone - usually it was closer to 90 and even that figure had jumped in recent years.

The refuge celebrated the milestone on Wednesday by unveiling ambitious plans to fundraise for a new community hub to cater for the growing need.

Refuge manager Simone Claire-Waring said family violence in the city was on the rise.

"We have got 90 plus referrals a month. I can't even go that's an average, I used to go 45 to 60. Now we're at 90 plus a month," she said.

The types of family violence in the community were extensive and included physical harm, child abuse, coercive control, animal torture and withholding access to basic needs including food and sanitary products.

"We've recently worked with a wahine who was only allowed to eat rice and oranges, and only allowed to feed her four tamariki rice and on the very occasion, a slice of orange," she said.

The refuge used a Kāinga Ora 12-bed safe house, but it was not fit for purpose or big enough.

Next year's fundraising campaign was to help create a purpose-built safe community hub that had whānau at its heart, she said.

"Within their own home, that has not been a safe place. The bedroom is not a safe place, the lounge, the kitchen, there's nowhere that's safe. So we want to create a space that is safe," Claire-Waring said.

"We want to create a space that is safe for our māmās to heal, to move towards their resilience, to move towards hope, that is the goal."

The refuge fed about 90 people a week, she said.

Board chair Zoë Bristowe said it was all part of a growing demand.

"The need for our services are escalating. At (the refuge), we're seeing unprecedented demand with whānau navigating increasingly complex circumstances, compounded by housing challenges, financial hardship, the cost of living," she said.

Zoë Bristowe (L), Suzanne Menzies-Culling (C) and Simone Claire-Waring celebrate 50 years of the Ōtepoti Dunedin Whānau Refuge. RNZ / Tess Brunton

The new community hub was expected to cost at least $2 million.

It would be more than an emergency shelter, Bristowe said.

"It's going to be a place of warmth and dignity and belonging. Somewhere where tamariki can sleep peacefully and play, and where whānau have the space and support to recover, rebuild and determine their own futures," she said.

The refuge had humble beginnings in February 1976 when Dunedin feminists Yoka Neumann and Suzanne Menzies-Culling hosted a public meeting in a Dundas Street flat to ask the community if they backed a safe house.

Menzies-Culling said they started getting phone calls the next day.

There was not a lot of information about domestic violence at the time, she said.

"I had no idea. I just thought it was poor people, blokes who were drinking and all that sort of stuff. The first couple of calls, one was from a wife of a Presbyterian minister," she said.

A 24-7 roster was created as they searched for a safe house.

It was challenging mahi, she said.

"We thought once women left and had a safe place with their kids they'd be able to start a new life, but they weren't," Menzies-Culling said.

"We didn't understand anything about the emotional control that the abuser has."

It was depressing the refuge was still needed 50 years on, but she was excited by the energy and support for it, she said.

"It's more professional. I don't know if it's better resourced.

"I remember when I was involved with Te Whare Pounamu (former name of the refuge), the amount that they got per bed night for women and children was hardly anything compared with what the government was prepared to spend on prison beds."

World.title: Business leaders doubt Christopher Luxon's political future, survey reveals
World.content:
Confidence amongst the country's leading business leaders has climbed in this year's Mood of the Boardroom Survey.

The annual survey by the NZ Herald is based on the views of around 150 of the country's top business executives.

It asks them to rate their confidence in the New Zealand economy on a scale of 1 to 5, with 1 being the least optimistic.

Respondents to this year's survey rated the domestic economy at 3.37 out of 5. That's up on last year's 2.82 out of 5.

Optimism about the global economy was weaker with just a 2.52 rating out of five.

The NZ Herald survey also traditionally ranks the performance of political leaders, with 74 percent of respondents rating Nicola Willis as a credible finance minister, 20 percent saying she wasn't and 6 percent unsure.

Education Minister Erica Stanford was rated by respondents as the top Cabinet minister, with 56 percent of respondents rating Stanford's ministerial performance as "very impressive". That saw her rating out of 5 hit 4.38.

Others rated as very impressive, included Todd McClay and Mark Mitchell.

Like last year, however, Christopher Luxon did not make the top 10, scoring just 2.52 out of five for his overall political performance as prime minister.

When asked whether Luxon would remain leader should the coalition be re-elected, those surveyed gave him an average rating of 2.27 out of 5.

However, when asked which leader had the strongest capacity to drive growth, Luxon fared better, winning the backing of 65 percent of chief executives and company chairs.

That is compared to just 3 percent for Labour leader Chris Hipkins. A further 13 percent favoured someone else, while 19 percent were unsure.

The survey also asked who CEOs trusted most to manage the economy through another economic shock.

Willis topped the list with 60 percent backing, ahead of Luxon with 57 percent.

Labour's finance spokesperson Barbara Edmonds attracted 30 percent support, just behind David Seymour at 33 percent.

World.title: Smith injured, Australia facing crushing defeat in Gqeberha
World.content:
Australia is staring down the barrel of a huge defeat in the second Test against South Africa, after a horror day of batting failures at St George's Park in Gqeberha.

Being made to follow on for just the third time this century, Australia's collapse came in stark contrast to the recovery of South Africa when faced with a similar situation on day three.

The Proteas were reduced to 6-110 before battling to 9-425.

The tourists though, were skittled for just 99 runs in their first innings, a whopping 326 runs behind South Africa's score, the largest first innings deficit Australia has faced since 1984.

They were then reduced to 4-156 at the close of play, still 170 runs short of making South Africa batting again, with Steve Smith yet to bat as he nurses a sore neck that may keep him from playing any further part.

A chastening morning saw a steady procession of Australian batters traipse back to the dressing room after making starts.

Night watchman Scott Boland did not last a single ball in the morning session, edging Marco Jansen (5-33) behind to Ryan Rickelton and setting the tone for a disastrous day.

Travis Head fell soon after, LBW to Jansen for 14, a decision overturned on review by the Proteas.

Australia's most profitable partnership was worth just 23 runs between Smith and Marnus Labuschagne, before the latter was spectacularly caught by Simon Harmer off the bowling of Anrich Nortje (1-5).

Anrich Nortje, right, found Marnus Labuschagne's edge. (AP Photo: Themba Hadebe)

That was to be Nortje's only wicket of the day after he aggravated a groin injury and played no further part.

Tellingly for Australia, the Proteas didn't miss him, smashing through the batting line up despite being a bowler down as Kagiso Rabada (2-33) and Wiaan Mulder (2-14) stepped up.

Matt Renshaw (12) fended a rising Jansen ball to Harmer at third slip, with Alex Carey (0) following him just two balls later after feathering behind to Rickelton, leaving Australia 6-65.

Beau Webster (13) became Jansen's fifth victim after fending a rising ball to second slip, with a clearly uncomfortable Smith (28) bowled soon after by Mulder, precipitating a rapid collapse.

Having enforced the follow on, Australia got off to the worst possible start with Nic Maddinson (8) edging Rabada behind with a shot that made him look hopelessly out of his depth.

With Smith indisposed, the partnership between Head and Labuschagne took on extra importance and, for a while at least, the two obliged.

Travis Head scored 50 in response. (Getty Images: Gallo Images/Richard Huggard)

However, their 176-ball, 92-run partnership came to a juddering halt when Labuschagne (39) attempted to loft Harmer over the long on boundary, where he was well caught by Jansen.

As ever, the Queenslander showed several bright moments in his 98-ball stay at the crease, but ultimately his 39 runs and calamitous ending further highlighted his lingering issues in the line up.

Renshaw (11) was bowled by Rabada, and Webster (8) was trapped LBW by Harmer before Boland came out as night watchman for the second time in as many nights.

He remains unbeaten on 2, with Head on 87 and within touching distance of a first century away from home, facing a tremendous task to save the game on the final day.

Look back on how all the action unfolded in our live blog.

World.title: Diamonds go down again as Ferns take control of Constellation Cup
World.content:
The Diamonds trail the four-game Constellation Cup series 2-0 after a 62-50 loss to New Zealand in Christchurch, continuing a five-year losing run across the ditch.

The series moves back to Australia for the final two matches — in Sydney on Sunday and Melbourne next Wednesday — as the Diamonds try to hang on to the trophy they reclaimed last year.

If the Silver Ferns win all four matches of the series they are expected to dethrone Australia from its number one world ranking for the first time since 2013.

After the six-goal loss in the opening match in Auckland, the Diamonds made a better start in game two but once again let the lead blow out to double digits by the third quarter.

The Diamonds regained the momentum and cut it to a two-goal difference just before three-quarter-time, but again the Silver Ferns responded and started the final term with a 10-3 run.

New Zealand captain Karin Burger praised her team for maintaining their focus even as the Aussies closed in.

The Silver Ferns were up and about as they took a 2-0 lead. (Getty Images: Joe Allison)

"Our training has been focused on staying really composed," she told Sky.

"In the past we've been guilty of letting that lead slip and then not being able to fight back."

The Diamonds shot just 82 per cent compared to New Zealand's 93, did not nab any intercepts, committed 18 turnovers to the Ferns' 11, lost the rebound battle 6-4 and, crucially, were penalised 31 more times in the game.

Captain Liz Watson credited the World Cup and Commonwealth Games champions, but suggested the Diamonds shot themselves in the foot more than a few times.

"Critical moments, turnovers, basic errors, those sort of things. Disappointing, really disappointing," she said.

"Sometimes it is perceived pressure rather than actual pressure. It could be the crowd, it could be [umpires'] calls, it could be what the Ferns are doing as well.

"They're a great team and when go hard they go really hard, so that can force errors, but we've got to be able to stay calm in those moments and read the game for what it is and not get caught up in what's happening around us."

Look back at how game two in Christchurch unfolded in our live blog below.

World.title: How Antonelli can become F1's youngest world champion this weekend
World.content:
Italian F1 driver Kimi Antonelli has his first chance to win the world championship this weekend, as the 20-year-old closes in on a maiden title in just his second season.

The Mercedes driver has been a class above the rest in 2026, with eight grand prix wins and a further six podium places across 17 rounds.

This Monday's (AEDT) United States Grand Prix will be Antonelli's first match point where he can officially seal a championship that has felt like his for many months.

The equation for Kimi Antonelli is very simple: win and hope for other results.

Antonelli enters this weekend's grand prix on 340 points, 102 more than teammate George Russell and 111 ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.

The Italian needs to have a lead of 125 points or more to seal the drivers' championship at the United States Grand Prix.

That will happen if Antonelli wins the race, Russell finishes ninth or worse, and Hamilton finishes fifth or worse.

Antonelli Russell Hamilton Championship result Win 9th or lower 5th or lower Antonelli becomes champion Win 8th or better 5th or lower Hamilton eliminated Win 9th or lower 4th or better Russell eliminated Win 8th or better 5th or lower Championship remains alive 2nd or lower Any Any Championship remains alive

After this weekend, there will be five grands prix left in the season — Mexico, Brazil, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

There will be a maximum of 125 points left to win.

If Antonelli finishes exactly 125 points ahead of either Russell or Hamilton in Texas, mathematically either of those drivers could end the season level on points — if they won every race and Antonelli failed to score another point.

Even in that unlikely scenario, Antonelli would still become champion through a tie-break, having won more grands prix than the others.

World.title: Australians run 80 hours or more in 'crazy' race with no finish line
World.content:
It sounds like a metaphor for torture: a running race with no finish line.

About 900 runners from 67 nations, including 15 Australians, crossed the start line of the Backyard Ultra World Team Championship at 11pm on Saturday AEDT at Kembla Grange in the New South Wales Illawarra.

In a deceptively simple test of physical and mental grit, each athlete completes a 6.7-kilometre course loop on the hour, every hour, until one runner remains.

They squeeze food and minutes of sleep into the remaining time, in an event that can stretch beyond four days.

Jonathan Ash was the first Australian to pull out, succumbing to injury on Monday afternoon after he exceeded the hour limit on his 41st lap.

He told the event's live stream that knee bursitis and muscle tightness from the 16th lap slowed him down.

"Basically every muscle in my body started to get knotted at some point," Ash said.

"We had to get a physio in to push that out.

"[It was] probably one of the most painful experiences of my life."

Jonathan Ash, 43, took up running in his 30s and is now one of Australia's top endurance athletes. (Supplied: Snapped Sport Pics)

The Shellharbour engineer is the second-ever Australian to complete 100 laps, equal to 670 kilometres, over four days in 2024, behind Phil Gore, who sits injured on the sidelines this year, tending to fellow athletes.

Gore broke the world record last year after running 119 laps, or 797.3km, after five days on a southern Queensland farm.

Each Australian runner has a team of supporters stationed in tents ready to provide first aid, food and water between loops. (Supplied: Snapped Sport Pics)

Melbourne's Brandon Lee Gretch tapped out after lap 73 about midnight on Wednesday and said he was proud of his effort, having achieved a personal best.

"I came in with 20 seconds to spare and had a shooting pain down my back. That was just killing me from about yard 67 onwards," he said.

"It was hell."

Brandon Lee Gretch, 32, described the world championship event as "running with 14 of my best friends". (ABC Illawarra: Justin Huntsdale)

The 32-year-old was cheerful as he snacked on chicken nuggets this morning with heavily bandaged feet.

"Myself as an eight-year-old would be so proud to know I got to put on the green and gold," Gretch said.

"It's weird because I am so sleep-deprived, I feel like my body automatically goes into recovery mode.

Dozens of local volunteers have helped coordinate the Backyard Ultra World Championship at the grassy Kembla Grange course. (Supplied: Snapped Sport Pics)

"The only bad thing is I always wake up [with] stiff legs, so I'll have to get moving again soon."

Backyard ultras were invented 15 years ago by Gary "Lazarus Lake" Cantrell and hosted at his Bell Buckle property in Tennessee.

"He wanted to challenge people to complete 100 miles in 24 hours," Australian race director Red Barnett said.

"It just grew in popularity as people pushed beyond the 24-hour mark.

"It is a bit of a crazy event."

Ash described the event as "the lesson that every person is incredibly capable of much more than they think they are".

"You don't know until you give it a shot," he said.

Dan Camac crossed the finishing line of lap 81 with about 10 minutes to spare on Wednesday morning, shortly after teammate Ben Nicholls. (ABC Illawarra: Justin Huntsdale)

All but one Australian runner ran more than 60km, but only two passed the 80km mark.

"There's a mixture of fatigue, not getting their nutrition right, body ailments that are going on," Ms Barnett said.

"So unfortunately, we just had one after the other [drop out] and are left with two [Australian competitors].

" If all goes well, these guys [Dan Camac and Ben Nicholls] are hoping to get to 100 hours, which is Thursday morning. "

Red Barnett started hosting Backyard Ultras in Wollongong's south in 2020 and is now managing the Australian course of the World Championship. (ABC Illawarra: Brooke Chandler)

Ms Barnett said things would become "drastically harder" for the remaining Australians.

"When there is only two left, they really need to work together," she said.

"Having a lot of people around to support and cheer them on, even through the nights, all that really helps, but it's going to be a huge mental test."

Dan Camac was the last Australian left standing, completing the 87th lap, with the Australian team finishing the event with a combined 1,069 laps.

World.title: PNG Chiefs unveil new logo ahead of 2028 NRL entry
World.content:
The PNG Chiefs have unveiled the club's inaugural logo and jersey ahead of its debut NRL season in 2028.

Revealed at a breakfast rich with singing, dancing and performance, the designs reflect Papua New Guinea's diverse cultures, according to the franchise.

Fashion designer Tabu Pelei, the artist behind the jersey, said finding a motif that could unite a country with over 800 different tribes was a challenge.

"I thought what better way than a kundu [drum], which is a cultural item that is found in every part of Papua New Guinea," she told the ABC.

A kundu drum is a musical instrument made from wood and animal skin that is often used in traditional performances.

Pelei said she also drew inspiration from the country's natural landscape and a tattoo from her own tribe, which represents sweat and tears.

Tabu Pelei designed the PNG Chiefs jersey. (ABC News: Marian Faa)

"I needed to include that in the design because of the process that it took to get the country through to the NRL," she said.

It is also a theme that will resonate with foundation Chiefs like Jerome Luai, Alex Johnston and Brian To'o.

"These are sporting icons for … not PNG alone but all over the Pacific and Australia. They'll be wearing one of my designs, [I'm] so extremely proud and excited," Pelei said.

With several marquee signings already announced, PNG Chiefs CEO Lorna McPherson hinted at more to come.

"November 1 is looming so you will see lots of things happen in the next couple of weeks but I can't reveal any of those secrets at this point," she told the ABC.

There has been speculation the Chiefs are looking to recruit star half back and Penrith Panthers player Nathan Cleary, who is free to begin contract negotiations next month.

But for now, McPherson is focused on the branding reveal, which she described as a defining moment for the new club in a nation obsessed with rugby league.

She said the unveiling of the logo marked "one of the most significant milestones in the journey of the PNG Chiefs".

"This is the first time that our club has its true, complete identity — a logo and jersey that our players, partners and fans can hold to as their own," McPherson said.

"The logo of the PNG Chiefs tells a story about Papua New Guinea — our people, what makes us strong and what makes us unique.

"The jersey of the PNG Chiefs is more than what players wear when they take to the field; it is a symbol of belonging, unity and the opportunity to represent millions of Papua New Guineans on the national stage.

"We know the responsibility that comes with establishing this club and we are incredibly proud to show our club to the world today.

"We strive for the PNG Chiefs to be something our country is proud of in every way — not because of the success that we will achieve on the field, but for the opportunities and legacy we will create for our country."

Elements of the PNG Chiefs logo

As per the PNG Chiefs media release

The feather headpiece: Inspired by Papua New Guinea's ceremonial plumes, the five feathers represent strength, beauty, chiefly status and national pride, with the Southern Cross connecting the club to the nation's flag.

The cassowary bone: Inspired by warrior traditions, the cassowary bone symbolises chiefly status, courage, power and the fighting spirit of the team.

The face: The chief's face represents the shape of Papua New Guinea, with ceremonial red paint showing a nation united through one warrior, one team and one purpose.

The kina shells: Representing traditional wealth, trade and prestige across Papua New Guinea's coastal, island and highland communities, the kina symbolises the value, legacy and future the club is building for the nation.

World.title: Snooker player in tears, hugged by presenter, after emotional and raw interview
World.content:
Former world number one snooker player Mark Allen has given an emotional and tearful interview, which involved a hug from the presenter and the admission that he may give up the game.

Allen, 40, took a break from playing after losing a dramatic semifinal in April's World Snooker Championship in April.

The Northern Irishman is understood to have taken time away from the game to deal with private matters, and it has cast doubt over the 40-year-old's future in the sport.

Loading Instagram content

Allen returned to the table for the first time since the world championship semi, where he missed a match-ball black that would have sent him to the decider, with a 4-2 defeat in the first round of the Northern Ireland Open to good friend Jordan Brown.

After the defeat, Allen did an interview with TNT Sports presenter Rachel Casey, where he admitted he was strongly considering throwing away the game he loved.

"I'm in a bad place at the minute, so even just to go out there and try was tough," Allen said.

"I think if I weren't playing Jordan, I wouldn't have come back.

"I felt like if I was going to play one last time, playing here at the Waterfront, where it all started in 2005, against one of my best mates — I thought that was a better way to sign out."

Asked if he was genuinely considering retirement, the winner of 12 ranking tournaments said it was a real possibility.

"I've been flooded with support but the problems are within. I just don't see a future with snooker in it, if I'm honest," he said.

"It's sad to say, because it's all I've loved to do since I was 12, but the last few months has been really difficult, and it's put snooker into perspective for me. At the minute, I'm just trying to survive."

In a touching moment, the interview was paused as Casey gave a clearly distraught Allen a comforting hug.

Allen also gave an interview with BBC Sport NI, where he said he was not prepared to retire now, but he had contemplated it "for a while".

Allen is a former world number one with 12 ranking titles in his career since turning professional in 2005.

He has won his home Northern Ireland Open twice, as well as two of the three Triple Crown events — Masters (2018) and the UK Championship (2022).

Loading Instagram content

Brown, who advances to the final 32 in Belfast with his win, described the match against his friend Allen as " the hardest match I've ever had to deal with".

"I don't even know what to say, I'm lost for words," he told Casey on TNT Sports.

"I've missed him, I love him. Just a great guy, through and through."

World.title: AFL sets date and time of AFL Origin between WA and SA
World.content:
The AFL has set the date for next year's State of Origin clash between Western Australia and South Australia.

The two states will clash at Perth Stadium on Saturday, February 27, marking South Australia's first Origin appearance in 28 years.

The match will begin at 4:40pm local time in Perth (7:10pm ACDT, 7:40pm AEDT).

"We are thrilled to officially confirm a date for AFL Origin in 2027, with Western Australia and South Australia set to reignite one of football’s greatest rivalries next February," AFL CEO Andrew Dillon said.

"[Perth] Stadium provided an incredible stage for AFL Origin's return earlier this year and we look forward to continuing to build on that momentum as we prepare for a meeting of two proud football states in Perth.

"We know football fans around the country will embrace the opportunity to celebrate the history, rivalry and unique spectacle that is AFL Origin."

WA and SA have not faced each other in a State of Origin since 1998, and the fixture coincides with the 150th anniversary of the SANFL competition.

State of Origin returned in 2026, with Victoria defeating WA by 36 points in Perth.

SA replaces Victoria for the 2027 edition, but the two old rivals will meet in 2028.

World.title: Ellis scores monster 47 points, most in WNBL game for over two decades
World.content:
Townsville's Abbey Ellis has produced one of the all-time great WNBL individual performances with a mammoth 47-point effort in the Fire's 86-68 away win over Adelaide.

The defending champions trailed 35-21 in the second quarter but outscored Adelaide 27-10 in the last term.

They improved to 1-1 while Adelaide dropped to 0-2.

Ellis kept her team afloat in the first half, scoring 25 of their first 33 points and their first 16 of the second quarter.

Her club record individual score, eclipsing the 45 points by Chandi Jones in 2005, was the equal fifth-highest in WNBL history and the largest in 21 years.

She joined league legends Lauren Jackson, Penny Taylor and Belinda Snell among the only players to record 47 points and six steals in a game.

"It's a pretty cool feeling," Ellis said.

She hit 16 of 24 from the field, nailing seven of 13 from three-point range.

"Credit to our team, we used the ball really well and found the hot hand," Ellis said.

Townsville coach Shannon Seebohm said Ellis was one of the bravest players he had coached.

"Abbey had probably one of the best games that I know I've ever seen In the WNBL, making huge shots, making big plays," Seebohm said.

"I said to her probably the thing I was most proud of her wasn't all the scoring, [it was] that she was fighting as hard as she could and defending her butt off."

Adelaide led by seven at quarter-time and Townsville scored the last seven points of the second quarter to get within three at the half.

As the game progressed, Townsville's defence improved and Ellis got more scoring support from Courtney Woods (14) and German centre Marie Gulich (13).

Alicia Froling grabbed 11 rebounds and Alexandra Fowler 10 to help Townsville collect 11 more boards.

Adelaide were shooting at 62 per cent from the field at half-time, but that dropped to 45 per cent by the end, as they scored just 25 points after half-time.

"We had a tough second half," Lightning coach Aja Parham-Ammar said.

Tayla Brazel led Adelaide's offence with a personal WNBL career-high of 19, at 72 per cent from the field.

Shay Ciezki tallied 13 points, Zitina Aokuso 12 and Opals star Steph Talbot had 11 and nine assists in her first game back from WNBA duties.

AAP

Tech.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion in penalties over the Cambridge Analytica scandal
Tech.content:
The Cambridge Analytica scandal has come back to haunt Meta after a New Mexico judge ordered it to pay $25 billion in penalties for more than 43 million violations of the state’s unfair practices law. The ruling marks the biggest legal hit Meta has taken this year, even as it’s faced several other losses or settlements.

A New Mexico jury ruled in September that Meta misled consumers over how it protected their data and prevented misinformation and hate speech on its platforms. The case stemmed from a 2021 complaint in the wake of the revelations a few years earlier that UK political consultancy Cambridge Analytica harvested data from millions of Facebook accounts to pinpoint messages that would resonate with voters leading up to President Donald Trump’s first election. The judge found that the “extraordinary number of willful violations found by the jury, the duration and repetition of the conduct, the breadth of subjects on which violations occurred, the involvement of senior Facebook leadership,” and other factors justified the highest penalty allowed under the law, at $5,000 per violation. That brings the total civil penalties to more than $219 billion, but the judge reduced it to $25 billion.

“This ruling, and the Attorney General’s approach to this enforcement, makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico,” Meta’s chief legal officer C.J. Mahoney said in a statement. “At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online. We are confident we will prevail on appeal.”

“New Mexico stood its ground”

Even this smaller sum is “one of the largest financial penalties against a corporation in U.S. history,” according to the AG’s office, and dwarfs other recent rulings and settlements involving Meta. In another landmark ruling in New Mexico state court, Meta was ordered to pay a total of nearly $1 billion in civil penalties and abatement for misleading the public about the safety of its products. In a separate agreement with most other state AGs, Meta settled an array of kids online safety complaints for $17.1 billion — but $5.3 billion of that is contingent on YouTube and TikTok installing similar measures.

New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez issued a triumphant statement after the latest in his string of wins against Meta (though the company managed to fight off many of the business changes the AG asked for in the remedies portion of the kids online safety case). “This case has always been about more than one company or one scandal,” Torrez said. “It is about whether corporations can mislead consumers about what happens to their personal information without facing meaningful consequences. New Mexico stood its ground, took this case to trial, and secured a verdict establishing millions of violations of our law.”

Update, October 21st: Added statement from Meta.

Tech.title: Cyberpunk 2077’s update for Edgerunners 2 brings mods to PS5, Switch 2, and Xbox
Tech.content:
Cyberpunk 2077 is getting a big new 2.5 update that, among other features, brings cross-platform mod support to consoles and content inspired by the new season of the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime on Netflix. There’s a lot to unpack in the full patch notes.

The Edgerunners-specific content includes a new side quest, a gear set based on the character Weak Kingsley, and a new radio station that plays Cyberpunk: Edgerunners music.

Even if you haven’t seen the show, the update also adds a Double Trouble perk option that allows dual-wielding of pistols and revolvers, plus a Richard Night-guided tour of the city side quest, and access to a selection of player-created mods via the in-game menu.

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2.

The new mod support extends to the currently supported consoles too, and CDPR says that more mods will become available over time. The notes don’t say which mods will be available at first, but it could extend the lifespan of a game that’s already nearly six years clear of its initially-troubled launch, even without the missing multiplayer mode.

Other tweaks include grouped saves that are sorted by playthrough, DLSS 4.5 support and glasses-free 3D effects, and an FOV slider for console players who want to see more (or less). The update launches on October 22nd on PC, Mac, PS5, and Xbox Series X / S, while it’s coming to Nintendo Switch 2 and the Mac App Store in the “days to follow,” according to CD Projekt Red’s patch notes.

Tech.title: Xbox mandates a four-day return to office
Tech.content:
Microsoft asked its employees to return to the office three days per week last year, and it’s now upping this requirement to four days a week for most Xbox employees. An internal memo, seen by The Verge, describes the change as a “need to create more opportunities for people to work together” after feedback from Xbox employees.

“Starting February 1st, 2027, Xbox employees in Puget Sound who live within 50 commuting miles of Studio D are required to work from the office a minimum of four days a week,” says Jacinda Chislum Pearson, Xbox chief people officer, in the internal memo. “We have thousands of Xbox employees within commuting distance of Redmond. Taking advantage of that proximity and working together in person makes it easier to review work, resolve issues, and make decisions without the burden of scheduling another meeting.”

The change to four days in the office will only apply to those close to Microsoft’s corporate campus in Redmond, Washington, and Pearson’s memo appears to suggest that “established in-office practices” for Xbox studios will remain unchanged.

Related Microsoft mandates a return to office

Microsoft has had exemptions to its return to office rules for certain roles, and Xbox employees with existing exemptions will need to resubmit them again. The return to office changes come just a day after a report suggested Microsoft was planning to announce further Xbox layoffs this month, and in November and January. Microsoft announced in July that it was planning to eliminate around 20 percent of Xbox jobs by the end of its financial year at the end of June 2027.

Xbox is also positioning its updated return to office policy as one that “should be worth the investment” of taking the time to commute into the office, especially for those 40-50 miles away. “Leaders should be present, and coming into the office should not mean spending the same day on Teams calls from a different building,” says Pearson. “Time well spent means reviewing work, solving problems, and playing games together, strengthening our path to becoming one Xbox.”

Tech.title: Star Wars Zero Company is a must-play strategy game at 20 percent off

is a tech journalist and commerce writer based out of Portland, Oregon. He’s contributed to sites like Digital Trends, Business Insider, and WIRED.
